lore.title: COSMIC ENTITIES AND ORIGIN
lore.body:
The Void:
The most primordial “place—thing—entity” — an endless, shapeless expanse of pure nothingness, could it really be referenced by that? For even the concept of nothingness has no hold on it, and the principles and laws of naturality has no grip on it for it doesn't really exist but it definitely does exist.
From the Void emerged forces, beings, and anomalies that defy logic and natural order.
It is considered the birthplace of both creation and destruction.

---
The Architects:
The first willful beings to emerge from the Void.
They are beings whose powers surpass all known existence. All that exist are the works of the architects.

Roles & Nature
The Architects are creators of universes, worlds, dimensions, and cosmic laws.

They are shapers of all lifeforms, energy, creatures of myth and legend, dragons, demons, and supernatural matter—all that exist, living and non—living came from the hands of the Architects.

An Architect’s power is so unfathomable that lower beings cannot comprehend it without losing their sense of self.


---
Arch Dragons:
Created to set balance to the world, made to counter, and battle the wyrms and their destructive effects on the world. The most powerful creatures ever crafted by the Architects. 

Traits
Ancient, divine beasts embodying pure cosmic essence.

Known as “World Anchors,” capable of stabilizing space and reality.

Their breath alone can heal curses, rewrite essence, or annihilate corruption.

Only five were ever created and none have appeared for millennials.


---
Arkhals:
Beings spawned directly by the Void.
They are not created — they manifest, shaped by the Void’s unpredictable will.

Characteristics
Aberrant and powerful creatures with no fixed form.

Some are mindless; others possess eldritch intelligence.

Considered natural enemies of all creations.
Where Architects build, Arkhals erode.


---
Demons:
The very first creatures created by the Architects after their emergence from the Void, they were seen as the embodiment of the void by the architects.

Forced to occupy the underworld as their presence caused terror to the humans and early creatures.

They were sealed in the underworld to retain balance in the mortal world.


---
Wyrms:
Entities whose sparks were ignited during the Architects’ era — specifically during their battle against Dracule.

Traits
Worm-like creatures, with scales harder than diamond, beings formed from cosmic fallout.

They feed on negative emotions and possess immense destructive powers.

Their very existence causes chaos in nature.


---
Demon Ranks.

1. Underdogs
These are the weakest demons to exist, they lack any form of supernatural, manipulative or psychic powers and are at the very bottom of the demon hierarchy. They're mostly used as servants and footsoldiers by higher ranking demons to do their biddings.

Although they lack any form of supernatural, manipulative and psychic abilities, they're faster than humans can react, they also possess immense strength and are mostly brutes. Their form varies, some walk on all fours, some on two  and others possess more legs and arms.

They cannot connect with the mortal plane, even with outside help, they do not have the ability to possess humans, so they have no potential to grow stronger.



---
2. Regular Demons
The most common denizens of the underworld.

They possess basic demonic abilities, varying from minor curse manipulation to moderate physical enhancement.

Many form pacts with humans to gain more power and influence on the mortal plane.

While dangerous in groups, they rarely rise beyond their station without outside help.


---
3. Noble Demons
The higher caste of demon society.

Whether by birth or evolution, Noble Demons possess innate potentials that far surpass regular demons.

They do not require human pacts to grow; their power naturally expands as they consume essence or corrupt energy.

When a Noble Demon surpasses a certain threshold—often after a catalyst, ritual, or battle—they can ascend to kinghood.



---
4. Demon Kings
Transcended Noble Demons who become rulers of vast underworld domains.

Their power is immense and unfathomable, rivaling great mages and mythical creatures.

Demon Kings can form pacts with humans, but unlike regular demons, the pacts they offer grant overwhelming power at catastrophic costs.

Each King has unique abilities tied to their lineage or the aspect of sin/chaos they embody.



---
5. Demon Emperors
The ultimate demonic sovereigns, above all Kings.

When a Demon King breaks through the final limit of demonic evolution, they become a Demon Emperor.

Emperors no longer require pacts, sacrifices, or offerings—they sustain themselves by feasting on human souls, which increases their power further.

Their physical forms and magical abilities are so massive that many cannot walk the mortal plane without rupturing space itself.

There are only five demons of this calibre that has ever existed.

Legends say a demon Emperors roar once split a continent, and a shadow of theirs alone can corrupt armies.


---
6. The Demon God.
The first being ever shaped by the Architects themselves.

His power is just one hair’s breadth shy of an Architect’s, making him the single most dangerous being below the cosmic creators.
The Architects created the demons in his image.

All demons—Regular to Emperor—fear him, worship him, and obey his will.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The End Of Everything
chapters.summary: Rick confronts the Arkhal King, who reveals that existence itself is a rebellion against the void, before slaughtering Rick’s comrades. Driven by grief, Rick embraces the void and battles the King, but their final clash destroys the world and the universe, returning all existence to nothingness.
paragraphs: "Now tell me, what do you think of the color white?"
"Uh," Rick replied, surprised by the awkward question before answering, "I think it represents perfection. White means an absolute, untainted, and pure personality," he said with uncertainty.
"Ain't that right," said the Arkhal King.
"Yeah, right!?" Rick responded with a wide smile.

The Arkhal King sat down, throwing Rick a disappointing gaze before continuing. "The color white is an illusion," he paused, gauging Rick's bewildered reaction before proceeding. "An illusion set to taint the true and only color that has ever existed from the very beginning."
Rick, confused and perplexed, asked, "Huh? How do you mean?"

"You see," the Arkhal King continued, ignoring Rick's question, "there are three types of beings. There are those who see existence in white, those who see it in black, and those who simply accept whatever color they perceive it to be."
He paused and glanced at Rick, who still looked confused. "I'm confused," Rick admitted. "Make me understand what you mean."

"Of course, little Rick," the Arkhal King replied mockingly. "Those who see existence in white are driven by a desire to make it even whiter—or brighter—in their own way. Those who see it in black do nothing but extend the blackness wherever they go. And the third group? They simply adapt to whichever colors they find themselves surrounded by."
"Oh... that's interesting," Rick said.
With a wicked grin, the Arkhal King asked, "Now, little Rick, tell me: which one do you happen to be?"

Brimming with certainty, Rick answered, "The white ones, of course!" He smiled as he continued, "All my life, I've been striving to make the world a better place. Though I started rough, I must say it has paid off. Seeing people happy, especially my friends and family, makes me happy. If you ask me, I'd say I deserve it!"

Rick's face lit up with pride, but the Arkhal King suddenly burst into ominous laughter. Rick, uncertain why the king found his words amusing, frowned. His voice deepened as he asked, "Demon King, which side do you belong to? Are you one of the black ones?"
He drew his massive sword and took a swipe at the Arkhal King, halting his laughter.
"Hell no!" the King yelled. "They're pathetic, in fact—you all are!"

Stunned by the answer, Rick's demeanor darkened. "Then which are you? I can clearly see you're not in the white category either. You've caused more harm than good, and I'd very much like to end you. But first, I'd like to hear your story."

The King's countenance shifted. His dark aura grew menacing as he stood from his throne. "You do make pretty good threats, boy," he said, his voice colder, sending chills down the spines of Rick's comrades, who had just entered the throne hall. "But I'll tell you, despite your arrogance and lack of respect."

The King strolled toward Rick. "I sit at the top of the list. Beings like me are known as Arkhals. I surpass demons by far. Demons see existence in black, but Arkhals see all of existence as void. We have existed from the very beginning—when existence was void and empty. We've been here long before the world you know came into existence. Comparing me to filthy demons is an insult."
Rick stood firm, unfazed by the King's life-threatening aura.
"Why now, then? Why try to destroy what exists?" Rick demanded, his voice sharp and unwavering.

The King’s smirk returned. "Because existence itself is a mistake. It’s a rebellion against the void. And I’m here to correct that mistake. You and your kind think you’re fighting for good, but your 'good' is nothing but an illusion—a fragile lie built on the backs of those who suffer for it. I will end it all."
A tense silence followed his words, broken only by the subtle shifting of Rick’s comrades as they prepared for battle.
"Enough talk," Rick growled. "Your time is up."

The air grew heavy as Rick charged forward, his sword gleaming with radiant energy. Monty and their comrades followed suit, unleashing their own attacks. The Arkhal King raised his hand, and a swirling mass of dark energy deflected their assault effortlessly.

The room erupted into chaos. Rick’s team fought valiantly, their combined power shaking the throne hall. But the King’s strength was overwhelming. He moved like a shadow, evading attacks with ease and striking back with devastating precision.
One by one, Rick’s comrades fell, their bodies motionless on the cold stone floor. Blood stained the once-pristine marble.
"No... NO!" Rick screamed, his voice echoing through the hall. He pushed himself beyond his limits, his body glowing with an otherworldly light. For a moment, it seemed as though he might succeed.
But the Arkhal King caught Rick’s blade with his bare hand, the light dimming as his grip tightened. "Foolish boy," the King sneered. "Did you really think you could defeat me?"
With a single, brutal strike, the King sent Rick crashing to the ground. Rick coughed, blood spilling from his lips as he struggled to rise.

As his trembling hands reached out to his fallen comrades, memories began flooding his mind—their laughter, their camaraderie, their shared struggles. They weren’t just his allies; they were his family.
"No," he whispered, his voice trembling. "This can’t be happening... this can’t be happening!"

Dark energy began to swirl around him. His memories grew faint, slipping from his grasp as the void began to consume him. The black aura surged, engulfing his body. He screamed, fighting against it, but it was too late.
The void spoke to him, its whispers seductive and relentless. "Let go, Rick. Let go of the pain, the loss, the light. Embrace the void."
"I... I can’t..." Rick muttered, but the aura grew stronger.

Finally, he succumbed. The dark energy solidified, covering his body like a second skin. His eyes glowed with an ominous black light, his humanity extinguished. But with it came power—power that rivaled even the Arkhal King’s.
The throne hall trembled as Rick rose to his feet, his aura pulsating with raw, destructive energy. The Arkhal King’s grin faltered, his eyes narrowing. "Interesting..." he muttered.
Rick’s voice was deep, hollow, and devoid of warmth. "I won’t stop... not until you’re gone."
The battle began anew, but this time, it was different.

Rick, now a vessel of the void, moved with terrifying speed and precision. Each swing of his blade sent shockwaves rippling through the throne hall, the dark energy emanating from his body tearing through the air like a storm.

The Arkhal King chuckled, though his movements betrayed a hint of unease. "So, you've embraced the void? You think that makes you my equal?" He unleashed a barrage of dark orbs, their power capable of leveling mountains, but Rick deflected them effortlessly.
"Equal?" Rick’s voice echoed, distorted and chilling. "No. I’ll surpass you. I’ll end you."

Their clash shook the entire castle, each blow shattering the walls and sending debris raining down. Rick fought like a man possessed, his attacks relentless and brutal. The Arkhal King matched him, their powers colliding in an explosion of light and darkness.

The battle raged, tearing apart the fabric of reality itself. Rick and the Arkhal King stood as the sole remnants of a once-vibrant world, their clash unrestrained and apocalyptic. Each strike fractured the earth, sent shockwaves through the heavens, and unleashed destruction that consumed everything in its wake.

Rick, consumed by the void’s power, fought with ferocity unlike any before. The memories of his fallen comrades had faded, replaced by the endless hunger of the void. The Arkhal King, equally drained yet resolute, met Rick’s onslaught with grim determination.

The earth groaned beneath them, the planet's very core destabilized by their relentless combat. Continents crumbled, oceans boiled away, and the air itself burned. Life, in all its forms, was extinguished, reduced to ash and echoes in the vast emptiness.

The Arkhal King, his body battered and flickering like a shadow in the wind, stepped back, observing the void that emanated from Rick with an eerie calm. "So, it has come to this," he murmured, a faint smile playing on his lips. "The void claims everything, just as it always does. This is the cycle—the truth of existence. You, Rick, have become its instrument, like I am."
Rick, now little more than a vessel for the void, growled in response. His voice was hollow, a distorted echo of the man he once was. "No... I won’t let you win. This ends here."
The Arkhal King chuckled, his voice weak but laced with certainty. "There is no winning, no losing. Only the void. You’ll see soon enough."

With the last remnants of their strength, they prepared their final attacks. The Arkhal King summoned the essence of the darkness he had mastered for centuries, condensing it into a swirling spear of obliteration. Rick, his void-infused form trembling, unleashed a massive wave of destruction, tearing through space itself.
Their attacks collided, and the impact was cataclysmic. The planet shattered, its debris scattered across the void. The energy of their clash consumed the stars, plunging the universe into darkness.
Rick and the Arkhal King, now weakened and near-death, collapsed on the remnants of the destroyed world. The void crept closer, tendrils of blackness absorbing the remnants of the shattered planet.

Rick, barely able to lift his head, watched as the dark aura began to envelop him completely. His memories—the faces of his comrades, the laughter, the struggles—were stripped away, one by one. He looked at the Arkhal King, who lay mere feet away, his own body dissolving into the void.
The Arkhal King smiled faintly, his voice barely a whisper. "Do you see it now? This was always the end. The void is where we began... and where we must return. It is everything and it is nothing."
Rick’s gaze flickered, and for a brief moment, clarity returned. But it was too late. The void consumed him entirely, his body and soul dissolving into its endless expanse.
The Arkhal King laughed weakly as his form disintegrated. "Welcome home, Rick... to the void."
As the last fragments of the earth were absorbed, the void grew silent. Everything—every memory, every soul, every trace of existence—returned to the void.
And then, as it was before creation, there was nothing only the void.
Eternal, unchanging, infinite black.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: A Song Of The Architects
chapters.summary: The world before the battle with the Arkhal King and the destruction of everything.
paragraphs: In the far east of Rover Kingdom stood a small village called Harmony, a place filled with love and peace. It was home to 200 people, including Rick, who had just turned six, his elder brother, his sister, and his parents. Everyone in the village lived in joyful bliss.
On this special day, it was late, and time for the family’s story hour.
“Grab a seat, Rika! Dad is about to tell us the story of the Architects who created the world!” Krai, Rick’s elder brother, said excitedly.
“Are you kids ready for the story?” Grey, their father, asked with a smirk.
“Yes!!” the kids yelled in unison.
“All right, kids! Remember, no interruptions during the storytelling, okay?” Grey added.
“Yes, sir!” they responded in amusement.

“Good. Now listen carefully...” Grey’s voice softened as he leaned closer. “In the very beginning, there was nothing but the Void. The Void was an endless expanse of nothingness—neither light nor dark, neither time nor space. It existed in perfect stillness, an eternal silence that stretched infinitely. It wasn’t empty, for nothing could truly be empty in a place where even the concept of absence had no meaning. Yet, it wasn’t complete.”
Grey glanced at his children, savoring their wide-eyed curiosity, before continuing.

“From the Void, something stirred—a single spark. It wasn’t a spark of light but of potential. An idea. A force. It was the seed of creation, not born from the Void but from something beyond it—something even the Void could not comprehend. It was the first breath of life.

From this spark came beings—powers that existed outside the realms of existence and nonexistence. These beings were neither gods nor mortals but something else entirely. They were the Architects, creators of the universe, born from the same essence that birthed the spark. They were beings of pure thought and will, capable of shaping reality itself.

The Architects were more than survivors of their kind; they were creators. Using their newfound powers, they designed and built the world we now call home, breathing life into the planet. From the vast oceans to the towering mountains, from the lush forests to the sprawling deserts, the Architects crafted every inch of the Earth with intention and care. Their creations were not simply physical; they imbued the world with the essence of their will, creating magic and energy that flowed through the land and its inhabitants.

But the Architects were not immortal. As eons passed, their powers began to wane, and they realized their time was coming to an end. They knew the world they created would have to thrive without them. And so, they disappeared, leaving behind their designs, their blueprints, and their legacy.

Before their final moments,” Grey continued, “the Architects gifted the Earth with life. From their hands came humans and creatures of every kind, imbued with the spark of creation. Over generations, that spark transformed, manifesting as creativity, resilience, and the potential for greatness in all living beings. Though the Architects vanished, their essence remains—woven into the fabric of the world itself.”
Grey paused, a wistful smile playing on his lips. “And that, my children, is how the world we call home came to be.”
Rick’s eyes shone with wonder. “Does that mean... part of the Architects is still inside us?”
Grey’s gaze softened. “Perhaps, Rick. Perhaps we’re all carrying a piece of their dream.”
“That was amazing, honey,” Sakura, their mother, said with a warm smile.
“I loved it, Dad! Can you tell it to me again another night?” Rick pleaded.
“I knew you’d like it, Rick!” Grey said, grinning.
“It’s awesome!” Krai exclaimed with a wide grin.
“Will you stop shouting, Krai?” Rika groaned. “I loved the story, Dad, but I don’t like how it ended.”
“That’s just how it ends, Rika. I can’t change the story to please you, but don’t worry. Next time, I’ll tell you a story with a nice, happy ending.” Grey patted Rika’s head affectionately.
“All right, kids, time for bed,” Sakura urged, gathering them for the night.

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Harmony’s Destruction
chapters.summary: Rick’s peaceful childhood comes to an end when he discovers an ancient ruin and experiences mysterious visions of the Architects and Harmony Village’s destruction. Returning home to find his family and village slaughtered, Rick is captured by marauders and sold into slavery, but despite his despair, he vows to one day regain his freedom.
paragraphs: Rick, now eight years old, had grown into a curious and restless child. His mind, sharp as a blade, always thirsted for knowledge. He spent hours exploring the forests, climbing the tallest trees, and searching through old ruins scattered across the land. His fascination with the ancient stories his father told him had grown into an obsession. More than once, he asked his father, Grey, “What happened to the Architects? Where are their creations? Why did they disappear?”
Each time, his father would smile wistfully and answer, “Some things are lost to time, Rick. But they live on in the world they left behind.”

One fateful evening, Rick ventured deeper into the forest than ever before, following a strange pull he couldn’t explain. As he pushed through the dense underbrush, he stumbled upon an ancient stone structure, half-buried beneath centuries of moss and vines. The air around him was thick with something unseen, something old.

The structure was a ruin, but the craftsmanship was undeniable. Carvings of symbols and strange geometric patterns decorated the walls, and in the center of the ruin stood a massive stone pedestal. On it lay an oval-shaped crystal orb, glowing with an otherworldly light. The world seemed to hold its breath.
Rick stepped closer, drawn by an invisible force. Could this be…? he wondered.
His hand trembled as he reached out and touched the orb.
The moment his fingers made contact, a pulse of energy surged through him. The world around him collapsed into a blinding white void, and suddenly—
He was somewhere else.
Rick’s mind filled with visions not his own.

Towering figures draped in ethereal light stood high above the world, their hands shaping mountains, carving rivers, painting the sky with stars. The Architects. The first beings, the creators of everything. Their power was immeasurable, their knowledge vast.

But something was wrong. The vision shifted. He saw them gathered in a grand, celestial hall, their luminous forms flickering like dying embers. He didn’t understand their words, but he felt their sorrow. Their time was ending—not by choice, but by something unseen, something inevitable.
Then, a final act. One Architect, cloaked in power, raised his hands toward the heavens. The vision blurred, but Rick felt what was happening—something had been sealed away, hidden, waiting.
And then, suddenly—
He saw Harmony Village.

But it was wrong. The sky above was twisted, unnatural, heavy with darkness. The air carried whispers—soft, insidious. Shadows slithered along the ground, creeping between houses. And then, the screams. Familiar voices, crying out in terror. The village was burning.
Rick gasped. His mind reeled. The vision shattered, and he was back in the ruin, his body trembling, his breath coming in ragged gasps.
Why had he seen Harmony in the vision? Why did it feel like something… had awakened?
His awe was shattered by a distant, bone-chilling sound—screams.
His heart pounded. He turned and sprinted toward the village, running as fast as his legs could carry him.
Smoke rose into the sky from the direction of home. His chest tightened. The closer he got, the stronger the scent of burning wood and charred flesh became.
When he arrived, Harmony was in ruins. Houses burned, their skeletal remains clawing at the sky. The streets were eerily empty, save for the bodies scattered like broken dolls.
He sprinted to the remains of his house, now a smoldering heap. Falling to his knees, he sobbed.
"Mother… Father… Rika… Krai… Where is everyone?"
His cries echoed through the ruined village, his small frame trembling with grief and exhaustion. The night felt darker than ever, thick with smoke, thick with silence.
But his wails did not go unnoticed.
From the shadows, movement. The attackers—merciless marauders who had laid waste to Harmony—heard his cries. Their ears perked. Their cruel grins widened.

Rick froze as figures emerged from the darkness. These were no ordinary men; they were clad in ragged armor, their faces hidden behind menacing masks. Their weapons, still stained with the blood of his village, gleamed in the dim firelight.
One of them pointed at Rick. "The boy’s still alive," he growled. "He might be worth something."
Rick scrambled backward. No. No. No.
"Stay away!" he pleaded, his voice breaking. But his small, weary legs were no match for their strides.
"Gotcha!" One of them lunged, seizing his arm. Rick kicked and thrashed, but his resistance only made them laugh.
"Feisty little one, isn’t he?" another sneered, tightening his grip on Rick’s wrist.
"Let me go!" Rick screamed, tears streaming down his face.
"Quiet, brat!" A heavy hand struck him across the face. The world blurred. His head snapped to the side. Pain bloomed across his cheek.
Dazed, he barely registered the ropes binding his hands. He was dragged through the remains of Harmony, his body too weak to resist. His cries faded to soft, broken whimpers.

The attackers led him to their encampment, where he was thrown into a crude cage alongside others—men, women, and children from other villages that had suffered the same fate. Rick curled into a corner, his body trembling as despair wrapped its cold fingers around him.
Days turned into weeks. The marauders, eager to profit from their raids, sold their captives to traveling merchants. One day, it was Rick’s turn.
A burly trader with cold, calculating eyes examined him like livestock.
"This one's scrawny," the merchant grumbled, prodding at Rick’s ribs.
"He’s young," one of the marauders countered. "Plenty of years ahead of him. He’ll grow."
The merchant smirked. "Fine. I’ll take him. But don’t expect a high price for a half-starved brat."
Chains clamped around Rick’s wrists and ankles. He was tethered to a line of slaves. As the caravan trudged forward, he turned, stealing one last look at the distant remains of Harmony.
His chest felt hollow, the weight of loss pressing down on him.
He didn’t know where he was being taken. He didn’t know what awaited him at the end of this journey.
All he knew was that his life as he had known it was over.
He was a slave now, a nameless piece of property.
But even as despair threatened to consume him, something flickered inside him. A defiance. A promise.
His father’s words echoed in his mind: “We’re all carrying a piece of their dream.”
Rick clenched his fists. He didn’t know how. He didn’t know when.
But he vowed—one day, he would be free.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The Stranger
chapters.summary: After three years of slavery, Rick continues to endure the merchant’s cruelty while repeatedly risking punishment to protect others from bullies. When a mysterious stranger witnesses Rick’s courage and loyalty toward Monty, he purchases both boys, giving Rick his first real chance at freedom and hope for a new life.
paragraphs: Rick's body ached as he scrubbed the floor of the merchant's shop. He had been here for three years now, his life a blur of hard labor, his body weary from endless toil. The merchant, a cruel man with a heart as black as the smoke that rose from the burning villages, had bought him after his parents died. He was nothing more than a tool to the merchant—a slave to do his bidding.

Though the merchant’s anger was often directed at him, Rick had learned to endure. But there was always a flicker of resistance in him, even on the darkest days. It wasn’t that he didn’t want to escape—it was that he was unsure if he could. He wasn’t strong enough. Not yet.

As Rick scrubbed, his thoughts wandered to what life could be like outside this place. The merchant had shown no mercy for anyone, but Rick was growing tired of the endless suffering. He was starting to wonder if escape was possible, but the fear of what might happen if he failed kept him grounded.
The merchant’s voice interrupted his thoughts.
“Boy, quit dawdling! The floor won't clean itself,” he barked, his voice sharp and unfeeling.

Rick flinched but didn’t respond. He had learned long ago that speaking out only made things worse. The merchant’s cruelty seemed boundless, as if every day was another test of how much Rick could endure. But even in the face of it, Rick felt something shift within him. Perhaps it was the memory of his parents' gentle love, or perhaps it was the strange fire that the merchant’s beatings only seemed to stoke. Rick couldn't say, but deep inside, he knew he had to find a way to escape.
And then, as if the universe was giving him a sign, it happened.

One of the merchant’s workers, a boy named Monty, slipped into the shop with a basket of goods. Rick had known Monty since his early days here, though the boy was younger and more fragile than he was. But Monty had been a beacon of kindness in Rick's dark world, a friend who always tried to comfort him, even if there was little to be done.
Monty caught Rick’s eye, giving him a soft, comforting smile. It was small, but to Rick, it was a promise—a reminder that there was still good in the world.
But that was before the beating.

The two bullies arrived at the shop without warning. Their sneers were twisted, their faces like shadows. They had been harassing Monty for days, and this time, they weren’t content to taunt him. They wanted to hurt him.
Rick’s heart raced. He couldn’t stand by and do nothing.
"Why don't you leave him alone!" Rick shouted, standing up and stepping between Monty and the bullies.
One of the bullies smirked, pushing Rick back. "What’s this? You want to play hero?" he mocked, before landing a fist in Rick’s stomach.
Rick stumbled and fell to the ground. The pain was excruciating, but he gritted his teeth, refusing to back down. His fists clenched, as he stood back up.

The other bully swung, but Rick was faster this time. He ducked and landed a punch on the bully’s chest, sending him staggering back. It wasn’t much, but it felt like the first real victory he had ever achieved.
The merchant entered the room just as the fight was breaking up. His eyes were filled with rage. Rick could see the fury bubbling just beneath the surface.
"You ungrateful little wretch!" the merchant roared, grabbing Rick by the arm and throwing him to the ground. "You left what you're supposed to do for a fight? You scoundrel!."

Rick’s body was bruised and battered, but the fire inside him burned brighter than ever. Each blow the merchant dealt him only seemed to stoke the embers of something deeper within Rick—a desire to be free, to stand up for what was right.
Monty helped him to his feet after the beating, his voice full of concern. "Rick, you shouldn’t have done that," he whispered, his eyes wide with fear. "He could kill you."
Rick winced, but his gaze was steady. "I couldn’t just let them hurt you," he said, the words coming out in a hoarse whisper. "You’re my friend, Monty. I’ll always protect you."
But even as he said the words, he knew they were dangerous. The merchant was growing desperate, and Rick’s small act of defiance could cost him everything.

The merchant locked Rick in the dark cellar once more, and left him there till the next day. The cold stone beneath him felt like ice, but Rick didn’t care. He had made his choice. He would stand up for those who couldn’t protect themselves, even if it meant paying the price.

While In the dark cellar, Rick's mind flew to the distant past when he was still in the village, a time when Harmony village was still vibrant and lively, the sun had just begun to set, casting long shadows across the peaceful village. Rick  sat beside his mother in their small home, her smile brightened him up as he watched the fire crackle. He could hear his father’s deep voice from outside as he worked on repairs to the roof, and his brother and sister's bantering could be heard in the background . He smiled, It was memories like these—quiet, peaceful and joyful that kept him going.

The next morning he was released from the dark cellar, and went back to his chores. As Rick scrubbed the merchant's floors, he couldn't help but wonder if escape was possible. Three years, and all he'd done was work for this cruel man. But perhaps there was another way—one that didn’t involve fighting his way out. But the question gnawed at him: Was he strong enough to leave, or was he already too broken?

The merchant looked at Rick, his thoughts torn. His business had been struggling—his goods were expensive, and the labor was hard to come by. He didn't want to be cruel, but every decision was a calculation for survival. Perhaps, just perhaps, he was doing what he had to, even if it meant breaking the boy "I've spent a lot on this boy! His demeanor and character has brought me nothing but losses! If I should calculate how much I've spent treating his wounds and healing him he'd end up serving me all his life! besides a little rod wouldn't kill him". He thought out loud before leaving.

For three long years, Rick has been serving under the merchant's harsh rule. Despite his young age, he carried out his duties diligently. He was honest and modest, earning the admiration of many of the other slaves. But Rick's most defining trait was his deep disdain for bullies. Whenever he saw someone being mistreated, he couldn't stand idly by. Time and again, he intervened, even though it often meant severe punishment for himself.

Whenever Rick stood up for another, he was beaten nearly to a pulp. Bruised and battered, he never regretted his actions. But the merchant didn't share this sentiment. Each time Rick was hurt, the merchant had to spend money on treatments to keep him alive and working. Frustrated and resentful, the merchant began locking Rick up more frequently than the other slaves, hoping to quell his rebellious streak. Yet, Rick's spirit remained unbroken.
One day, as Rick was running errands in the bustling market, he heard a commotion.
Turning toward the noise, he saw Monty, his closest friend, cornered by four older boys. Monty's face was already bruised, his body trembling from the beating.
Yet, the bullies showed no signs of stopping.
Rick's heart burned with anger. Without a second thought, he dropped the bag he was carrying, the merchant's goods spilling onto the dirt. He rushed to Monty's side, shoving one of the bullies aside.
"Leave him alone!" Rick shouted, his small frame standing defiantly between the bullies and Monty.
The boys laughed. "What are you going to do about it, huh little slave?"

Rick didn't back down. He lunged at them, fists flying, determined to protect his friend. The fight was brutal. Rick was no match for the four bullies, but he fought valiantly, refusing to give up. Bruised and bloodied, he finally managed to drive them away.
Monty, weak and sobbing, clung to Rick's arm. "Why did you do that? You'll only get punished again."
Rick gave a faint smile, wiping the blood from his mouth. "Because no one should be bullied or treated like this, Monty."
As the two boys sat on the ground, catching their breath, a shadow loomed over them. Rick's heart sank when he saw the merchant approaching, his face twisted in anger.
The merchant's eyes fell on the bag Rick had dropped. The goods inside were destroyed, scattered across the ground.
"Rick!" the merchant bellowed. "Do you know how much these cost me? Useless brat!"
Rick stood, shielding Monty behind him. "It's my fault," he admitted, his voice steady despite the fear in his chest. "Don't blame anyone else."
The merchant raised his hand, ready to strike Rick, when a voice interrupted. "Stop."

All heads turned toward the source of the voice. A man dressed in a long, dark cloak stepped forward from the crowd that had gathered to watch the scene. He didn't look that old to Rick but he was in his early 30s. His eyes were sharp, his presence commanding. He had been observing the entire incident from a distance, and now, he stood between Rick and the merchant.
"Mind your business young man!" The merchant contorted "I own him and I can do whatever I please with him"

The man stepped forward, his presence so overwhelming that the merchant’s confidence faltered, his body trembling before the stranger "Sir can you please not hit him right now" the man said with a wild grin as he leaned closer to the merchant "Well now that you asked nicely I can do that" the merchant said as he dropped his hand and took a few steps further from the man as the aura around him almost made him pee his pants.
"I'll take the boy," the stranger said calmly, his voice leaving no room for argument.

The merchant hesitated, his anger giving way to greed. No one had shown interest in buying Rick before, not with his rebellious nature and tendency to cause trouble. "You want him? He's nothing but trouble. A worthless runt."
The man's lips curled into a faint smile. "I'll pay whatever price you deem fair."
The merchant's greed won over his anger. "Fine. But don't come complaining to me later. He's yours." They quickly struck a deal, the merchant practically salivating at the coins handed to him.
Rick, however, shook his head. "I'm not going anywhere without Monty."
The stranger raised an eyebrow, surprised by the boy's boldness. "You'd refuse freedom for his sake?"
Rick stood firm, his battered face set with determination. "I can't leave him behind."
The stranger regarded Rick for a long moment, then turned to the merchant. "How much for the other boy?"
The merchant laughed. "Monty? No one wants that runt. He's weak and useless. Take him for half the price."
The stranger nodded, handing over more coins. "Done."
Rick's eyes widened in surprise. "You'll take Monty too?"
The man gave a small nod. "Loyalty like yours is rare. I'd be a fool to leave your friend behind."

Rick's heart swelled with gratitude. For the first time in years, he felt a glimmer of hope. As the stranger led them away from the merchant, to a nearby pool where they could wash themselves. Rick turned to Monty and whispered, "We'll be okay now. I promise."

The mysterious man glanced back at the two boys, a strange glint in his eyes. "You both are quite a sight" he said with a faint smile "we'll head back to the merchant for your luggage after you've washed yourselves.
Rick didn't know what the future held, but he felt a spark reignite in his heart. For the first time since Harmony's destruction, he allowed himself to hope for a brighter tomorrow.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: A New Beginning
chapters.summary: After being rescued from the merchant, Rick and Monty begin a new journey with Marcus, a former soldier who sees potential in Rick and encourages both boys to discover their purpose. Marcus takes them to a restaurant, where they enjoy their first peaceful meal without fear or hatred. Exhausted, the boys fall asleep and are carried to Marcus’s home, where they finally find safety, comfort, and the hope of a new beginning.
paragraphs: Rick and Monty walked cautiously behind the stranger, their small bags slung over their shoulders. Each boy carried only a few ragged clothes—the entirety of their worldly possessions. Despite the relief of being freed from the merchant's cruelty, the uncertainty of their future gnawed at them.

As they left the market square behind, Monty glanced up at the tall man leading them. His steps were sure and deliberate, his dark cloak brushing the ground as he walked. The sun was setting, casting long shadows over the dirt path. Finally, Monty gathered the courage to speak.
“Sir, thank you,” Monty said, his voice soft but sincere.
Rick quickly added, “We don’t know how to repay you, but we’re really grateful for what you did back there.”

The man slowed his pace, turning slightly to face them. A faint smile tugged at his lips, though his sharp eyes remained as steady as steel. “You don’t owe me anything, boys. What I did was the right thing to do.”
The boys exchanged a glance, unsure how to respond.
The man continued, “I didn't quite catch your names. Mind telling me?”
“I’m Rick,” Rick said, his voice steady despite the lingering exhaustion in his body.
“And I’m Monty,” Monty added, clutching his bag tightly.
"Well, it's good to meet you both," the man said, extending his hand. "You can call me... Marcus."
The boys hesitated for a moment before giving him a polite nod.
"Thank you, sir," Monty said again, emphasizing the title.
"Sir Marcus," Rick added with a grin.
Marcus raised an eyebrow. "Just Marcus is fine."
The boys exchanged a glance but remained steadfast. "We’d rather call you 'sir.' It’s how we were taught back at the merchant’s place," Rick explained.
Marcus chuckled. "Suit yourselves."
Rick tilted his head. “Why did you help us, Sir? You didn’t have to.”

Marcus stopped walking and turned fully to face them. His gaze bore into Rick, sharp yet not unkind. “I helped because I saw something in you, Rick. Potential. A fire. With the right guidance, you could become a fine martial man. Maybe even a soldier, if that’s what you want.”

Rick blinked, his chest tightening at the unexpected praise. No one had ever spoken to him like that before. When the merchant caught him secretly training how to fight, he was brutally beaten and punished. His chores were doubled to keep him too busy to train. He’d eventually given up to stop the punishment.
“What about me, Sir?” Monty asked hesitantly, his voice barely audible.
Marcus regarded him thoughtfully, then said, “I haven’t figured you out quite yet, Monty. But don’t let that trouble you. Everyone has a purpose—it just takes time to uncover it.”
Monty gave a mock pout. "What? Nothing? Not even a little potential?"
"Don't sweat it, kid! Like I said, everyone has a purpose. Yours might just take a little bit more time to surface," Marcus replied with a smile.
Monty nodded, though his face remained downcast.

As they resumed their journey, Marcus began to talk about himself. “I used to be a soldier,” he said. “Served in the military for years. I’ve seen battlefields, watched men rise and fall. It was a life of discipline and sacrifice, but it taught me more than I could ever learn elsewhere.”
“Why did you leave, Sir?” Rick asked.
Marcus’s expression darkened briefly. “Personal reasons,” he said, his tone leaving no room for further questions.

Silence hung between them for a while, broken only by the sound of their footsteps. As they reached the edge of the bustling market district, Marcus gestured toward a large, brightly lit building. The boys stared in awe—it was a restaurant, far grander than anything they had ever seen.
“Come on, kids,” Marcus said, ushering them inside.

The interior was even more impressive. Tables adorned with crisp white linens were surrounded by well-dressed patrons. The air was filled with the aroma of roasted meats, freshly baked bread, and exotic spices. Rick and Monty hesitated at the entrance, their ragged clothes making them feel out of place.
“Don’t just stand there,” Marcus said with a chuckle. “Come on in!”
He led them to a corner table, where they sat down hesitantly. A server approached, eyeing the boys curiously but saying nothing as Marcus placed their order.
“Anything you want,” Marcus said, looking at Rick and Monty.

The boys exchanged uncertain glances, their stomachs growling as they glanced at the menu. They’d never seen so many choices in their lives—roasted chicken, thick soups, pies, and even desserts dripping with honey and fruit.
“Are you sure, Sir?” Monty asked, his voice barely a whisper.
Marcus gave them an encouraging nod. “You kids have definitely been through a lot. Tonight, you eat until you’re full.”

Rick and Monty hesitated no longer. They chose dishes they had only ever dreamed of, their excitement bubbling over as plates began to arrive. Roast lamb, steaming bread, buttery vegetables, and sweet pastries filled the table.
For the first time in what felt like forever, they ate without fear or restraint.
As the meal came to an end, Rick and Monty could barely keep their eyes open. The warmth of the food and the comfort of the restaurant were like a lullaby, coaxing them into a peaceful drowsiness.
Marcus leaned back in his chair, noticing their heavy eyelids. “You two look like you’ve had one too many battles with sleep,” he said with a grin.
Rick yawned. “No, Sir. We’re fine…” His words trailed off as his head began to bob.
Monty tried to chime in, “I’m not—” but before he could finish, his head hit the edge of the table with a soft thud.
Marcus chuckled, shaking his head. “You boys are hopeless.”

With surprising ease, he hoisted Monty over one shoulder and Rick over the other. The restaurant staff gave him amused glances as he walked out, muttering something about “having kids without the trouble of raising them.”

Rick snored softly, while Monty mumbled incoherently about bread and fighting chickens. Marcus tried not to laugh as he carried them to his home—a modest but cozy abode nestled in a quiet corner of the city.

As he reached the house, he unlocked the door and stepped inside. He gently laid Rick and Monty on a large, cushioned couch. Rick clutched a throw pillow like a long-lost treasure, while Monty sprawled out, one leg dangling off the side.
Marcus sighed, pulling a blanket over them. “You’ve got a lot to learn, boys,” he said softly. “But for tonight, rest.”
He turned off the lights, leaving them to their dreams, which for once, were not filled with fear or hunger, but with the promise of a new beginning.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The Nightmares That Bind
chapters.summary: Rick is haunted by a terrifying nightmare about his family, but Marcus comforts him by sharing his own painful past. Monty also reveals the tragedy that led to his slavery, bringing the three closer together. As they find strength in their newfound bond, Marcus promises to take the boys to Rover Kingdom the next day, giving them something new to look forward to and a renewed sense of hope.
paragraphs: Rick jolted awake, his chest heaving as cold sweat drenched his brow. His breath came in ragged gasps as the image of his family lingered in his mind. In his dream, they had been so happy—his sister Rika singing joyfully, his mother humming as she worked, his father and older brother Krai building something together. But then, everything had turned horrific. Their faces began to distort, blood pouring from their eyes, their screams echoing in his mind as they begged for help.

Rick’s sobs broke through the quiet of the room, his hands trembling as he wiped his face, trying to escape the terrifying images. He couldn’t shake the feeling that they were still calling to him, pleading for help. His heart ached, and he felt utterly lost.
Monty, who had been sleeping soundly beside him, stirred at the sound of Rick’s sobs. His eyes fluttered open, confusion quickly turning into concern when he saw the tears streaming down Rick’s face.
“Rick? are you Okay?, what’s wrong?” Monty whispered, his voice thick with sleep.

Rick tried to compose himself, but the emotions overwhelmed him. “I—I saw them, Monty... my family. My mom, my dad, Krai... they were all calling my name, but then... then they... they were bleeding, and they—” His voice faltered, breaking into more sobs.
Monty placed a hand on his shoulder, unsure of how to comfort him, but trying nonetheless. “It’s okay, Rick. It was just a dream. Just a bad dream. They’re not gone. They’re not.”

Marcus, who had been resting in a chair nearby, heard the distress and quietly stood. His face softened as he walked over to the boys, sensing the weight of the nightmare that had shaken Rick. He placed a reassuring hand on Rick’s head.
“It’s alright, Rick,” Marcus said, his voice steady but filled with empathy. “I know the feeling. I’ve been there.”
Rick looked up at Marcus through his tear-filled eyes. “You… you know how it feels?”

Marcus nodded as he sat closer to the kids. “When I was about your age, only a bit younger, my world shattered too. My parents died in a war that broke out unexpectedly. I was left with nothing but the clothes on my back and a heart full of rage and confusion. It wasn’t easy. For years, I blamed the world, blamed myself. But I learned to keep moving forward.”
Rick sat up, the sobs receding, but his eyes were still filled with sadness. “I don’t know how to move on, Sir Marcus. Every time I close my eyes, I see them. I hear them screaming for help.”

Marcus bringing Rick into his embrace. “I understand. But the truth is, Rick, you can’t change what happened. What you can do is choose how to live now. Your family may be gone, but their memory, the love they gave you, that’s something no one can take from you. You have to keep their legacy alive by being strong, by using what you have left to make the world a better place.”
Rick, detaching from Marcus' embrace wiped his eyes, feeling the weight of Marcus’ words. It wasn’t a cure, but it was a start. He nodded slowly. “I’ll try, Sir Marcus.”

Monty, who had been listening quietly, now spoke up. “I know how you feel too, Rick. When I was younger, my parents were killed in an ambush by bandits. I was taken, and sold as a slave to that merchant. I didn’t have anyone to turn to, and I thought I was alone. But now… I’m here with you. And Sir Marcus.” He smiled weakly. “So we’re not alone, right?”

Rick glanced over at Monty, the comfort of his words starting to settle in. He reached out and gave Monty a quick hug, feeling the bond of friendship strengthen. “Thanks, Monty. I’m glad we’re together.”
Marcus stood up, his hands clasped behind his back. “You two have a lot of strength in you, even if you don’t see it yet. Keep holding on to that. The world is tough, but so are you.”

The three sat in the quiet of the room for a while, the night stretching on as they shared their stories and their pain. The shadows outside deepened, but inside, the warmth of their newfound connection grew.
"You know what kids?" Marcus said with a bright smile "Tomorrow I'll take you guys to Rover Kingdom" he said as he smiled
"Rover kingdom?" Rick asked
"Where's that?" Monty added
"It's a bright and beautiful city, you kids will love it!"
"Are we now travelers, Rick?" Monty asked with excitement
"I don't think so Monty, but since it will be our first time in Rover kingdom we could be regarded as travelers, right Sir Marcus?" Rick implied as they tilted their heads towards Marcus
"Of course!" Marcus answered brightly "you guys will get to see a lot of amazing things and places in the Rover Kingdom"
"Yay!"
"Alright!" The kids yelled with excitement

After a while, Rick and Monty, their minds quieted by the soothing words of Marcus, finally drifted back to sleep. This time, their dreams were less haunted by fear and more by the faint hope of a future they could shape with their own hands.
Marcus watched them, a soft smile playing on his lips. He had helped them take one step forward in their journey, and he knew there would be many more steps to come.
With a deep breath, Marcus whispered to the sleeping boys, “Rest, you’ve earned it. Tomorrow’s a new day.”
And so, in the quiet of the night, they found some peace.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The Journey Begins
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty prepare for their journey to Rover Kingdom with Marcus. After enjoying breakfast, Marcus surprises them with new clothes and boots, giving them a fresh sense of confidence. They then board a wagon pulled by majestic Shirys and begin their journey. As the road unfolds before them, Rick feels hopeful and excited about the new world and possibilities awaiting them.
paragraphs: The morning sun streamed through the window, casting a warm glow across the room. Rick and Monty awoke to the sound of birds chirping outside, their faces bright with excitement. Today was the day they would finally set off to Rover Kingdom, a place they had only heard about in passing, a place of promise and mystery.
As they rubbed their eyes and stretched, Marcus walked in, a gentle smile on his face, his eyes gleaming with the same excitement they felt.
"Time to get ready, boys," Marcus said, his tone light and encouraging. "I'll show you to the restroom, so you can freshen up."

Rick and Monty followed Marcus with eager steps, each of them feeling the anticipation growing with every step. They had no idea what to expect from Rover Kingdom, but the thought of seeing a new city, experiencing new things, filled them with wonder and hope.

As they bathed, the cool water helped clear the remnants of their lingering fears from the night before. Monty was the first to finish, quickly dressing and running his fingers through his hair with an excited grin. Rick took a little longer, taking in the calm, the silence of the moment. For once, his thoughts weren’t clouded by grief.
When Rick finished, he met Monty outside the restroom. The sunlight bathed them both in warmth, and Rick couldn’t help but smile as he saw the pure excitement on Monty’s face.
As they walked out of the restroom, Rick couldn't help but ask, "Are we heading to Rover Kingdom now, Sir Marcus?"

Marcus glanced at them with a chuckle. "Of course not, Rick. First, you need to fill your stomachs. A journey like this requires a lot of energy," he said, his eyes twinkling with humor. "Besides, it'll be quite a long trip."

At that moment, Monty’s stomach growled loudly, echoing through the hallway. The boys all laughed, the sound breaking through the heaviness that had lingered around them ever since their painful pasts had come to light.
"You hear that?" Marcus said with a grin. "We definitely need some food first."

They made their way out into the streets of Bellowing City, where the morning air was crisp and filled with the hustle and bustle of the city. As they passed through the crowded market district, Rick took in the sights and sounds—the calls of street vendors, the hum of distant chatter, the scent of fresh bread and roasted meats wafting through the air. For a moment, it felt like the world was full of possibilities.
At last, Marcus led them to a charming restaurant nestled between two towering buildings. A wooden sign swung gently in the breeze, its carved letters reading "The Roaming Rooster."

The moment they stepped inside, the rich aroma of freshly baked bread and sizzling meat enveloped them. The restaurant was warm, the atmosphere cozy, with soft laughter filling the space. They found a seat by the window, where the sun’s rays streamed in and cast a golden glow over their table.

Marcus ordered a hearty meal—bread, meats, eggs, and fruits—and the three boys dug in. The food was delicious, each bite filling them with warmth and energy. Monty’s eyes lit up with joy as he tasted the fresh bread, while Rick savored the flavors, appreciating how something as simple as a meal could bring such comfort.

After a while, Monty’s stomach, now thoroughly satisfied, grumbled again. He looked up at Marcus with an eager expression. “Can we go now?” His voice was full of excitement, his eyes shining with anticipation.
Marcus raised a finger, a mischievous glint in his eyes. "Not yet, Monty," he said, his smile widening. "Not in these torn clothes, anyway."
The boys blinked in confusion, looking down at their worn-out clothes. They were comfortable but far from new or presentable for the adventure ahead.
"What do you mean, Sir Marcus?" Rick asked, tilting his head in curiosity.
Marcus’s grin widened. "We’re going to get you two some new clothes first! It’ll be much more fitting for your journey," he said with a wink.
The kids’ faces lit up in surprise and delight. "New clothes?!" Monty and Rick yelled in unison, their voices filled with astonishment and excitement.
Marcus chuckled, his heart light at seeing their joy. "Yes, new clothes! And I know just the place."

They paid for their meal and walked out of the restaurant, the warm sun beating down on them as they stepped into the lively streets of the city. The market buzzed with activity, and Rick marveled at how different the world seemed now. With his new friends by his side, it almost felt like a new beginning.

As they walked down the street, Marcus pointed to a tall building with a wooden sign reading “Vaughn’s Fine Tailoring.” It was a shop filled with vibrant fabrics and delicate embroideries, the window displays showcasing a collection of finely crafted garments.

Marcus pushed open the door, and the bell above it jingled as they stepped inside. The warm, earthy smell of dyed cloth and the sight of neatly stacked piles of fabric greeted them. Behind the counter stood an older man with graying hair and a welcoming smile.
"Good morning!" the tailor said. "What can I do for you, Marcus?"
"I need some new clothes for these two fine lads," Marcus said with a grin. "Something practical but nice. They’ve got a long journey ahead."
The tailor’s eyes sparkled as he looked at the boys. "Of course! We’ll make sure they look presentable." He immediately began to measure Rick and Monty, his hands swift and skilled.

The boys were soon outfitted with new tunics, trousers, and sturdy boots. The fabrics were soft but durable, perfect for their upcoming travels. Rick could hardly believe how different he felt in the new clothes—he was no longer the ragged orphan he had once been, but someone ready for the next chapter of his life.

As they admired their new clothes, Monty grinned widely. “Thank you, Sir Marcus!” Rick echoed his sentiment, both of them feeling a wave of gratitude wash over them. They had come so far in such a short time.
Marcus clapped his hands together. “You look perfect, ready for the journey ahead.”

With their new clothes and a renewed sense of excitement, the three of them set out toward Rover Kingdom. The road ahead would be long, but it was the beginning of something far more exciting than they had ever imagined.

As they exited the tailoring shop, Marcus led them to the city's transport center where the wagons awaited. Instead of regular horses, magnificent Shirys—large, feathered creatures resembling giant winged deer—stood in their harnesses, their wings gently fluttering as they nuzzled the ground. These graceful beings were known for their strength and agility, and their majestic presence made them the perfect choice for long journeys.

The Shirys were each hitched to a large, ornate wagon, their feathers shimmering in the sun's glow. Their gentle eyes met the trio’s, and there was an unspoken bond of trust between them and their riders.
Marcus gestured to the wagons. "These fine creatures will take us to Rover Kingdom. They’re swift and sure-footed, perfect for the journey."
Rick and Monty’s eyes widened at the sight of the Shirys, their excitement growing even more.
“Are they really going to pull the wagon?” Rick asked, his voice filled with awe.
Marcus nodded with a grin. “They are. These creatures are more reliable than any horse, and their strength is unmatched.”

The trio climbed into the wagon, the Shirys pulling the load effortlessly as they began their journey. The road to Rover Kingdom was long, but as they rode, the adventure truly began. The air was crisp, the landscape stretched out before them, and Rick couldn’t help but feel a sense of wonder at the world opening up to them.
“You know what, kids?” Marcus said, his voice filled with optimism as they rode side by side. "This is only the start. There's a whole world out there waiting for us."
Rick felt his heart swell with a sense of hope. For the first time in a long while, the future seemed full of promise.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Bandits at Lavender Mountain.
chapters.summary: While traveling through Lavender Mountain, Rick, Monty, and Marcus are ambushed by a group of bandits. As the boys are overcome by fear, Marcus calmly steps in and defeats the attackers with incredible ease, even without using a weapon. His overwhelming strength leaves the guards and bandits stunned, hinting that Marcus possesses a power far beyond what they imagined. With the threat eliminated, the journey to Rover Kingdom continues.
paragraphs: The sun shone brightly over the vast plains of Lavender Mountain, casting a golden glow over the rolling hills and rich lavender fields that stretched for miles. The air was fragrant with the soothing scent of blooming flowers and the rustle of trees that seemed to hum with life. Rick and Monty sat in the back of the wagon, their hands busy with a simple hand game to pass the time. Laughter filled the air, and for a moment, the tension of the journey was forgotten.

Marcus, ever the picture of ease, was napping peacefully. His head rested against the wooden frame of the wagon, and his chest rose and fell in steady rhythm. Even in sleep, there was an air of quiet authority about him—a sleeping lion amidst sheep.
Suddenly, a sharp cry shattered the tranquility. The rider of the Shiryl barked loudly, "Bandits!"
Rick and Monty froze, their faces drained of color. The Shiryl rider shouted again, more urgently, "Bandits! Bandits!"

Monty’s heart dropped into his stomach. His breath quickened, and his mind filled with the haunting memories of the bandit raid that had taken his parents away. His trembling fingers dug into Rick’s arm, and he could feel the boy’s heart pounding in his chest.
Rick, equally terrified, shook Marcus awake, his voice barely a whisper as he tugged on the older man’s sleeve. “Sir Marcus, there are bandits outside.”

Marcus groggily stirred, barely registering the fear in Rick’s voice. He opened his eyes to the sound of clashing swords and frantic shouts. Sitting up, now fully alert, he saw Rick and Monty huddled in the corner of the wagon, their faces pale and eyes wide with terror.

With a knowing smile, Marcus said in his usual sarcastic tone, “Don’t worry, kids. Everything's going to be fine. Stay here, and I'll go handle those bad guys.” His faint, reassuring smile seemed to calm them slightly before he stepped out of the wagon.

Outside, chaos reigned. The security men, six in total, were fighting desperately against a group of fifteen bandits. The attackers were armed with swords, daggers, and makeshift weapons, while the security men were valiant but visibly outnumbered. Some were already wounded.

Marcus surveyed the scene, his expression calm and almost bored. He spotted four bandits standing back, watching the chaos unfold. With a sigh, he grabbed a nearby wooden stick and dashed toward a security man who was about to be stabbed.

Marcus moved like a blur, his stick striking with such precision that the bandit crumpled to the ground instantly. “Rest now,” Marcus said, gently laying the wounded guard down. “I’ll handle these miscreants.”

The remaining bandits turned to Marcus, their initial confidence faltering. One lunged at him with a sword, but Marcus sidestepped effortlessly, his movements so fluid it seemed time itself slowed. With a single strike from his stick, he knocked the man unconscious.

Another bandit tried to tackle Marcus from behind, but with a fluid motion, Marcus spun around, delivering a crushing elbow strike to the bandit’s chest. The man flew backward, already out cold before he hit the ground.
The four bandits who had been watching now stepped forward, their eyes narrowing. “Who is this guy?” one muttered, disbelief etched on his face.

One of them, a towering figure with a scar on his chin, wielding a massive hammer, clapped his hands mockingly. “You’re quite skilled, young man,” he said with a grin. “Why don’t you join us? We can make it worth your while.”
Marcus sneered at the offer. “Me? Join you weak miscreants? Not happening.”
The bandit’s grin faltered, his eyes darkening with fury. “You dare insult us?” another growled, stepping forward with a sharp iron whip. “You’ll pay for that with your life!”
Marcus casually tossed his stick aside, an evil grin spreading across his face. “You know what? I’ll defeat all four of you with nothing but my bare hands—just to show you how weak you are.”
The bandits bristled with anger, and one bellowed, “You ignorant bastard! This will be the end of you!”

They lunged at Marcus as one, their weapons glinting in the sunlight. The hammer-wielder swung with terrifying force, but Marcus ducked under the swing, his movements graceful and almost lazy. The hammer struck the ground with a deep thud, missing by miles.
Marcus rolled his eyes. “What’s wrong? You’re moving slower than my morning stretch,” he quipped, dodging another attack with ease.

The bandits growled in frustration. The spear wielder thrust at him, but Marcus grabbed the shaft mid-thrust, yanking it from the man’s hands. With a swift motion, he used the spear to knock the man backward, sending him sprawling to the ground.

The iron whip lashed out, aiming for Marcus’ legs. He jumped over it effortlessly, landing a spinning kick to the whip wielder’s chest. The bandit flew back, crashing into a tree and slumping unconscious.
The sword wielder hesitated, sweat beading on his forehead. “Who... who are you?” he stammered, his voice trembling.

Marcus grinned. “Just a guy who’s had enough of bandits like you.” He dodged the sword’s swing, landing a devastating punch to the bandit’s gut, followed by an uppercut. The man dropped like a sack of potatoes.
Rick and Monty watched in awe, their fear replaced by admiration. “Wow, Sir Marcus is really strong!” Monty whispered, his tears forgotten.
Rick nodded, his voice filled with relief. “Yeah... we don’t need to cry anymore. He’ll definitely protect us.”
The security men and the Shiryl rider were speechless, staring at Marcus in awe. “He defeated all those bandits alone!” one guard whispered.
“They weren’t just any bandits,” another added. “Those last four were probably in the Obsidian Tier of the Earth Realm. And he knocked them out with one move each.”
“Does that mean...” one guard trailed off in shock. “Is he at the Immortal Realm?”
Marcus ignored their whispers and strolled back to the wagon. Tilting his head toward the conscious bandits, he said, “Take your people and leave. Now. Or I’ll change my mind.”
The bandits scrambled to their feet, carrying their fallen comrades as they fled into the distance.
“Now,” Marcus said, offering a reassuring smile to Rick and Monty, “let’s get back on the road. We’ve got a long way to go.”
The wagon rolled onward, the lavender fields stretching endlessly before them. For Rick and Monty, Marcus wasn’t just a protector—he was an unstoppable force of nature.

chapters.label: Chapter 9
chapters.title: Arrival at the Rover Kingdom.
chapters.summary: After a long journey, Rick, Monty, and Marcus finally arrive at the magnificent Rover Kingdom. Along the way, they stop at a village to rest and eat before continuing to the kingdom’s grand gates. Once inside, Rick and Monty are amazed by the bustling city and its vibrant streets. Marcus treats them to a meal and a comfortable night at an inn, giving the boys a chance to rest before discovering what Rover Kingdom has in store for them.
paragraphs: The sun had begun its descent, casting a warm, golden hue across the horizon as the wagon rolled steadily onward. The lavender fields had long disappeared, replaced by open plains dotted with trees and patches of farmland. After traveling for a while, the group approached a small, peaceful village nestled against a backdrop of gentle hills.

Rick, staring out at the serene surroundings, was reminded of Harmony Village during its days of peace and prosperity. The memory lit up his face, his eyes glistening with a mixture of nostalgia and happiness. Monty’s stomach, however, had other priorities—it let out a loud growl, breaking the momentary silence.

Everyone, including Marcus, burst into laughter. “Alright, that’s enough,” Marcus said, shaking his head with a grin. He leaned forward and tapped the Shiryl rider on the shoulder. “Let’s stop here for a while. The kids need some food, and the men could use a bit of rest.”

The Shiryl rider nodded and pulled the reins, bringing the wagon to a gentle halt near the village square. The security men, still nursing their injuries from the bandit attack, took the opportunity to visit a nearby physician’s store for treatment. Meanwhile, Marcus, Rick, and Monty strolled through the village, searching for a place to grab some snacks.

The air in the village was filled with the enticing aroma of freshly baked bread and roasted meat. Rick and Monty excitedly picked out a few treats, their laughter ringing through the square as Marcus handed over some coins to a smiling vendor. After a short rest and some much-needed refreshment, the group returned to the wagon and resumed their journey.

Hours passed, and the gentle rocking of the wagon lulled the kids into a deep sleep. The once-vibrant laughter was replaced by the rhythmic creak of the wheels and the occasional chirping of crickets. Marcus leaned back, his sharp eyes scanning the road ahead.

In the distance, the grand gates of the Rover Kingdom began to take shape, illuminated by the glow of lanterns hanging from tall, ornate posts. To Marcus, the sight was familiar yet reassuring, like a trusted sentinel guarding the vibrant life within the city walls. He couldn’t help but feel a twinge of relief as they neared their destination.
He gently nudged the kids awake, his voice soft but firm. “Wake up, kids. We’ve arrived.”

Rick and Monty stirred, rubbing their eyes groggily. As they sat up, the majestic gates came into view, and their fatigue was instantly replaced by wonder. The wagon slowed as they approached the gates, and the Shiryl rider brought it to a halt.

A group of soldiers clad in polished armor stood guard, their spears gleaming under the lantern light. One of them stepped forward, his voice commanding. “Halt! State your business and present your pass.”

The Shiryl rider reached into his satchel and handed over a rolled-up pass. The soldier inspected it carefully before signaling to his comrades. Another soldier approached the wagon and peered inside, his eyes narrowing as he noticed the bandages on some of the security men.
“What happened to your men?” the soldier asked, his tone laced with concern.

“An unfortunate encounter with bandits,” the Shiryl rider explained. “We were lucky to have this man with us.” He gestured toward Marcus, who remained seated, his face calm and composed. The soldier gave Marcus a respectful nod before stepping back.
“All clear!” he shouted, signaling to the gatekeeper. The massive iron gates groaned as they swung open, revealing the bustling city beyond.

As the wagon rolled into the kingdom, Rick and Monty poked their heads out, their mouths agape. The city of Rover was alive with activity, even at this late hour. The streets were lined with shops, taverns, and homes, their windows glowing with warm light. Merchants shouted from their stalls, hawking their wares to eager customers. Horses trotted by, their hooves clacking against the cobblestone streets, and children played near fountains adorned with intricate carvings.

Marcus glanced at the kids and smiled. “Welcome to the Rover Kingdom, kids,” he said with a faint, proud grin. Rick and Monty were too mesmerized to respond, their eyes darting from one spectacle to another.

The wagon eventually came to a stop at the kingdom’s transportation center, a bustling hub filled with travelers, wagons, and Shiryls. Marcus helped the kids down from the wagon before turning to the Shiryl rider.
“How much do I owe you?” Marcus asked, his tone firm but polite.
The rider waved his hand dismissively. “Oh no, mister. Don’t bother about such a thing. Besides, it’s because of you we’re alive!”

Marcus frowned slightly. “No, I have to pay for the services I received. I was just doing my duty protecting the kids. Besides, I know you all need the money.” Without waiting for a response, he tossed a small bag of coins to the rider.
“Make sure to pay the security men well so they can get good treatment,” Marcus added as he turned and began walking away with the kids.

The rider caught the bag and stared at it for a moment before calling out, “Of course, young sir! Thank you!” His voice was filled with gratitude as he watched Marcus disappear into the bustling crowd, Rick and Monty trailing behind him.

By now, hunger had begun to gnaw at their stomachs again, and Marcus decided it was time for a proper meal. He led the kids to a nearby restaurant, its warm lights and inviting aroma drawing them in. They found a cozy corner and ordered a hearty meal, sharing stories and laughs as they ate. The food was delicious, and Rick and Monty devoured their portions with enthusiasm, earning a few amused glances from the other patrons.

After the meal, Marcus led them to an inn not far from the restaurant. The building was grand and glamorous, its polished wooden beams and golden accents glinting in the lantern light. As they stepped inside, Rick and Monty’s eyes widened in amazement, their excitement barely contained.

Marcus approached the innkeeper, who welcomed them warmly and handed over a key to their room. The room itself was spacious and luxurious, with soft beds draped in fine linens. There were two beds—one for Marcus and one for the boys to share.
Rick and Monty immediately jumped onto their bed, their laughter filling the room. Marcus smiled, watching them for a moment before settling onto his own bed.
“Get some rest, kids,” he said softly. “Tomorrow’s a new day, and we’ve got plenty to do.”
The boys nodded, their energy quickly fading as exhaustion took over. Within minutes, they were fast asleep, their faces peaceful. Marcus lay back, his mind filled with thoughts of the journey ahead.
As the city of Rover thrummed with life outside, the three of them drifted into a deep, restful sleep, ready to face whatever awaited them in the days to come.

chapters.label: Chapter 10
chapters.title: Old Friends, New Beginnings.
chapters.summary: Marcus reconnects with his old friends, Lucy and Laura, after arriving in Rover Kingdom and asks to stay with them while he searches for a home. He introduces Ricky and Monty to their welcoming household, where they are given a safe room, food, and a warm sense of belonging. As Marcus explains how he rescued the boys from the merchant, his friends promise to help care for them. For Ricky and Monty, their new home marks the beginning of a peaceful life surrounded by people who genuinely care about them.
paragraphs: The sun’s warm rays poured into the room as Ricky and Monty stirred awake, their youthful excitement still bubbling from the previous day. Marcus smiled as he watched them stretch and chatter, already eager for the day ahead.
"Alright, boys," Marcus said as he pulled on his boots, "let’s head to the public pool. Time to freshen up!"

The pool was a lively hub of activity, with townsfolk splashing, laughing, and enjoying the morning. For Ricky and Monty, it was an entirely new experience. The cool water, the joyful noise, and the camaraderie of shared space filled them with glee. Marcus chuckled as Monty tried to splash Ricky, only for Ricky to retaliate with surprising precision.

After drying off, they made their way back to the restaurant they’d visited the night before, now officially named The Golden Plate. The warm aroma of freshly baked bread and sizzling meat welcomed them as they entered. Marcus ordered a hearty meal for the three of them, and they ate with relish, savoring every bite.

Once back at the inn, Marcus knelt to meet the boys at eye level. "Alright, you two," he said with a gentle but firm tone, "I have to take care of something important. Stay here, and don’t cause any trouble. The innkeeper will keep an eye on you."
The boys nodded, though Monty’s face fell slightly at the thought of being left behind. Marcus ruffled his hair. "I won’t be long," he promised before heading out into the bustling streets of Rover.
Marcus arrived at a modest but well-kept house on the eastern side of the city. Before he could knock, the door swung open, revealing a woman with piercing green eyes and short, fiery-red hair.
"Marcus!" she exclaimed, throwing her arms around him.
"Lucy," Marcus greeted warmly, returning the hug.
A moment later, another figure emerged—tall, with raven-black hair tied into a neat bun.
"Look who decided to show up," Laura teased, crossing her arms with a sly smile.
"Well, I couldn’t stay away forever," Marcus said, his tone light but sincere.
The three friends settled into the living room, reminiscing about old times over cups of steaming tea.
"So," Laura began, leaning forward with a mischievous glint in her eye, "what brings you back to Rover? And don’t tell me it’s just for the scenery."
Marcus chuckled, rubbing the back of his neck. "I’ve been traveling," he began, "and I’ve got a couple of companions with me this time."
"Companions?" Lucy interjected, arching an eyebrow. "You? With companions? Are they bounty hunters too?"
"Not this time," Marcus replied with a laugh. "They’ve been through a lot, and I was hoping you’d let us stay here for a bit until I find a place of our own."
Lucy and Laura exchanged glances. "Of course," Lucy said without hesitation. "You’re family, Marcus. You’ll always have a place here."
"Thanks," Marcus said, his voice thick with gratitude. "I really appreciate it."
"Just one thing," Laura added, her curiosity piqued. "These companions of yours...what are they like?"
Marcus hesitated, a small smile playing at his lips. "You’ll see soon enough," he said cryptically.
Back at the inn, Ricky and Monty were thrilled when Marcus returned. "Sir Marcus!" they called out, rushing to greet him.
"Get your things," Marcus said with a grin. "We’ve got a new place to stay."

The boys quickly packed their belongings, their excitement palpable. Marcus settled the bill with the innkeeper before leading them out into the afternoon sun. As they walked toward Lucy and Laura’s home, the boys bombarded Marcus with questions about where they were going and who they’d be staying with.
"You’ll find out," Marcus replied with a knowing smile.
When they finally arrived, Lucy and Laura were waiting at the door, flanked by several unfamiliar faces.
"Welcome!" Lucy called, her smile bright.

Beside her stood Miriam, the gentle housekeeper with kind eyes and a warm smile, and Elias, the sharp-eyed but warm-hearted gardener. Rosa, the ever-cheerful cook, peeked out from behind them, wiping her flour-covered hands on an apron, while Theo, a lively and playful young man, leaned against the doorframe with a mischievous grin.
"These are your companions?" Lucy asked, her surprise evident as her gaze fell on Ricky and Monty.
Marcus nodded. "Yep. Meet Ricky and Monty," he said with a grin.
The boys stepped forward shyly, offering small waves. Lucy and Laura exchanged a glance before their expressions softened.
"Well," Laura said, crouching to their level, "welcome to our home. We’re happy to have you."
Maura stepped forward with a motherly smile. "Hello, boys. I’m Maura. I’ll make sure you feel right at home here. Are you hungry? I made some fresh pastries earlier."
