The mention of food immediately brightened Monty’s expression. "Yes, ma’am!" he said eagerly, and Ricky nodded politely.
"And I’m Elias," the gardener added, his tone gentle but cheerful. "If you ever want to see the garden or help me out with the flowers, you’re always welcome."
"I’m Theo," the young man said with a wink. "You’ll see me around. I’ve got some fun stuff to show you when you’re ready."
"And I’m Rosa," the cook said with a laugh. "If you like sweets, I’ve got plenty of those too."
The boys’ shyness began to melt away as they were welcomed warmly. "Thank you, ma’am. Thank you, sir," Ricky said politely, while Monty beamed up at them.

Inside, Laura gave the boys a tour of the house while Maura whisked away to prepare some snacks. The tour concluded in their new room, a cozy space with two beds, soft linens, and a small window that overlooked Elias’s vibrant garden.
"This is incredible," Monty whispered as he ran to the window, staring out at the colorful flowers below.
Laura smiled warmly. "You deserve a safe and comfortable place, both of you. Make yourselves at home."
Meanwhile, Maura returned with a tray of pastries and milk, placing them on the table in the boys’ room. "Here you go," she said softly. "Eat up, and let me know if you need anything else."
The boys nodded enthusiastically, digging into the treats.
Later, Lucy stayed behind with Marcus in the sitting room. "So, where did you find them?" she asked, her voice low as she studied Marcus closely.

Marcus sighed and leaned against the wall. "It was a long road. I found them in a merchant's camp. I saw potential in them plus their talents were being wasted, and I couldn’t just walk away. So I ended up buying their freedom, giving them a chance at a better life."
Lucy’s eyes softened with understanding. "You’ve got a good heart, Marcus."
He smiled faintly. "I’m just trying to do right by them. They’ve been through a lot, and they deserve a safe place, just like we did."
As their conversation ended, Elias passed through the hallway, offering Marcus a nod. "They’ll be alright here, Marcus," he said with quiet confidence. "We’ll make sure of it."

The day ended with laughter and warmth as Marcus and his friends caught up, and the boys reveled in the wonders of their new surroundings. Maura tucked Ricky and Monty into bed, humming a soft tune, while Elias stayed up late tending to the garden, preparing it for the boys to explore the next day.
It was a moment of peace, a respite from the chaos of their past, and Marcus knew that this was the start of a new chapter for them all.

chapters.label: Chapter 11
chapters.title: A New Routine.
chapters.summary: Ricky and Monty slowly begin adjusting to life in their new home, learning that they no longer have to fear punishment or mistreatment. After being welcomed into the household, they enjoy a warm breakfast and spend the day exploring Rover City, including an exciting ride through the skies on the city’s magnificent creatures. Although they worry about Marcus being away, their new friends reassure them that he will return. With each passing day, the boys grow more comfortable, hopeful, and trusting as they begin building a new life.
paragraphs: Laura and Lucy exchanged amused glances as they approached the boys’ room. To their surprise, Ricky and Monty were already awake, sitting upright with wide, startled eyes.
“Aren’t you boys supposed to be asleep?” Lucy teased, her voice warm and amused. “You must be used to waking up early.”
Ricky scrambled to respond, his voice trembling slightly. “Oh, sorry, ma’am! We thought it was morning already. Please don’t punish us. We’ll wake up earlier next time, I promise!”
Monty, clutching the blanket tightly, nodded vigorously, his face pale.

Before Lucy could respond, Elric, who had overheard from the hallway, leaned casually against the doorframe, his tone light yet firm. “Punish you? That’s not how we do things around here, boys. You're safe now.”

His presence seemed to calm them slightly, though their expressions remained wary. Lucy crouched to their eye level, her tone soft. “There’s no need to wake up early here unless you want to. You can sleep as much as you like. No one will hurt you here, I promise.”
Ricky hesitated, casting a nervous glance at Monty before whispering, “Our owner... I mean, the merchant used to punish us if we woke up late. We didn’t want to make you angry.”

Miriam, passing by with an armful of freshly folded clothes, paused mid-step. Her expression softened, and she walked into the room, placing the clothes on a nearby chair. “Oh, sweethearts,” she said gently. “No one here will ever treat you like that. You’ve been through so much, haven’t you?”
The boys nodded, their shoulders relaxing slightly.

Rosa peeked into the room, her voice warm but teasing. “You two are lucky. Do you know how many people would love to sleep in a warm bed like this and have everyone fuss over them? You’d better enjoy it!”
The boys exchanged a glance before Ricky smiled tentatively. “Thank you. We’ll try.”
Lucy straightened, her usual cheerfulness returning. “We actually came to see if you’d like to join us for morning exercises,” she said.
“Exercises?” Ricky asked, his brow furrowed.
Theo stepped into the doorway, grinning. “Yeah! It’s more fun than it sounds. It’s how we all stay in shape—well, except for Elias, who just likes to watch and make comments.”
Elias, leaning against the wall, raised his hands in mock protest. “Hey, someone has to supervise. And besides, I don’t need exercises; I’m naturally perfect.”
His playful tone drew a small chuckle from Monty, who quickly hid his smile behind his hand.
Lucy noticed the boys’ lingering exhaustion and softened her tone. “Actually, you both look like you could use more rest. Why don’t you sleep in today and join us tomorrow instead?”
Relieved, the boys nodded, lying back down. Before they drifted off, Ricky whispered to Monty, “Everything’s different now. I promise to get stronger so I can protect people who need help.”
Monty smiled faintly. “Me too. We’ll make sure no one goes through what we did.”
The two shared a quiet chuckle before sleep claimed them, hope flickering like a small but steady flame in their hearts.
When dawn broke, Ricky and Monty awoke feeling refreshed. They made their way to the bathroom, marveling at the warm water in the tub.
“This is amazing!” Monty exclaimed, splashing water with a wide grin.
“You think they’ll let us use this every day?” Ricky asked, laughing.
“Why not?” Rosa’s voice came from the hallway as she passed by. “It’s your bathroom now. Just don’t flood the place, okay?”
The boys dressed quickly, their spirits buoyed, and headed to the dining hall. The aroma of freshly baked bread and sizzling meat greeted them.
“Good morning, boys!” Laura said brightly, motioning for them to sit.

The table was already lively. Theo was animatedly recounting a funny incident from the stables, while Miriam chided Elias for stealing food off her plate. Ricky and Monty hesitated, scanning the room.
“Where’s Marcus?” Ricky asked nervously.
Lucy, seated beside Laura, smiled reassuringly. “He had to leave for a quick business trip. He didn’t want to wake you, but he’ll be back soon.”
Monty’s face fell. “Did he… abandon us?” he whispered, his voice barely audible.

Elric, seated across from them, leaned forward, his expression serious but kind. “Marcus would never abandon you,” he said firmly. “He probably thought you’d feel safer if he didn’t disturb you. Trust me—he’ll be back before you know it.”
Though still uncertain, the boys began eating, their spirits lifting as the others pulled them into the lively conversation.
After breakfast, Laura clapped her hands. “All right, everyone. It’s time to show these boys the best parts of Rover City!”
The group made their way to the stables, where the boys were introduced to the incredible creatures housed there.
“Whoa!” Ricky gasped, staring wide-eyed at a massive, bird-like horse with shimmering feathers.
Monty darted from stall to stall, his excitement bubbling over. “Can we ride them?” he asked eagerly.
“You sure can!” Theo said, already saddling one of the creatures. “With a little help, of course.”
Elric helped Ricky mount a horse, while Rosa and Miriam assisted Monty. Once everyone was ready, they took off into the sky, the boys’ laughter ringing out as they soared above the city.
“Look at that!” Monty shouted, pointing to the bustling streets below. “Everything looks so small!”
Ricky, awestruck, could only nod, his gaze fixed on the vibrant gardens and colorful rooftops below.
By the time they returned home, the boys were brimming with excitement, eagerly recounting their favorite moments to anyone who would listen.
As bedtime approached, Ricky hesitated at the door of his room. “Are you sure Marcus will come back?” he asked quietly.
Elias, leaning against the wall, rolled his eyes dramatically. “You’re starting to sound like an old grandmother. Yes, he’ll come back.”
Rosa nudged him with her elbow. “Elias, be nice,” she said before turning to Ricky. “Marcus always keeps his word. You’ll see him tomorrow.”
Reassured, Ricky nodded and climbed into bed, Monty already snuggled under the covers.
From the sitting room, Laura and Lucy watched the house settle into peaceful quiet.
“They’re starting to trust us,” Lucy said softly, her tone hopeful.
“It’ll take time,” Elric said from his spot by the window. “But they’ll get there.”
And as the stars lit up the night sky, the boys slept soundly, their hearts filled with the promise of a brighter tomorrow.

chapters.label: Chapter 12
chapters.title: Marcus's Absence – The Bounty Hunt.
chapters.summary: While away from the boys, Marcus tracks down a dangerous fugitive and engages him in a fierce battle, ultimately capturing him alive. Before being taken to the guild, the fugitive reveals cryptic information about an upcoming awakening and three mysterious factions working behind the scenes. Marcus reports the disturbing revelation to the guild master, realizing that a much larger conspiracy may be unfolding within the Rover Kingdom.
paragraphs: Marcus stepped silently through the dense forest of the Rover Kingdom, his senses sharp and honed from years of experience. The wind whispered through the trees, and the earth seemed to hold its breath as he pursued his quarry—a fugitive wanted for a string of heinous crimes that had stirred unrest across the kingdom. His target was no ordinary criminal. The man was a formidable foe, a master of martial arts, and ranked just below Marcus at the Eternal Vanguard level, but not quite at the peak. Even though he was technically weaker, the fugitive's agility and cunning were what made him dangerous.

Marcus had spent the past few days tracking the fugitive, piecing together his movements and planning his next move. The kingdom’s bounty hunting guild had put a hefty price on this man’s head, and Marcus’s reputation as one of the best bounty hunters in the kingdom had led him to take the mission personally. What he didn’t expect was the storm of events that would follow.

The air was thick with tension as he crept closer to his target’s last known location. The fugitive’s presence had been marked by a trail of blood—a warning of the man’s violent nature. But Marcus wasn’t worried. He’d faced worse. In fact, he’d been expecting a fight. It was only a matter of time before the fugitive realized he was being hunted.

Suddenly, a sharp snap of a branch echoed through the silence. Marcus froze, senses flaring. Before he could react, an arrow whizzed through the air, missing him by inches. His reflexes kicked in, and he ducked, rolling to the side just in time to avoid a second volley.

The fugitive was nearby. Marcus could feel his presence—a predator watching from the shadows. Without a word, Marcus sprang into action, using the environment to his advantage. He moved swiftly through the trees, his every movement deliberate, his body poised for combat.

It didn’t take long for the two to meet. Marcus was quick, but the fugitive was faster, leaping from the shadows with surprising grace. The fugitive’s body was lithe, his movements fluid, and his eyes narrowed with a quiet determination.
"So, you’re the one they sent," the fugitive sneered, his voice dripping with arrogance. "Let’s see if you’re as good as they say."
Marcus remained silent, his expression unreadable. He didn’t need words. His eyes, sharp and focused, spoke volumes as he shifted into a combat stance.
"Let’s end this quickly," Marcus muttered, his voice calm but firm.

The battle began in an instant. The fugitive attacked first, a flurry of quick jabs and rapid kicks aimed at Marcus’s head and torso. Marcus blocked and parried with precision, his movements sharp and calculated. Every strike the fugitive landed was met with a perfect counter, as if the two were dancing, their bodies in perfect synchronization despite the violence of their movements.

Marcus’s strength was undeniable, his strikes powerful enough to break bones. But the fugitive was no slouch. His speed and agility were remarkable, and he ducked and weaved around Marcus’s blows, striking when Marcus least expected it. The two warriors clashed again and again, their fists and feet moving like lightning, each attack resonating with the force of a thunderclap.

The fight raged on, neither side giving an inch. Marcus’s experience began to show as he weathered the fugitive’s attacks with calculated ease, but the fugitive was a step ahead, his unpredictability keeping Marcus on his toes.

For a moment, the two broke apart, circling each other warily. Both were winded, their muscles aching, but neither showed any sign of backing down. It was clear that this battle would not be won easily.
"You’re strong, but not strong enough," the fugitive taunted, breathing heavily.
Marcus’s lips curled into a slight grin. "We’ll see about that."

The fugitive launched a series of vicious blows, aiming for Marcus’s midsection. His fists were quick and relentless, landing with precise accuracy. For a brief moment, Marcus felt the pressure, his guard momentarily slipping as one of the fugitive’s strikes grazed his ribs. It was the first hit Marcus had taken in the entire fight, and it stung.

But that was all it was—a momentary lapse. Marcus’s instincts kicked in, and he shifted his weight, spinning on his heel to deliver a crushing kick to the fugitive’s chest. The blow sent the fugitive skidding backwards, but he recovered almost immediately, launching himself at Marcus once more.

Marcus didn’t give him the chance. With lightning speed, he moved, locking the fugitive in a tight hold. His grip was unyielding, and with a swift twist, he brought the fugitive to the ground. Pinning him there, Marcus leaned down, his voice low and firm. "Yield."
The fugitive gritted his teeth, but it was clear he had been beaten. He nodded reluctantly, his pride wounded but his life spared.
Marcus stood over the defeated fugitive, his chest rising and falling with each breath. "Who sent you?" Marcus demanded. "What’s going on with these attacks? Who’s behind them?"
The fugitive’s eyes burned with defiance, but after a long pause, he finally spoke. "You think you can stop what’s coming? The world’s about to change... the balance is already tipping."
Marcus’s grip tightened. "What are you talking about? Speak plainly."

The fugitive’s lips curled into a bitter smile. "There will be an awakening... three factions pulling the strings in the kingdom will see to it's success. You have no idea what’s really going on... but you’ll see soon enough."
Marcus’s eyes narrowed. He pressed further, his voice demanding answers. "Who are these factions?"

But the fugitive remained silent, his gaze distant. Despite Marcus’s attempts to get more information, the fugitive refused to speak. In the end, Marcus was left with only fragments—dangerous fragments—that hinted at something far greater than he could fully comprehend.

With no further answers to be had, Marcus tied the fugitive up and began his journey back to the guild. The mysterious words echoed in his mind. A conspiracy... Marcus knew the kingdom was on the brink of something, but what? And who could he trust?

As Marcus returned to the guild, the familiar sight of the tailor merchant—who was also the guild master—greeted him. He received his payment and a nod of approval, but Marcus’s mind was elsewhere. The cryptic words of the fugitive haunted him, and he knew that this was only the beginning.

Once the transaction was complete, Marcus made his way toward the back of the guild hall, where the guild master usually took refuge when there was little to do. The tailor merchant was seated at a wooden table, needle and thread in hand as he worked on a delicate stitch. He looked up as Marcus approached.
"I take it the job’s done?" the tailor asked, his tone casual, but there was a knowing glint in his eyes.
Marcus nodded, the weight of the bounty and the mission heavy on his shoulders. "It’s done. The fugitive’s captured, but I ran into something... strange."
The tailor’s hands paused, and he tilted his head, sensing the change in Marcus’s demeanor. "Strange? What kind of strange?"

Marcus lowered his voice, glancing around to ensure no one else was listening. "I think there’s something bigger happening—something brewing in the shadows. The fugitive mentioned factions, an awakening... three groups working together to manipulate the kingdom for its success. It’s more than just simple lawlessness."

The guild master raised an eyebrow, his fingers tapping lightly against the table as he considered the implications of Marcus’s words. "Factions? Three groups? That’s a troubling thought. But you’re not the first to mention something like that."
Marcus’s eyes narrowed. "You’ve heard of it?"
"Not in detail," the tailor replied. "But there have been rumors—whispers of discontent, of power struggles happening at the highest levels. It’s been... unsettling, to say the least."

The tension in Marcus’s body eased, but his mind was still racing. "I need to find out more. Whatever is going on, it’s going to be real big." He said "But I can't seem to figure it all out" he added as he dropped his head to his palm, giving out a soft slap.
The tailor nodded. "You’ll get your answers. Just remember, not all answers come easily. But you’ve got a lot more on your plate now than just a bounty."
"Well I better head back home now! I'll let you know if I find out something new" Marcus said as he stood up from the chair.
"My regards to them! And I'll also let you know if I find anything useful," the merchant replied.

With that, Marcus knew his journey was far from over. As he left the guild, the mystery deepened. The threads of the awakening were beginning to weave together, but Marcus was only scratching the surface. The calm before the storm was over, and the real battle had just begun.

chapters.label: Chapter 13
chapters.title: Training Day.
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty begin their martial training under Lucy and Laura, with Rick quickly showing natural talent while Monty struggles with self-doubt. After encouraging Monty and witnessing an impressive sparring match between their mentors, the boys receive a powerful lesson from Marcus, who teaches them his self-created technique, the Fist of Iron. Though the training leaves them exhausted, both boys gain confidence and determination, taking their first real steps toward becoming warriors.
paragraphs: The sun had barely risen, casting a soft golden hue over the sprawling land of Rover City, as Rick and Monty awoke. The excitement swirling in their chests felt vastly different—Rick’s resolve burned bright, unyielding, while Monty wrestled with a tangle of anticipation and self-doubt.
Lucy and Laura had promised to lead the way, and as soon as the boys were ready, they made their way through the grand halls of the mansion.
“Why is this place so big?” Monty muttered, craning his neck to take in the towering ceilings.
“It’s not just big,” Rick replied, his voice tinged with awe. “It’s like a castle!”
Laura overheard them and chuckled. “You’ll get used to it. Just don’t get lost—we won’t always be around to rescue you.”
Monty gave her a sheepish grin. “I think I already got lost twice yesterday.”

The training room lay beyond the large courtyard, and when they arrived, the boys were stunned into silence. The room was massive, with polished wooden floors, open areas for drills, sparring rings, and walls adorned with weapons from different eras. The air buzzed with the energy of countless warriors who had trained there before them.

“This is where you’ll learn to fight,” Lucy said, her voice steady and purposeful. “But remember, true strength isn’t just about physical power. It’s about discipline, control, and knowing when to fight—and when to hold back.”

Rick nodded eagerly, his eyes gleaming with determination. Monty, however, shuffled his feet nervously. Laura noticed and stepped beside him. “Hey,” she said softly. “It’s okay to be nervous. Everyone starts somewhere. Trust me—you’ve got this.”
Monty managed a small smile. “I’ll try.”
The training began in earnest. Lucy paired up with Monty, while Laura worked with Rick.
Monty struggled through the drills, his wooden staff slipping from his grip more times than he cared to admit. Each mistake left him red-faced, his frustration growing with every stumble.
“Relax,” Lucy said, her tone firm but patient. “You’re holding the staff too tightly. It’s about control, not brute strength.”
Monty tried to follow her instructions, but his movements still felt awkward. “I’m terrible at this,” he muttered under his breath.

Lucy crouched down to meet his gaze. “Listen, Monty. No one is good at something the first time they try it. Do you think I was born a warrior? It took years of practice and a lot of failures to get where I am now.”
“Really?” Monty asked, his eyes wide.
“Really,” Lucy said with a smile. “So cut yourself some slack, okay?”
Meanwhile, Laura put Rick through a series of fast-paced combat drills. His strikes were precise, his movements fluid.
“Not bad,” Laura said, nodding in approval. “But you’re dropping your left shoulder when you pivot. That’s a weakness your opponent could exploit.”
Rick adjusted his stance, focusing intently. “Like this?”
“Better,” Laura said. “But don’t overthink it. Trust your instincts.”
Rick grinned. “Got it!”
After hours of relentless practice, the group gathered for a break. The boys sat on the floor, gulping down water as Lucy and Laura joined them.
“How are you feeling?” Laura asked.
“Sore,” Rick admitted, wiping sweat from his brow. “But in a good way.”
Monty hesitated before speaking. “I feel... frustrated. Like I’m not good enough.”
Lucy placed a hand on his shoulder. “Monty, no one expects you to be perfect. Training is about progress, not perfection. You’ve already improved since this morning—you just don’t see it yet.”
Monty glanced at Rick, who gave him a reassuring smile. “She’s right, Monty. You’re doing great.”
Encouraged by their words, Monty straightened his back, a flicker of determination returning to his eyes.
Their conversation was interrupted by Marcus’s booming voice. “Hey, kids!” he called from the doorway, his broad figure backlit by the afternoon sun.
“Sir Marcus!” the boys chorused, scrambling to their feet.
“Perfect timing,” Lucy said with a smirk. “Come to steal the spotlight again?”
Marcus chuckled, scratching the back of his neck. “I just couldn’t resist seeing how our young warriors are doing.”
Rick and Monty beamed at the compliment, their earlier exhaustion momentarily forgotten.
“So, how’s the training going?” Marcus asked, crossing his arms.
“It’s hard,” Monty admitted. “But I’m trying.”
“Good,” Marcus said with a nod. “The harder it is, the more it means you’re growing. And trust me, Monty—every great warrior feels like quitting at some point. The key is to keep going.”
Lucy and Laura stepped into the sparring ring for a demonstration, drawing the boys’ attention.
“Pay close attention,” Laura said. “You’ll learn a lot by watching us.”

The boys watched in awe as the two women began their spar. Their movements were a blur of speed, precision, and power. Each strike, block, and counterattack displayed their extraordinary skill. At one point, the intensity of their duel made Rick and Monty shrink back, fearing they might harm each other.
Marcus, noticing their apprehension, placed a calming hand on their shoulders. “Relax,” he said. “This is how warriors train. They’re not trying to hurt each other—they’re pushing their limits.”
“They’re incredible,” Monty whispered, his earlier doubts momentarily forgotten.
Rick nodded, his eyes wide. “Do you think we’ll ever be that good?”
“Someday,” Marcus said, a proud smile on his face. “If you keep training.”
The spar ended in a draw, leaving the boys buzzing with excitement.
“That was amazing!” they exclaimed in unison.
Laura smiled warmly. “Thank you, but this was nothing special. You should see Marcus train.”
“Oh, stop it,” Marcus said with a sheepish grin, rubbing the back of his neck.
Lucy grinned. “Thank you. But remember, this is just the beginning. You have the potential to be even better.”
“Well, that’s enough for us today,” Lucy said. “Time to freshen up.”
Laura nodded, leading the way out of the ring.
As the women left, Marcus turned to the boys. “Hey, kids, I’d like to teach you something before we call it a day,” he said, stepping into the ring.
“Wow! A technique from Sir Marcus!” Monty exclaimed, his excitement spilling over.
“It must be top-tier,” Rick added, eagerly following him.

“Watch carefully,” Marcus said, taking a stance. Slowly, he raised his hands, clenching them into fists before bringing them down to his stomach. He pivoted his feet, turning to face a wooden mannequin. As he moved, his fists began to glow with a golden aura. With a swift motion, he unleashed a punch, releasing the energy in a blinding blast that shattered the mannequin and half the sparring ring.
The boys stared, mouths agape.
“Oops,” Marcus said with a sheepish grin. “Guess I overdid it. That was supposed to be 5% of my power.”
“Five percent?” Rick whispered, awestruck.
Marcus chuckled. “Alright, stop gawking. Take your stances.”
“But we don’t have magic yet,” Monty said hesitantly.

“That doesn’t matter,” Marcus replied. “Even without magic, this technique can be devastating. It's a technique I created myself, I call it the Fist of Iron. Master it now, and when your magic awakens, it’ll be even more powerful.”

The boys nodded eagerly, mimicking Marcus’s movements as he guided them. After several attempts, they began to grasp the basics, though their punches lacked the explosive energy of Marcus’s demonstration.
“You’re doing well,” Marcus said, patting their shoulders. “Keep practicing, and this will become second nature.”
By the time they finished, their bodies were sore but their spirits were high.
That evening, the group gathered in the dining hall for dinner. The boys chatted excitedly about the day’s lessons, their earlier exhaustion replaced by a renewed sense of purpose.
“You both did well today,” Lucy said, raising her glass.
“To Rick and Monty,” Laura added with a smile.
“To Rick and Monty!” the group echoed, their voices ringing with camaraderie.

As the boys basked in the warmth of their mentors’ support, they realized something important: they weren’t alone on this journey. With each other—and their mentors—they were ready for whatever challenges lay ahead.

chapters.label: Chapter 14
chapters.title: The Challenge Ahead.
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty continue their training until Lucy and Laura are unexpectedly summoned to the imperial palace because of a looming war. With their mentors gone, Marcus and the others take over their training and reveal that the boys will soon face a martial arts academy selection tournament. Later, while exploring Rover City, Rick and Monty are mocked and insulted by a group of bullies because of their past, but four mysterious children step in and defend them before disappearing. Despite the painful encounter, the boys gain renewed determination to become stronger and prove themselves.
paragraphs: The morning sun painted the training grounds in golden light as Rick and Monty began another day of drills. They felt invigorated, their muscles aching but growing stronger after the previous day’s training. Lucy and Laura watched over them with pride, offering tips and corrections as the boys worked on their stances and reflexes.

Nearby, Elias was sparring with Elric, their movements fluid and precise. Despite Elias’s calm demeanor, his strikes carried a strength that kept Elric on edge. “You’re too predictable, Elric,” Elias said, sidestepping an attack effortlessly.
Elric grinned, wiping sweat from his brow. “And you’re too serious. Loosen up a little, old man!”
Rosa and Miriam, seated on a nearby bench, giggled at the banter while preparing a light breakfast for everyone. “They’ll never stop arguing, will they?” Rosa asked, shaking her head.
Miriam smiled warmly. “It’s how they show they care. In their own way.”

Lucy and Laura exchanged amused looks before their expressions turned serious. A rider in imperial armor galloped into the courtyard, dust trailing behind him. The messenger dismounted swiftly, his expression grim as he approached Lucy and Laura, bowing respectfully.
“Generals,” he began, handing Lucy a sealed scroll. “Urgent news from the imperial palace. Your presence is requested immediately.”
Lucy’s eyes flickered with concern as she broke the seal and scanned the letter. Laura leaned closer, reading alongside her.
“What is it?” Rick asked, noticing their sudden change in demeanor.
Lucy sighed, folding the parchment. “It seems another kingdom is on the brink of declaring war. Laura and I are being summoned to help strategize.”
Monty’s face fell. “You’re leaving?”

“Yes,” Laura said gently, crouching to meet the boys’ eyes. “This is important. We don’t know how long we’ll be gone, but Marcus, Theo, and the others will continue your training. Trust them, and stay focused.”
Though the boys tried to hide their disappointment, Lucy noticed and softened her tone. “You’re stronger than you think. Use this time to prove it to yourselves. We’ll return soon.”
With that, Lucy and Laura left to prepare for their journey, leaving the group feeling a little emptier in the expansive training grounds.
Marcus quickly stepped in, taking charge of the training. “All right, no moping. Lucy and Laura wouldn’t want you to slack off. Today, you’ll spar with Theo.”
Theo stepped forward, a mischievous grin plastered across his face. “Time for some fun, kids. Let’s see what you’re made of.”
The sparring sessions were far less rigid under Theo’s guidance. He turned every drill into a game, making jokes and playfully teasing Rick and Monty when they missed their marks.
Nearby, Elias observed quietly, occasionally offering pointers. “Keep your balance, Rick,” he called out. “A solid stance is key to delivering a strong attack.”
Elric, on the other hand, couldn’t resist chiming in with sarcastic quips. “Or you could just trip and make them think it’s part of your plan!”
Rosa and Miriam watched from the sidelines, cheering enthusiastically whenever Rick or Monty landed a solid hit. “You’re getting better!” Rosa exclaimed, clapping her hands.
During a water break, Theo pulled the group together. “Listen up, you two. You’re doing great, but there’s something bigger coming your way. Marcus will fill you in.”

Marcus, overhearing, nodded. “You’ll be joining a martial arts academy soon. It’s a place where you’ll get access to better training, resources, and allies. But first, there’s a selection tournament.”
Rick and Monty exchanged glances, excitement and nerves bubbling inside them. “What’s the tournament like?” Rick asked.

Marcus’s expression turned serious. “It’s a test of everything—strength, strategy, and endurance. Only a hundred students will be chosen, and competition is fierce. Train hard, and you’ll have a chance.”
Elias stepped forward, placing a reassuring hand on Rick’s shoulder. “Don’t worry. With the skills you’re building here, you’ll be ready.”
“Yeah,” Elric added with a grin. “And if you’re not, just bluff your way through. Works every time!”
Everyone burst into laughter, the tension melting away.

The boys were eager to prove themselves but couldn’t help missing Lucy and Laura. Their absence left a void that even Theo’s humor couldn’t completely fill. Sensing their somber mood, Theo hatched a plan.
“You know what? Staying indoors and training all day isn’t good for you,” Theo said, clapping his hands. “Let’s go outside and meet some other kids. A bit of fresh air will do wonders.”

Though hesitant at first, Rick and Monty eventually agreed, following Theo into the bustling streets of Rover City. Rosa and Miriam joined them, excited to show the boys around, while Elias and Elric tagged along, teasing each other as always.

The group wandered through the lively town square, stopping occasionally to watch street performers and try snacks from local vendors. At one point, Theo excused himself to buy more snacks, leaving Rick and Monty to explore with Rosa and Miriam. Elias and Elric, caught up in a competitive game of darts with some older teens, were briefly distracted. While Rosa and Miriam got carried away, admiring a fancy dress sampled outside a merchants' store.
It was during this moment of separation that trouble found Rick and Monty.
A group of older kids, all smirks and sneers, approached the two boys. They had clearly heard about the newcomers.
“So, you’re the new kids” one boy said mockingly, his arms crossed. “Don’t look like much to me.”
Rick tried to stand his ground. “We’re just waiting for our friends,” he said firmly.

“Friends?” a girl in the group scoffed. “Who would wanna be friends with you two scrawny bastards? You’d be better off going back to wherever you came from.” she said as their group laughed mockingly.
"I heard they're slaves and a good mister bought them" another snapped.
"Why don't you come wash my clothes and do the dishes" he mocked.
"Ohh come on don't be rude to them!" The girl implied "I bet their parents are slaves too" she added as another ominous round of laughter eloped the group again
"Oh wait they don't have parents" another teased, bringing the laughter to an halt. "doesn't that make them bastards" he added as they all continued laughing.
Monty clenched his fists, the bullies’ words digging deep. The taunts reminded him of everything he’d lost—his family, his village, his sense of safety.
“Look at them,” another bully chimed in. “Do you even know how to throw a punch?”
Before things could escalate further, four kids stepped forward from the crowd: three girls and a boy. They looked about the same age as Rick and Monty but carried themselves with a quiet confidence.
“That’s enough,” one of the girls said sharply, her braided hair swaying as she stepped in front of Rick and Monty.
“Yeah,” another girl added, her piercing green eyes narrowing at the bullies. “Pick on someone your own size.”
The boy in the group cracked his knuckles, his tone low and menacing. “Unless you’re looking for trouble.”
The third girl, her demeanor calm but firm, crossed her arms. “Leave them alone. Now.”
The bullies hesitated, clearly outmatched. After a few tense moments, they retreated, muttering under their breath.
Rick and Monty stared at their unexpected saviors in awe. “Thank you,” Monty said quietly, his voice shaky.
“No need to thank us,” the braided girl replied with a smile. “Just watch your back around here. Not everyone is friendly.”
Before Rick and Monty could ask their names, the four kids disappeared into the crowd, leaving the boys to process what had just happened.
Theo arrived moments later, holding a bag of snacks. He froze when he saw Rick and Monty’s shaken expressions. “What happened?” he demanded, his usual carefree tone replaced with concern.
Rosa and Miriam rushed over, having just noticed the commotion. “We’re so sorry!” Rosa exclaimed. “We should’ve been paying more attention.”
Rick quickly explained what had happened, including how the four kids had come to their rescue.
“Four kids, huh?” Theo said thoughtfully, rubbing his chin. “Sounds like you made some new allies.”
“They didn’t even tell us their names,” Monty said, a hint of sadness in his voice.
Theo grinned. “Don’t worry. If they helped you once, I’m sure you’ll see them again.”
Elias and Elric returned soon after, having heard bits of the story from other bystanders. “Figures trouble would find you two,” Elric said, though his teasing lacked its usual edge.
Elias placed a reassuring hand on Monty’s shoulder. “You handled it well. Next time, just remember—you’re not alone."

The group spent the rest of the afternoon playing games and sharing stories, trying to lift Rick and Monty’s spirits. Though the boys laughed and joined in, the bullies’ words lingered, casting a shadow over their day.
As the sun began to set, the group headed back to the mansion. Rick and Monty walked in silence, their thoughts heavy.

That night, lying in their beds, the boys reflected on everything that had happened. The kindness of the four strangers and the unwavering support of Theo and the others shone brightly against the backdrop of their doubts and fears.
The spark of hope that had built up in them was once again reignited—and a determination to prove themselves worthy of the trust others had placed in them.

chapters.label: Chapter 15
chapters.title: Shadows of War.
chapters.summary: Lucy and Laura arrive at the imperial palace to help the kingdom prepare for a possible war with Marador after enemy forces gather near the border. However, they soon discover that a faction within Marador is secretly pushing for war despite the king’s desire for peace. A mysterious woman named Selene, who once survived because of their fallen brother Ethan, provides evidence of the conspiracy. With the threat becoming clearer, Lucy and Laura prepare to expose the plot and prevent a devastating war while Marcus returns home to continue guiding Rick and Monty.
paragraphs: The grand halls of the imperial palace were a sight to behold. Sunlight streamed through stained glass windows, casting colorful patterns on the marble floors. The towering arches and intricate carvings spoke of a kingdom steeped in history and power. Yet, the air was heavy with tension as Lucy and Laura strode through the palace corridors, their faces set in grim determination.

The sisters had been summoned in haste, their presence requested by the royal council to aid in a crisis threatening the fragile peace between kingdoms. As they entered the council chamber, a wave of voices greeted them—nobles, generals, and advisors were deep in debate.

“Ah, Generals Lucy and Laura,” a commanding voice interrupted the clamor. King Alaric, seated at the head of the table, gestured for silence. His piercing blue eyes surveyed the room, his expression a mix of weariness and resolve.
“Your Majesty,” Lucy and Laura said in unison, bowing deeply.

“We have much to discuss,” the king began, his voice steady. “Our spies report that the Kingdom of Marador is amassing troops along our borders. They claim it’s a defensive measure, but we suspect otherwise. Your expertise is needed to prepare for what may come.”
Laura stepped forward, her tone measured. “Do we have any intelligence on their movements or intentions, Your Majesty?”
A middle-aged general, clad in ornate armor, answered. “Their forces have been spotted near the Strahl Pass—a strategic point. If they control it, they’ll have a direct route to our capital.”

Murmurs filled the room, but Lucy silenced them with a raised hand. “If they take Strahl Pass, it will be catastrophic. We need to fortify it immediately and deploy scouts to gather more information.”
The king nodded. “Exactly what I was hoping you’d say. Generals, I’m assigning you to oversee this operation. You’ll have full authority to organize the defenses and rally troops as needed.”
“We won’t let you down,” Lucy assured, her voice resolute.

As the council continued deliberating, Lucy and Laura listened intently, offering strategic insights where necessary. Laura’s sharp mind dissected the logistical challenges, while Lucy’s tactical expertise provided actionable plans. Their synergy was unmatched, earning the respect of even the most seasoned generals in the room.

After the meeting, Lucy and Laura were led to their temporary quarters to prepare for their mission. On their way, they passed a small garden within the palace walls. The soft rustling of leaves caught Laura’s attention, and she paused.
“Do you hear that?” she asked, her voice low.
Lucy nodded, her hand instinctively moving to the hilt of her sword. The sisters stepped cautiously into the garden, their senses on high alert.
In the shadows, a figure emerged—a young woman in a hooded cloak, her features obscured. “Generals,” she said softly, her voice carrying a sense of urgency.
“Who are you?” Lucy demanded, her eyes narrowing.
The woman pulled back her hood, revealing striking green eyes and a scar that ran across her cheek. “My name is Selene. I bring a message from within Marador.”
Laura exchanged a quick glance with Lucy. “Speak.”

Selene hesitated, her gaze darting around the garden. “Marador’s king doesn’t want war, but his council is divided. A faction within his court is pushing for conflict, seeking to expand their territory and power. If they succeed, the war will be inevitable.”
“And why should we trust you?” Lucy asked, her voice cold but curious.
Selene’s expression hardened. “Because I owe my life to someone who believed in peace—your brother, General Ethan.”
The mention of Ethan, their fallen brother, sent a shockwave through Lucy and Laura. They hadn’t heard his name in years.
“You knew Ethan?” Laura asked, her voice softer now.
Selene nodded. “He saved me during the Battle of Eldwyn, risking his life for someone he didn’t even know. I vowed to honor his sacrifice by preventing more needless bloodshed. That’s why I’m here.”
Lucy studied Selene for a long moment before sheathing her sword. “If what you say is true, then you’ll need to prove it. Do you have evidence of this faction’s plans?”
“I do,” Selene said, reaching into her cloak to produce a sealed envelope. “This contains the names of those involved and their strategy. Use it wisely.”
Laura took the envelope, her mind racing. “If this information is accurate, it could change everything. But if it’s a trap—”
“It’s not,” Selene interrupted firmly. “I’ll stay within the palace if you need more from me. But please, act quickly. Time is running out.”
The sisters watched as Selene disappeared into the shadows, her parting words lingering in the air.
Preparing for the Mission

Back in their quarters, Lucy and Laura poured over the documents. The names listed confirmed their worst fears—key figures within Marador were indeed plotting war, using the king as a puppet to mask their true intentions.
“This changes everything,” Lucy said, her voice heavy with the weight of responsibility. “We need to present this to the king and adjust our strategy.”
Laura nodded. “But we must tread carefully. If the Marador king is a pawn, exposing him could backfire and push them further into war.”
Their conversation was interrupted by a knock at the door. Marcus entered, his expression serious.
“I heard about the situation,” he said. “Do you need reinforcements?”
Lucy smiled faintly. “No, Marcus. You’re needed back home. The kids still have much to learn, and they’ll need your guidance in our absence.”
Marcus hesitated, clearly wanting to stay, but he nodded. “Understood. Just don’t take too long, or Theo might turn the training into a circus.”
The sisters laughed, the tension easing for a moment.

As Marcus left, Lucy and Laura returned to their planning, their determination unshaken. They knew the road ahead would be fraught with danger, but they also knew they had to succeed—for the kingdom, for the kids, and for the memory of their brother.

chapters.label: Chapter 16
chapters.title: The Turning Point.
chapters.summary: Lucy and Laura successfully prevent war between Rover and Marador by exposing the conspiracy within Marador’s royal court and helping establish a new alliance between the kingdoms. Meanwhile, back at the mansion, Monty struggles with his training and begins to doubt himself compared to Rick. Marcus helps him understand that true strength comes from perseverance and believing in his own abilities. With Marcus’s guidance, Monty makes his first major breakthrough in combat, regaining his confidence and realizing that he can become strong in his own way.
paragraphs: The tension within the war room was palpable as Lucy and Laura presented the documents Selene had delivered. King Alaric studied the parchment with a furrowed brow, his expression a mixture of disbelief and anger.
“So, it’s true,” he muttered. “Marador’s king is being manipulated by his own council.”
“We need to act now, Your Majesty,” Laura said firmly. “If we can expose this faction to the Marador king and offer him a way out, we can avoid unnecessary bloodshed.”
The king nodded, his decision swift. “You have my full support. Take a small envoy with you. If diplomacy fails…” He paused, his voice heavy. “We’ll prepare for war.”

Lucy, Laura, and a handpicked team of trusted soldiers set out for Marador under the cover of darkness. Selene accompanied them, her knowledge of Marador’s court proving invaluable as they navigated through enemy territory.
When they reached the gates of Marador’s capital, they were met with hostility. Armed guards blocked their path, demanding their business.
Laura stepped forward, her voice steady but commanding. “We are envoys of King Alaric Alden of Rover Kingdom. We seek an audience with King Imai to discuss matters of utmost urgency.”
After tense deliberation, the guards relented, escorting them to the royal court. The Maradorian king, a wiry man with a tired expression, regarded them warily from his throne.
“State your purpose,” he said, his tone cold.
Lucy didn’t waste time. “Your Majesty, we’ve come to expose a conspiracy within your court—one that aims to use you as a pawn to wage an unjust war.”
Gasps echoed through the hall as Lucy handed over the documents. The king read them in silence, his hands trembling as he uncovered the betrayal.
“This cannot be…” he whispered, his voice barely audible.
Selene stepped forward. “Your Majesty, I’ve seen their plans firsthand. They seek to undermine your rule and seize power for themselves. You must act now to root them out.”
The king’s eyes burned with fury as he summoned his guards. “Bring me the council members named in these documents. They will answer for their treachery!”
By dawn, the conspirators had been arrested, their schemes laid bare before the court. The Maradorian king, now free from their influence, turned to Lucy and Laura.
“I owe you a debt I can never repay,” he said, his voice filled with gratitude. “Your actions have not only saved my kingdom but have also prevented a war that would have cost countless lives.”
Lucy inclined her head. “Peace is the only debt we seek, Your Majesty. Let this be the start of a new alliance between our kingdoms.”
The king smiled faintly. “An alliance it shall be. You have my word.”
With the treaty signed and peace restored, Lucy and Laura returned home as heroes. The kingdom erupted in celebration, but the sisters couldn’t shake the weight of the past weeks.
“We did what we had to,” Laura said as they watched the fireworks light up the night sky.
Lucy nodded. “But now it’s time to look to the future.”
Back At The Mansion.

The training sessions had grown increasingly demanding. Each day tested Rick and Monty’s resolve, pushing them to their physical and mental limits. While Rick thrived on the challenge, his determination blazing like a fire, Monty often found himself struggling to keep up.
On this particular day, the sun beat down mercilessly over the courtyard as Lucy led the group through a grueling series of drills.
“Again!” she barked, pacing the rows of sparring dummies. “Precision is everything. Strength without control is just wasted energy.”
Rick struck his target with focused determination, sweat dripping from his brow. Monty, however, swung wide, his wooden staff missing the dummy entirely. He stumbled, his frustration mounting.
Lucy sighed, placing her hands on her hips. “Monty, you’re too tense. Relax your grip and let the movement flow.”
Monty gritted his teeth, trying to mimic Rick’s fluid movements, but the more he tried, the clumsier he became. Finally, he threw down the staff. “This is pointless!” he snapped.
The group fell silent, the tension thick in the air. Laura stepped forward, her voice calm but firm. “It’s not pointless, Monty. Every warrior faces this. Even Rick struggled at first.”
Rick opened his mouth to protest but closed it quickly, catching Laura’s pointed look.
Monty shook his head. “I’m not a warrior. I’m just... me. Rick’s the fighter. I’m just slowing everyone down.”
Before anyone could respond, Marcus appeared at the edge of the courtyard, his towering figure casting a long shadow. “Monty,” he called, his voice steady. “Walk with me.”
Monty followed Marcus reluctantly, his shoulders slumped. They walked in silence until they reached a quiet corner of the estate, where the hum of training faded into the distance.
“Do you know what makes a warrior?” Marcus asked, breaking the silence.
“Strength?” Monty guessed, echoing the answer he’d given before.

Marcus shook his head, a small smile playing on his lips. “Not just strength. It’s about perseverance—the ability to keep going when everything inside you says to stop. Do you think Rick is strong because he never fails? No. He’s strong because he doesn’t let failure stop him.”
Monty looked away, his gaze fixed on the ground. “But I’m not like Rick. I don’t have his focus or his... talent.”
Marcus crouched down, meeting Monty’s eyes. “You don’t need to be like Rick. You need to be you. Strength comes in many forms, Monty. The question is, are you willing to find yours?”
Monty hesitated, then nodded slowly. “I think so.”
“That’s all I need to hear,” Marcus said, clapping a hand on his shoulder. “Now, let’s get back. I have something to show you.”
Back in the training area, Marcus gathered the group. He stepped into the sparring ring, gesturing for Monty to join him.
“Today,” Marcus announced, “we’re going to focus on finding Monty’s strength. Watch closely.”
He handed Monty a wooden staff, then took one himself. “Attack me,” Marcus instructed.
Monty’s eyes widened. “What? But I—”
“No excuses,” Marcus interrupted. “Just try.”
Swallowing his nerves, Monty swung the staff. Marcus parried effortlessly, guiding Monty’s movements with gentle corrections.
“Too much force,” Marcus said. “Focus on precision.”
“Better, but your stance is too wide. Adjust your footing.”

As the session continued, something shifted. With each correction, Monty’s movements became more confident, his strikes more precise. By the end, he was holding his own, even landing a few hits against Marcus’s defense.
When they finished, the group erupted into applause.
“You see?” Marcus said, smiling. “You’ve got what it takes. You just needed to believe it.”
Monty grinned, his confidence restored. For the first time, he felt like he truly belonged.
That evening, as they sat around the dining table, Monty turned to Rick.
“Thanks for not giving up on me,” he said quietly.
Rick grinned. “You kidding? I knew you had it in you all along.”
Lucy raised her glass. “To Monty’s first breakthrough,” she declared.
“To Monty!” the group echoed, their voices ringing with camaraderie.

As Monty basked in the warmth of their support, he realized something important. Strength wasn’t about being perfect or fearless—it was about showing up, trying, and finding the courage to keep going.
And in that moment, Monty knew he was ready for whatever challenges lay ahead.

chapters.label: Chapter 17
chapters.title: A Chance for Monty.
chapters.summary: Monty learns that he is too young to participate in the upcoming Selection Tournament for the Martial Arts Academy. Refusing to let his age discourage him, he trains harder and impresses Master Grahn with his skill, determination, and perseverance. After reconsidering the rules, Grahn grants Monty special permission to compete. With the entire group supporting him, Monty prepares alongside Rick for the tournament that could change their futures.
paragraphs: The sun dipped low in the sky, painting the training grounds in hues of gold and orange. Marcus stood before the group, his arms crossed, his expression as solemn as ever. The children, though weary from the day’s drills, were eager to hear his announcement.
“I’ve just received word from the kingdom,” Marcus began, his voice steady. “The Selection Tournament will take place the day after the next full moon at the Kingdom’s Stadium in Rowe, the capital.”

Excited murmurs rippled through the group. The tournament was more than just an event; it was an opportunity for those with talent and determination to join the prestigious Martial Arts Academy—a gateway to honor and greatness.

“But there’s a rule you all need to know,” Marcus continued, his tone sharpening. “Only children aged ten and above are permitted to participate. That means…” His eyes flicked to Monty, who stood a little apart from the group, clutching his wooden staff. “Monty, you’re not eligible.”
A heavy silence followed. Monty’s face fell, and though he tried to hide it, the disappointment was evident in his posture.
“But Marcus,” Rick protested, stepping forward. “Monty’s been training just as hard as the rest of us. He’s ready!”

“Rules are rules,” Marcus replied firmly. “And I don’t have the authority to change them. But that doesn’t mean Monty’s training has been for nothing. I expect you to train just as hard, Monty. Prove to yourself and everyone else that you belong.”
Monty nodded, though his heart felt heavy. “I understand,” he said quietly.

The next day, Monty threw himself into training with a renewed intensity. Every swing of his staff, every step in his drills, carried the weight of his determination. Lucy and Laura, watching from the sidelines, couldn’t help but admire his spirit.
“He’s got the heart of a warrior,” Laura murmured.
Lucy nodded. “But will that be enough to convince the officials?”

Two days later, an unexpected visitor arrived at the training grounds. Master Grahn, a senior official of the Selection Tournament, was conducting inspections of the participants across the kingdom. His stern demeanor and piercing gaze made even the bravest among the group nervous.

As Grahn observed the training session, his eyes lingered on Monty, who was sparring with Rick. Despite the difference in their sizes, Monty’s movements were precise, his strikes calculated. When Rick lunged, Monty sidestepped and countered with a swift blow that knocked Rick’s staff out of his hands.
Impressed, Grahn stepped forward. “You’re skilled,” he said, addressing Monty. “But you’re too young to compete.”
Monty straightened, meeting Grahn’s gaze. “With all due respect, sir, age doesn’t determine skill. I’ve trained just as hard as everyone else, and I’m ready to prove myself.”
Grahn raised an eyebrow, intrigued by Monty’s confidence. “We’ll see about that,” he said, turning to Lucy and Laura. “I’ll consider his inclusion, but I make no promises.”
That evening, the group gathered around Monty, offering their support. Rick gave him a friendly nudge. “You were incredible out there today. If anyone can change Grahn’s mind, it’s you.”
Laura placed a reassuring hand on Monty’s shoulder. “No matter what happens, remember this: you’ve already proven yourself to us.”
Monty smiled, his spirits lifted by their encouragement.

Two days later, Grahn returned with his verdict. Standing before the group, he addressed Monty directly. “After careful consideration, I’ve decided to allow you to participate in the Selection Tournament. Your skill and determination have earned you this opportunity.”
Cheers erupted from the group as Monty’s face lit up with a mixture of relief and joy. He turned to Marcus, who gave him a rare smile.
“Don’t let us down, Monty,” Marcus said simply.
“I won’t,” Monty promised, his voice steady.
With the tournament looming, the group trained harder than ever. Each day brought new challenges, but they faced them together, their bond growing stronger with every passing hour.

On the eve of the next full moon, as the group gathered for a final meal before their journey to Rowe, Lucy raised her glass. “To the Selection Tournament—and to Monty, who’s shown us all what it means to persevere.”
“To Monty!” the group echoed, their voices ringing with pride and camaraderie.
As they laughed and shared stories, the weight of the coming tournament hung in the air. It was a moment of calm before the storm, and the kids knew that their lives were about to change forever.

chapters.label: Chapter 18
chapters.title: The Road to Rowe - The Selection Tournament.
chapters.summary: Rick, Monty, and the others travel to Rowe for the Selection Tournament, but their journey is interrupted by a dangerous attack from a group of Kahngorls. Marcus reveals his overwhelming strength by effortlessly defeating the beasts and their powerful leader. Upon reaching Rowe, Rick and Monty reunite with Kara, Shirley, Whitney, and Edmond before the Grand Selection Tournament officially begins. The rules and tournament structure are announced, and Rick and Monty discover that they have been placed in Group 10, marking the true beginning of their journey toward the Martial Arts Academy.
paragraphs: The morning sun bathed the sky in shades of gold and rose as the caravan set off toward Rowe City. The air buzzed with excitement, for this journey marked the beginning of the prestigious Selection Tournament. For many of the children and their families, this was the opportunity of a lifetime—a chance to join the Kingdom’s renowned martial arts academy. While excitement hummed in the air, an underlying tension lingered, the kind that always accompanied the unknown.

Marcus lounged lazily in one of the wagons, his eyes shut in feigned indifference. Meanwhile, Lucy, Laura, Elric, Elias, Theo, and the other children marched alongside the travelers, chatting animatedly about the tournament.
“Do you think we’ll really get to see the academy?” Monty asked, his eyes sparkling with wonder.
“Of course,” Rick replied, grinning ear to ear. “They say the academy’s training grounds are the largest in the kingdom. Imagine sparring there!”
Laura chuckled, her lips curling into a smirk. “Don’t get ahead of yourselves. First, you need to survive the tournament.”
Their banter was interrupted as the caravan entered the dense Eroth Forest, a path notorious for its lurking predators. They had barely advanced when a guttural roar echoed through the trees.
Lucy, walking beside the caravan, remained alert, her hand resting on the hilt of her sword, ready for action.
“Elric,” she called, her voice steady. “Make sure everyone stays in formation. This forest is dangerous.”
Elric nodded and turned to relay the orders. “Stick close! No straying!”
Theo, ever curious, glanced around nervously. “What kind of dangers are we talking about?”
“Kahngorls,” Lucy replied, her tone grim. “Vicious magical beasts. Imagine a gorilla, but with armored skin and claws that can shred steel.”
Monty frowned. “How do you kill one?”
“By imbuing your weapon with magical energy,” Elias explained. “But even then, you’ll need precision and skill. Kahngorls aren’t just strong—they’re smart.”
“I heard getting hit by one is like being struck by a boulder the size of a wagon,” Theo added, his voice tinged with fear despite the attempt at humor.
Rick gulped audibly. “And we’re just walking into their territory?”
“It’s the fastest route to Rowe,” Elias said matter-of-factly. “Besides, we’re prepared.”
The group continued, the chatter subdued, tension thickening in the air. The only sounds were the rustling of leaves and the distant calls of birds.
Lucy and Laura exchanged a glance, noticing the kids’ visible fear. The other travelers’ children were equally shaken. Everyone, that is, except Marcus, who remained lazily napping in the wagon.
Suddenly, a guttural roar shattered the silence. The caravan screeched to a halt, and panic spread through the travelers.
“Stay calm!” Lucy shouted, drawing her sword. “Everyone, take defensive positions!”
From the shadows, the Kahngorls emerged—massive, hulking forms with glowing red eyes and armored hides that shimmered in the dappled sunlight.
Rick moved swiftly, drawing his twin daggers. “Stay behind me, Monty!” he called out.
Monty nodded, though his hands trembled as he gripped his blade.

The beasts were relentless, attacking with razor-sharp claws and a ferocity that even the seasoned fighters struggled to counter. Elric and Elias fought side by side, fending off two beasts at once. Rosa and Miriam defended a group of travelers, while Theo provided cover with his bow. Lucy and Laura moved with practiced precision, cutting down any beast that ventured too close.
But the beasts began to overwhelm them.
Amidst the chaos, Marcus stirred in the wagon, his eyes fluttering open. He stretched lazily, yawning as the clash of swords and the cries of battle filled the air.
Stepping out of the wagon, he surveyed the scene with a raised eyebrow. The group was locked in a desperate struggle, their movements showing determination despite their exhaustion.
“Eh, they’ve got it covered,” Marcus muttered, leaning casually against the wagon.
Lucy, spotting him, gritted her teeth. “Aren’t you going to quit gawking and help us, Marcus?!” she yelled, slashing at a beast.
Marcus scratched the back of his neck, feigning indifference. “It’s just a few Kahngorls. Thought you guys could handle them.”

As he surveyed the battle, he noticed a massive beast—a king among the others—watching from the shadows, issuing guttural orders to its underlings. Marcus’s demeanor shifted slightly. Drawing his sword, he began walking toward the leader but paused, seeing the group and the other travelers struggling to hold their ground.
The children were visibly exhausted, their movements slowing. Even Lucy and Laura showed signs of strain.
Marcus sighed. “Guess I’ve got no choice.”
The moment Marcus entered the fray, the atmosphere shifted. His presence was overwhelming, an aura of sheer power that sent shivers down the spines of everyone present—beasts and humans alike.

With fluid, precise movements, he dispatched the beasts one by one. His sword glowed with magical energy, and each swing left devastation in its wake. The group paused, momentarily awestruck by his display of strength.
“How strong has he become?” Lucy muttered to herself.
Laura, wiping blood from her cheek, thought, His battle aura has changed... It’s even more intense than before. Has he broken through to the Immortal Realm?
Marcus made quick work of the beasts, his sword flashing like lightning.
"...Incredible," Rick whispered, his voice tinged with awe.
“Guess it’s your turn,” Marcus said, pointing his sword at the king of the Kahngorls.

Seeing its underlings slaughtered, the beast let out a deafening roar and lunged forward, releasing a surge of magical energy toward the caravan. Marcus dashed forward to intercept, deflecting the blast with a swift motion of his sword. The redirected energy carved a path of destruction through the forest.
“Even beasts like playing dirty, huh?” Marcus muttered, charging at the creature.
The king of the Kahngorls roared again in fury and lunged at Marcus. With a single, decisive strike, Marcus sidestepped and drove his blade deep into the beast’s heart.
The battlefield fell silent, save for the ragged breathing of the group and the travelers.
“That man is a monster,” one traveler whispered. “He overwhelmed the leader with such ease.”
“We were struggling with the beasts just moments ago, but he wasn’t even fazed by them,” another murmured.
“Who is he?” asked another. “How can someone possess such power?”
“I heard a rumor he’s Sir Marcus of the Imperial Army!” a merchant piped up. “The army flourished under his command.”
“Yeah? I heard he retired eight years ago,” someone else speculated.
“That’s the power of a retired general,” another remarked in awe.
Marcus sheathed his sword with a casual flick. “Next time, try not to let things get this messy,” he said nonchalantly, sneering at Lucy.
Lucy opened her mouth to retort but thought better of it. She sighed and muttered, “You’re insufferable.”

As the dust settled, the travelers began to tend to the wounded. The air, once thick with tension, was now heavy with the scent of blood and sweat. Some were nursing cuts and bruises, while others had deeper injuries that needed immediate attention. Elric, Miriam, and other healers swiftly moved through the caravan, administering first aid where they could. Elias assisted, helping with bandages and ensuring that the worst of the injuries would be manageable until they could reach Rowe.
Theo and Rick, still catching their breath from the battle, helped gather herbs and water for the injured. Rick’s face was pale, his usual bravado shaken by the intensity of the fight.
"Stay strong," Theo encouraged, handing a vial of healing elixir to a wounded traveler. "We’re almost through this."

Though the battle was over, it was clear that the toll had been heavy on some of the travelers. Several were too injured to continue on their own, and those who were unhurt had stepped up to help them.

“Here, let me help,” Laura said, kneeling beside a wounded child, her hands glowing with soft magical energy. She healed the child’s shallow cuts and bruises, making sure they were well enough to walk again.

Lucy stood nearby, keeping an eye on the situation, her sword resting at her side. She spoke with the other leaders of the caravan, making sure everyone had what they needed. It was clear that despite the victory, the fight had left its mark.

Monty, still shaky from his near encounter with one of the beasts, stood with Marcus. His voice barely above a whisper, he asked, “How did you do that, Marcus? The way you handled those Kahngorls… it was like you were unstoppable.”
Marcus gave him a nonchalant shrug, though a slight smirk tugged at the corner of his lips. “It’s all in the training. But, hey, you did alright yourself,” he added, nodding toward Monty’s sword.

After a moment of quiet contemplation, Marcus looked out over the group, watching the wounded being tended to. His expression shifted, something more serious in his eyes than the carefree demeanor he usually wore. “This was a close one,” he muttered under his breath.
“Do you think there will be more?” Rick asked, stepping up beside him.
Marcus tilted his head slightly, considering the question. “I hope not. But with the amount of activity around here, it’s hard to say.”

The caravan slowly began to regain its composure. The wounded were tended to, and the group started moving again, though at a slower pace. The earlier tension lingered in the air, but there was a sense of relief, too. The beasts had been defeated, and they had survived.

As the group prepared to continue, a few of the travelers turned to Marcus with gratitude. One of the merchants who had been in the thick of the battle stepped forward, clutching his hand to his chest. “You’ve saved us, Sir Marcus. Truly, you’re a hero.”
Marcus waved him off with a lazy grin. “I’m no hero. Just doing what I can to make sure you all don’t get yourselves killed.”

The mood lightened, and even the children couldn’t help but look at Marcus with awe, their earlier fear and uncertainty melting away. They had witnessed firsthand the power of a true warrior—one who had their back, even when things looked darkest.

As the caravan finally continued its journey through the Eroth Forest, the kids walked in silence, still processing the battle and the sheer strength Marcus had displayed. Rick’s mind raced with thoughts of the tournament ahead, but his gaze often drifted to Marcus, the man who had just proven that even in the face of overwhelming odds, true power could be wielded effortlessly.
The sun was beginning to dip lower in the sky, casting long shadows over the forest as they pressed forward. The path to Rowe was still long, but now, it felt a little less daunting.

The caravan finally reached Rowe City, its towering gates a welcome sight after the harrowing journey. The capital was a marvel of architecture and life, with bustling streets and soaring spires that seemed to touch the heavens.
In the distance, the Kingdom’s Stadium loomed—magnificent, exuding both power and prestige.
As they entered the city, the kids couldn’t help but marvel at their surroundings. For them, having never visited Rowe City before, the sights were almost overwhelming.
“This place is incredible,” Rick whispered, his eyes wide with wonder.
Marcus, however, remained cautious. “Rowe may be beautiful, but don’t let your guard down. It’s as dangerous as it is grand,” he warned.
“Is Rowe City really that bad?” Rick asked nonchalantly.
“It’s bad,” Rosa answered with a sigh. “Though the bustling activities cover it most of the time, the nobles of Rowe City are known for trampling on the weak and poor.”
“Keep up, guys!” Laura called with excitement. “The stadium is just ahead!”
At the stadium, they spotted familiar faces—the four kids who had stood up for them back in Rover City.
“Look who’s here!” Edmond grinned at Rick and Monty, waving.
“Hello!” Rick said, a bright smile spreading across his face.
“It’s nice to meet you here!” One of the girls greeted them. “I’m Kara!” she introduced herself, pulling her sister forward.
“I’m Shirley,” she said shyly.
“I’m Whitney,” the third girl said, her face alight with energy.
“And I’m Edmond,” he added. “What are your names?”
“I’m Rick,” Rick replied. “And this is my friend Monty,” he added, with Monty waving shyly. “Nice to meet you all.”
“Are you guys here for the tournament too?” Kara asked eagerly.
“Yes!” Rick exclaimed.
“We hope to be selected among those chosen for one of the martial arts academies,” Monty added.
“Great!” Shirley chimed in. “We’re here for the tournament too,” she said, her shyness fading as she warmed up to them.

“Hmmm...” Edmond muttered, leaning in and studying them closely. “You guys look different. Must have been doing a lot of training, huh?” he remarked brightly. “I can tell you’re definitely a lot stronger than when we first met.”
“Just a little training,” Rick replied sarcastically, scratching the back of his neck. “Maybe a little too much?” he added, and they all burst into laughter.
As they chatted, Theo and the others approached, their expressions composed yet intrigued. They hadn’t seen Rick and Monty so cheerful with others before.
“Looks like you’ve made some new friends,” Theo said as he walked over, draping an arm across Rick’s shoulders. “You’re the ones who saved my brothers back in Rover City, right?”
“Come on, Theo,” Rosa interrupted, rolling her eyes. “That’s not how you thank people!” she exclaimed.
“Please pardon Theo’s personality,” Elias said dryly. “His humor always gets ahead of him.”

“That’s not how to do it either, Elias,” Miriam snapped, before turning to the group with a smile. “Thank you all for standing up for Ricky and Monty that day. We didn’t notice what was happening, but we appreciate it. Who knows what could have happened otherwise?”
“You’re welcome!” Kara and Whitney chorused in unison.
“We just can’t stand bullies,” Edmond added.
“You boys sure have a lot of grown-ups looking out for you,” Shirley remarked with a smirk.
“We do—except for Theo, of course!” Rick shot back with a wicked grin, teasing Theo. The two of them began bantering playfully.
“Well, we’ll be off now,” Kara said as Theo and Rick continued their banter.
“Just so you know,” Edmond said, leaning toward Rick with a friendly smirk, “I won’t be holding back if we face off in the tournament.”
Rick raised an eyebrow, unsure of Edmond’s seriousness. “Oh, alright!” he exclaimed with a smile. “Bring it on!”
“See ya!” Monty added.

As they walked away, Rick and Monty felt a growing sense of happiness and ease, a connection with the kids that was both comforting and exciting. They noticed, however, that Laura, Lucy, and Marcus were nowhere to be seen.
“Where are the others?” Monty asked curiously.
“Oh, they’re VIPs,” Elric explained. “They had to go meet the king and other nobles.”
“Will they be able to watch the tournament?” Rick asked.
“Of course they will!” Theo interjected. “They’ll be sitting next to the king tomorrow, watching everyone.”
“Oh, alright,” Rick replied, as they wandered into the crowd.

That night, they stayed in a modest inn near the stadium. Sleep was elusive, each member of the group consumed by thoughts of the tournament. Before retreating to his room, Marcus gave them one last piece of advice: “The tournament isn’t just about strength, boys. Keep your wits sharp.”
His words seemed to lift their spirits, and they drifted off to sleep, the weight of the upcoming challenge sinking in.
The next morning, the stadium was alive with energy. The stands were packed with spectators, their cheers echoing through the air. The colosseum was filled with excitement, the atmosphere electric.

Among the audience were nobles seated in ornate booths, their luxurious attire gleaming in the morning light. In the royal section, the king sat, flanked by his advisors and prominent knights, and royal emissaries from other kingdoms. The leaders of the five Martial Arts Academies were also present, seated in an elevated booth. Their expressions were stern but filled with curiosity as they observed the participants.

Lucy, Laura, and Marcus were seated near the royal entourage. Despite her stoic demeanor, Lucy occasionally glanced at the arena, her eyes betraying her concern for the kids. Laura, on the other hand, watched intently, her lips curved into a small smile of anticipation.
“I hope they remember their training,” Laura said softly.
“They’ll be fine,” Marcus replied nonchalantly, leaning back in his seat. “If they don’t crumble under the pressure, that is.”
“Welcome, citizens and participants, to the Grand Selection Tournament!” the prime minister’s voice rang out, amplified by magic to reach every corner of the massive arena.

“On behalf of His Majesty, King Alaric, I welcome you all to Rowe,” he continued. “The Selection Tournament stands as a testament to the strength and unity of our kingdom.” He paused, scanning the crowd.
“Here, young warriors will rise, alliances will form, and the future of our realm will be shaped,” he added, gesturing to a man standing beside him in ceremonial robes.

“Allow me to introduce Lord Adrian, who will oversee this year’s grand event. Under his watchful eye, your journey to greatness begins.” He paused and glanced at the participants. “May the bravest and most cunning among you triumph!”
Lord Adrian stepped forward, his piercing gaze sweeping across the sea of eager faces. The air was thick with anticipation as he raised his hand, commanding silence.

“The rules of this tournament are simple but unyielding,” Adrian began, his voice calm yet firm. “First and foremost, under no circumstances shall any participant take the life of another. This is the sacred law of the tournament. Any violation will result in immediate expulsion and severe consequences.”

He paused, letting the weight of his words settle in before continuing. “Additionally, any act of violence that leaves an opponent beyond recovery—unable to heal or continue life normally—will be treated as an equivalent offense to killing. Such actions undermine the purpose of this tournament and will not be tolerated. Fight with honor, not cruelty.”
He allowed a moment of silence before speaking again. “Beyond this, all other tactics, skills, and strategies are permitted. Consider everything else fair game.”
Adrian shifted his tone, now explaining the structure of the competition.

“The tournament will unfold in stages. The first round will divide participants into groups of ten. Within these groups, you will compete until the strongest emerge. Once we reach 120 participants, the format will shift to one-on-one duels. These duels will test your strength, skill, and resilience to their limits.”

He gestured toward the Academy leaders seated in an elevated gallery. “At that stage, the leaders of the Martial Arts Academies will handpick an additional 50 participants who demonstrate exceptional promise. These individuals will join the top 50 from the duels to form the final 100.”

His expression grew more somber. “With this, the tournament will officially conclude. The chosen 100 will carry the honor of representing our future and ascend to greater heights of training and purpose. Fight with dignity, give it your all, and remember—this tournament is not just a test of strength, but of character.”
A roar of approval erupted from the crowd, and the participants exchanged glances, a mixture of determination and nervous excitement painted on their faces.

Rick clenched his fists, his heart pounding with a mix of anticipation and nerves. Beside him, Monty exhaled deeply. “Group of ten, huh? Let’s hope we don’t get matched with the monsters in the crowd.”Moments later, the participants were ushered to a large board displaying the group assignments. Rick quickly scanned the list, his eyes landing on his name: Group 10. He turned to Monty, who grinned and nudged him.
“Looks like we’re in the same group,” Monty said, his grin widening.
Rick allowed a small smile to tug at his lips. “Good. At least I know I’ve got one ally.”
The two boys turned their attention back to the stage, their minds racing with thoughts of the challenges ahead. For better or worse, their journey through the tournament had begun.
Marcus, leaning against a wall, scanned the arena with a smirk. “This is where the real fun begins,” he murmured.
Rick and Monty exchanged nervous glances, their excitement tempered by the weight of what lay ahead.

chapters.label: Chapter 19
chapters.title: Into the Illusionary Ruin.
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty enter the tournament’s first major challenge: a dangerous illusionary ruin where teamwork, strategy, and adaptability are tested. Despite being the only magicless members of their team, they prove their worth through courage, observation, and quick thinking. After overcoming bridges, puzzles, a powerful stone golem, and a shifting labyrinth, their team successfully advances to the next round alongside 24 other teams.
paragraphs: The stadium buzzed with ecstasy and anticipation as Lord Adrian stepped forward, his rich voice silencing the murmuring crowd.

“This year’s tournament will test not only your strength and intellect but your ability to work as a team. Each group will enter an illusionary ruin—a realm created by the kingdom’s most skilled mages. There, you will face challenges designed to test your resolve, strategy, and cooperation. Only 25 teams will proceed to the next round, while the remaining five will be disqualified. Injuries in the illusion will feel real, so tread carefully.”
