He gestured toward the towering magical constructs spread around the stadium: 30 glowing magic screens hovering in midair. Each screen displayed a different perspective of the ruins, ready to follow each team’s journey. The crowd erupted in excitement, cheering for their favored contestants.
Rick scanned the audience, his heart pounding as he noticed the sheer size of the crowd. Nobles, merchants, and common folk alike leaned forward in their seats, their eyes glued to the screens.
Monty nudged him. “Everyone’s watching. Don’t freak out.”
Rick grinned nervously. “I’ll try.”

Lord Adrian raised his hand, signaling the robed mages stationed along the stadium’s perimeter. With a unified chant, the mages summoned a wave of radiant energy that spread across the participants. In a flash of light, the ground beneath Rick vanished, and his team was transported to the illusionary realm.
The Illusionary Ruin

Rick blinked as the light faded, revealing their new surroundings. They stood in the middle of an ancient ruin, its crumbling walls stretching toward a darkened sky. The air smelled of damp stone and moss, and the faint sound of distant howls sent chills down Rick’s spine.
“Everyone here?” Lila’s sharp voice cut through the silence.

Rick turned to see the rest of their team: Lila, their group leader who has a quick mind and sharper tongue; Monty, the youngest at just 9 years old, with boundless enthusiasm and a sharp eye for detail; Rick, two years older but equally determined; two 11-year-olds who were twins with complementary magic; Brock, a towering presence with earth magic to match; Zara, a healer who rarely spoke but always observed; and three others, all over 12 and well into their magical training.
Everyone except Rick and Monty had awakened their magic.
“Looks like the two magic-less kids survived the teleport,” one of the older boys muttered with a smirk.
“Enough,” Lila said, her voice cold. “Magic or no magic, we’re a team. If you can’t work together, this illusion will eat you alive.”
Monty grinned, unfazed by the jab. “Don’t worry about us. We’ll pull our weight.”
Rick nodded. “We may not have magic, but we’re not useless.”
“Prove it,” Brock said, his voice a low rumble. “The illusion isn’t going to wait for us to argue.”
Back in the Stadium
The crowd leaned forward as the magic screens came to life, each one assigned to a team. Gasps and murmurs rippled through the audience as the illusionary ruins unfolded in vivid detail.
“That’s my boy!” a woman cried, pointing at one of the screens.
“Look at the magic users in Group 6,” another voice said, awestruck. “They’ll sweep the whole thing!”

At the royal box, nobles debated the strengths of the contestants. “That boy, Monty,” a baroness mused. “He shouldn’t even be here, technically. But he earned his spot, didn’t he? The determination in his eyes is something special.”
“His team will carry him,” another noble scoffed. “Look at Group 10—two magic-less children? They’re doomed.”
King Alaric sat silently, his piercing gaze fixed on Rick and Monty’s team. Beside him, the prime minister murmured, “This year will be one to remember, Your Majesty.”
The First Challenge

The ruins wasted no time in testing the teams. The first obstacle appeared in the form of a massive chasm, its depths shrouded in darkness. Rick’s group approached cautiously, noting the narrow, crumbling bridges spanning the gap.
“We’ll need to stabilize the bridge,” Lila said, assessing the situation. “Zara, use your wind magic to steady it. Brock, anchor it with your earth magic. Everyone else, cross one at a time.”
As the group worked together, Rick noticed another team on a nearby bridge. Their leader waved his hand, and a shimmering barrier appeared beneath their feet, allowing them to cross effortlessly.
“Magic makes everything look easy,” Monty muttered.
“Focus,” Rick said, steadying the bridge for Lila. “We’re doing fine.”
By the time they crossed, Rick’s arms burned from holding the rope in place, but the team remained intact.
Deeper into the ruins, the team encountered a massive stone door etched with glowing runes.
“It’s a puzzle,” Lila said, studying the symbols. “Give me a minute to figure it out.”
While she worked, the others kept watch. Nearby, another team used magic to bypass a similar door, their leader conjuring a spectral key to unlock it instantly.
“They’re not playing fair,” Monty grumbled.
“They’re using what they have,” Brock said, his tone neutral. “And so are we. Let’s not waste time complaining.”
“Got it!” Lila exclaimed as the door creaked open. Beyond it lay a sprawling courtyard filled with illusionary beasts.
The ground trembled as an enormous stone golem rose from the earth, its red eyes glowing with malice.
“Take it down!” Lila shouted.
The magic users sprang into action, their spells lighting up the courtyard. Brock’s earth magic slowed the golem’s movements, while Zara shielded the team with a protective barrier.
Rick and Monty darted around the battlefield, distracting the creature with quick, precise movements.
Nearby, another group used fire and lightning magic to bring down a similar golem in seconds. The contrast was stark, but Rick refused to feel discouraged.
“Keep moving!” he shouted, dodging a swipe from the golem’s massive arm.
After a grueling fight, their golem crumbled into dust, and the team pressed on.
The last challenge was a labyrinth of shifting walls, each turn more disorienting than the last.
“This is impossible,” one of the twins said, frustrated. “The walls keep moving!”
“Watch the ground,” Rick said, pointing to faint glowing marks. “They’re showing the pattern. Follow them.”
Guided by Rick’s observation, the team navigated the labyrinth, avoiding dead ends and traps. Finally, they emerged through a glowing archway, just as the ruins began to collapse around them.
The illusion shattered, and the team reappeared in the stadium to thunderous applause. The announcer’s voice boomed over the crowd.
“The first round is complete! Congratulations to the 25 teams moving forward!”
Rick and Monty exchanged relieved smiles, but the exhaustion in their eyes was clear.
“We made it,” Monty said, clapping Rick on the shoulder.
“Yeah,” Rick replied, his gaze drifting toward the other teams—especially the magic users who had breezed through the challenges. “But this was just the beginning.”

chapters.label: Chapter 20
chapters.title: The Second Trial.
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty face the tournament’s second trial, a dangerous climb across unstable cliffs and shifting platforms where teamwork, resilience, and adaptability are tested. Despite losing teammates along the way, the boys rely on their training, sharp instincts, and determination to help their team reach the summit. Their team finishes among the 20 groups that qualify, earning praise from Marcus, Lucy, Laura, and the others. As they prepare for the third trial, Rick and Monty realize that the tournament is becoming increasingly difficult—but they are determined to keep fighting together.
paragraphs: The sun hung high over the arena as Lord Adrian ascended the stage once again. The murmurs of the crowd hushed as his commanding voice echoed across the stadium.

“Congratulations to the 25 teams who survived the first trial. Your next test will push you even further, demanding not just teamwork, but resilience, strategy, and adaptability. This trial will take place in a terrain of ever-changing danger—a realm of unstable cliffs, shifting platforms, and unpredictable natural hazards.”
A collective gasp rippled through the audience. The magic screens showed glimpses of the new terrain: towering rock formations, treacherous ravines, and dense mist swirling over gaping chasms.

Lord Adrian continued, “The objective is simple: reach the summit of the central plateau as a team. Only the first 20 teams to reach the top will qualify for the next round. But beware—the challenges you face will be unlike any before. Injuries will not follow you back, but serious harm or a fall from the cliffs will disqualify you instantly. Losing teammates will not stop a team from qualifying, but the journey will grow harder with every loss.”

Rick glanced at his team. Monty stood at his side, his small frame practically vibrating with excitement and nerves. The older teammates exchanged uneasy glances, and even Lila’s confidence seemed shaken.
“We stick together,” she said firmly. “No one gets left behind. If we lose people, we lose our edge.”
“Easy for you to say,” muttered one of the older boys. “You’ve got magic. Rick and Monty are the weak links here.”
Monty opened his mouth to retort, but Rick grabbed his arm, shaking his head. “Ignore it. Let’s just focus.”
Before anyone could respond, the mages began their chant. The ground shimmered, and with a blinding flash of light, the 25 teams vanished.
The Shifting Terrain

When the light faded, Rick found himself standing on a narrow ledge, the ground below lost to a swirling abyss. Jagged cliffs loomed ahead, and shifting stone platforms hovered over deep ravines. The faint sound of wind whistled through the air, and the terrain rumbled ominously.
“Move!” Lila barked, pulling the team into action.

The group scrambled across the first stretch of rocky ground, narrowly avoiding a section that crumbled beneath their feet. Brock used his earth magic to stabilize a collapsing path, while Zara’s wind magic pushed away a falling boulder that threatened to crush them.
Rick and Monty took the rear, their sharp eyes scanning for hazards. Without magic, they relied on quick reflexes and instinct to navigate the treacherous terrain.
As they approached a series of hovering platforms, Lila motioned for the group to stop. “We’ll need to jump. Zara, can you create a wind current to help?”
“On it,” Zara said, her hands glowing as she conjured a steady breeze.
One by one, the team leapt across, aided by the magic. Rick hesitated, his stomach churning as he stared into the void below.
“You got this,” Monty said, giving him a firm shove forward.
Rick gritted his teeth and jumped, landing hard on the next platform. Monty followed with a whoop of triumph.
Ahead of them, chaos erupted as another team encountered a collapsing bridge. Screams echoed as two members plunged into the abyss, their bodies vanishing as the magic disqualified them.
Rick’s heart clenched. “They’re okay, right?”
“They’re fine,” Lila said without looking back. “Keep moving.”
“But they’re out of the tournament,” Monty said grimly.

The group pressed on, but the losses weren’t confined to other teams. During a harrowing climb up a crumbling cliff, one of Rick’s teammates, a twin with fire magic, misjudged his footing. A falling boulder struck his shoulder, sending him tumbling into the mist.
“Lila!” Rick shouted.
“I saw,” she said, her voice tight. “Keep moving.”
Back in the Stadium
The crowd was on edge as the screens showed team after team suffering losses. Gasps and cheers erupted with every close call and narrow escape.
Marcus, watching intently muttered to himself "You boys are doing better than I anticipated"
Lucy on the other hand said brightly "They sure didn't forget their training" she chimed "I'm proud!".

"We're good teachers!" Laura interjected "I must say I'm pretty surprised though,...I haven't seen kids this determined before" she added, "you've got real good eyes Marcus" Laura thought out loud, Marcus smiled at both of them.
At the royal box, King Alaric leaned forward in his seat, his sharp gaze fixed on Rick and Monty’s team.
“They’re holding their own,” the prime minister observed. “But without magic, those two will be hard-pressed to survive much longer.”
“They’ve made it this far,” Alaric replied. “Perhaps they’ll surprise us yet.”
Meanwhile on another side of the stadium, Theo and the others were thrilled and excited.
"They're nailing it!" Theo yelled.
"As expected of them" Elias replied.
"Even without magic the boys aren't fazed at all" Elric said "they're truly remarkable I must say" he muttered.
"I'll cook them more scrumptious and delicious meals for sure!" Rosa chimed brightly.
"Their training has definitely paid off" Miriam implied "but they still got a long way to go" she added.
Reaching the Summit
By the time Rick’s team neared the central plateau, their numbers had dwindled to seven. Exhausted but determined, they scaled the final cliff, their muscles burning with effort.
At the summit, they collapsed onto the ground, gasping for air. Around them, other teams were arriving, some with their full complement of members, others reduced to half their original size.
A booming voice filled the air as the mages’ spell ended, returning the participants to the stadium.

“The second trial is complete!” Lord Adrian announced. “Congratulations to the 20 teams who have advanced. You have proven your strength and resilience, but the road ahead will only grow more challenging.”

As the sun dipped below the horizon, Lord Adrian spoke again. “That will be all for today. The tournament will resume tomorrow with the third trial. Rest well, for the challenges ahead will demand all of your strength and courage.”
With that, the crowd began to disperse, and the participants were led to their quarters to recover.
Rick and Monty barely had time to process their relief before a familiar voice called out.
“Rick! Monty!”

They turned to see Theo running toward them, the others following behind their faces lit with relief and joy. Rosa, Miriam, Lucy, and Laura followed closely behind, with Marcus bringing up the rear, his steady presence as calming as ever.
“You guys did it!” Theo shouted, pulling Monty into a bear hug.
“Barely,” Monty said with a laugh, though his voice trembled with emotion.
Rick felt an arm around his shoulders and turned to see Marcus. The man’s sharp eyes softened as he gave Rick a firm squeeze. “You did good, kid. I knew you would.”
“Thanks,” Rick said quietly, his throat tight.
Miriam and Rosa peppered them with questions, while Lucy and Laura bombarded them with insights of how they could have failed it they had slacked off on their training.
Elias clapped Rick on the back, grinning. “You’re both tougher than you look. Not bad for a couple of ex-slaves.”
Rick stiffened, but the warm humor in Elias’s tone made him relax. They were no longer strangers—they're family now.
Rick and Monty sat on the edge of their cots, the day’s events replaying in their minds.
“We’re still here,” Monty said softly.
“Yeah,” Rick replied. “And we’ve got them.”
“Tomorrow?”
Rick nodded. “Tomorrow.”
For now, they allowed themselves a moment of peace—together, and still in the fight.

chapters.label: Chapter 21
chapters.title: The Final Group Trial.
chapters.summary: Rick, Monty, and the remaining teams face their most dangerous group trial yet—a deadly crossing over a chasm of fire and lava filled with swinging weapons and collapsing paths. Using their agility, teamwork, and determination, Rick and Monty help their team survive, though their group is reduced from ten members to just four. With only 148 participants remaining, they advance to the individual stage of the tournament, knowing the real competition is about to begin.
paragraphs: The morning sun bathed the arena in golden light as the 20 remaining teams stood in anticipation. The atmosphere was thick with tension, and even the audience seemed subdued, their excitement tempered by the weight of what was to come. The massive screens displayed the participants’ solemn faces, their exhaustion from the previous trials evident.

Lord Adrian ascended the stage, his expression as unyielding as ever. "Welcome to the final group trial," he began, his voice ringing across the stadium. "You have proven your strength and courage, but this test will determine not just your resilience, but your adaptability, decisiveness, and willingness to endure. Only 150 participants will advance beyond this round. Survive the trial, or face disqualification."

A murmur swept through the audience, and the screens flickered to reveal the new trial: a nightmarish chasm of fire and lava. Illusionary weapons dangled over the abyss, their glinting edges promising pain and danger. The only way forward was a narrow, cracked path that barely seemed wide enough for a single person. The oppressive heat shimmered in the air, and faint sparks rose from the chasm like malevolent fireflies.

“The rules are simple,” Lord Adrian continued. “You must cross the path within the time limit. Those who fall into the chasm will be disqualified. When time runs out, the bridge will collapse, and anyone still on it will face the same fate. Choose your steps wisely, for hesitation may cost you everything."

Gasps echoed through the stadium as the screen focused on the boiling lava below. Even those with water magic were visibly uncomfortable, beads of sweat forming on their brows despite their calm demeanor.
"Begin!" Lord Adrian commanded.
The Trial Begins

The air shimmered as the mages activated their spell, and with a flash, the participants found themselves in the illusionary realm. The heat hit Rick like a wall, the searing air drying his throat and soaking his shirt in seconds. The chasm yawned before them, and the dangling weapons swayed ominously as if daring them to proceed.
Lila, their leader, scanned the path. “We move as a unit. Stay focused, don’t panic, and trust your instincts. Rick, Monty—your agility will be key here. Lead us through.”
Rick nodded, glancing at Monty, who gave a small, nervous grin. “Guess we’re the stars of the show now,” Monty muttered.

The group stepped onto the path, the heat radiating from the chasm below making every step feel heavier. The walls on either side cracked ominously, and chunks of stone occasionally broke free, plunging into the fire below.

The first obstacle was a series of swaying platforms, each one narrower than the last. Illusionary weapons swung across the path at unpredictable intervals, forcing participants to time their movements with precision.

“Go!” Lila barked as the group leapt onto the first platform. Rick and Monty led the way, their light frames and quick reflexes making them ideal for the treacherous task. Monty ducked under a swinging axe, his foot skimming the edge of the platform as he landed. Rick twisted to avoid a spiked mace, his pulse pounding in his ears.

Behind them, Brock used his earth magic to stabilize the platforms temporarily, allowing Lila to cross safely. But the team wasn’t unscathed—one of their members misjudged a jump and was struck by a swinging blade. With a cry, he toppled into the abyss, his figure vanishing into the flames. Another miscalculated her jump before lunging, she landed on an unbalanced brick that slipped the instant she stood on it, sending her falling into the chasm of fire and lava with screams.
“Keep moving!” Lila shouted, her voice cutting through the panic.

Halfway across, the path narrowed even further, forcing the group to move single file. The heat was unbearable now, even for those using magic. Rick’s shirt clung to his back, and his hands were slick with sweat as he gripped the unstable rock.
Monty slipped but caught himself at the last second, his breath coming in shallow gasps. “I hate this! I hate this so much!” he yelled.
“You’re doing fine!” Rick called back. “Just keep going!”
The time limit loomed over them like a shadow. Rick could hear the faint sound of gears grinding—a warning that the bridge’s collapse was imminent. They were running out of time.

The last stretch of the path was a series of crumbling stones, each one sinking into the lava moments after being stepped on. The group broke into a sprint, desperation driving them forward. Brock shouted, using his magic to create footholds where the stones had already fallen, but even his power was faltering under the intense heat.

Monty was the first to leap onto solid ground, collapsing in a heap as Rick followed close behind. Lila and Brock arrived moments later, just as the bridge gave a final, shuddering groan and collapsed into the flames.
The four of them lay on the ground, gasping for air. Around them, other teams were arriving, their numbers visibly reduced. The once-strong group of ten had been cut to four.
Back in the Stadium

The illusion faded, and the participants found themselves back in the stadium. Cheers and gasps erupted from the audience as the final count was revealed: only 148 participants remained, scattered across the 20 teams. Some teams had been reduced to just two or three members, their losses evident in their weary faces.
The royal box was abuzz with conversation.
“A brutal trial,” King Alaric remarked, his eyes scanning the survivors. “But necessary. Only the strong will prevail.”
Theo and the others were on their feet, cheering wildly for Rick and Monty.
“They did it again!” Theo shouted.
“Barely,” Elias said, though his grin betrayed his pride. “Those two are something else.”
Rosa wiped a tear from her eye. “I knew they could do it,” she said softly.
Back on the field, Rick and Monty stood shoulder to shoulder, their breaths still labored. Rick glanced at his group, their leader and Brock both nodding in silent approval.
“We made it,” Monty whispered, his voice trembling with exhaustion and relief.
Rick nodded. “Yeah. But it’s not over yet.”
Monty managed a weak grin. “We’ve got this.”

As the sun dipped lower in the sky, the crowd’s cheers echoed across the arena, a testament to the resilience of those who remained. The final group trial had ended, but the tournament was far from over.

chapters.label: Chapter 22
chapters.title: The Final Round Approaches.
chapters.summary:
With only 148 participants remaining, the tournament enters its final and most decisive stage: one-on-one duels. Only 50 participants will qualify through the matches, while the academy leaders will personally select another 50.

Rick and Monty face renewed doubt and mockery from other contestants for being magic-less, but their friends, former teammates, and mentors remind them of how far they have come. Rick discovers that his opponent is Erynn, a formidable golden-sashed fighter, setting up a difficult 25th match.

As the participants prepare for the following day's duels, Rick and Monty receive encouragement from everyone at the inn, especially Marcus, who believes their unique achievements may earn them a place in an academy regardless of their final ranking. With the tournament now at its most critical point, the boys settle in for a restless night, determined to give everything they have.
paragraphs: The tension in the arena was palpable as Lord Adrian stepped forward once more. His voice echoed through the massive stadium, silencing the murmurs of the crowd and participants alike.

"Congratulations to the 148 of you who remain. You have proven your resilience, strength, and teamwork. However, the final round will be different. This is the one-on-one duel—a true test of individual skill and determination. Only 50 of you will qualify to join the martial arts academies. Additionally, the academy leaders will handpick another 50 based on their discretion, bringing the total to 100."

He paused, letting the weight of his words sink in. "Let me remind you of the rules: no killing. Beating or wounding an opponent beyond recovery, even with magic, is strictly forbidden. Violators will face severe punishment. This is a test of your abilities, not a stage for cruelty."
The participants nodded solemnly, their faces a mix of determination and apprehension. Lord Adrian gestured toward the stadium exit, where staff members awaited.
"Proceed to the next floor. There, you will find the list of your dueling opponents. Good luck."

The participants shuffled out of the arena and onto the next floor. In the center of the spacious hall stood a large board, glowing faintly with enchanted light. A meticulously drawn chart filled the board, listing participants’ names and their corresponding dueling opponents in neat columns and rows.
Excitement and nerves filled the air as participants crowded around the board, scanning the chart to find their matchups. Some pointed eagerly, while others exchanged worried glances.
Rick and Monty approached the board, only to hear familiar voices calling their names. Turning, they saw Edmond approaching, grinning broadly as he pulled them into a quick embrace.
"You guys made it! I knew you would!"

Their reunion was filled with laughter and relief. Kara and the other girls joined them, their smiles wide as they congratulated one another. However, the moment of joy was interrupted by sneering voices.
"Look at them," one participant muttered, loud enough for others to hear. "No magic, and they still made it. Their team must’ve carried them the whole way."
Another scoffed. "I hope I get matched with one of them. It'll be an easy win."
Rick and Monty stiffened but said nothing. The whispers became bolder, some participants openly pointing and laughing. One of them, a tall figure with a golden sash, sneered.
"Enjoy your moment while it lasts. Once you're up against real fighters, you'll crumble."
Kara placed a hand on Monty’s shoulder, her voice calm and reassuring.
"Don’t let them get to you. Even losing is a chance to learn and improve. You’ve already come so far."
Whitney and Shirley chimed in, nodding in agreement. "You’ve earned your place here. No one can take that away from you."
Edmond stepped forward, his sharp gaze silencing the crowd.

"Remember what I said?" he told Rick and Monty, his voice steady. "If we’re matched against each other, I won’t go easy on you. Don’t expect special treatment from me." He gave them a small smirk before walking away with his friends.
Despite the simple words, they struck a chord with Rick and Monty, reigniting their determination.
Lila and Brock, their former teammates, approached them next. Lila crossed her arms, a proud smile on her face.
"If it weren’t for you two, we wouldn’t have made it past the first trial. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise."
Brock nodded. "You two were the backbone of our group. Don’t let anyone undermine what you’ve achieved."
Their words lifted Rick and Monty’s spirits, banishing the doubts planted by their detractors. Together, the group approached the board to see who they would be dueling.

Rick scanned the chart for his name, his heart pounding. When he finally found it, his breath caught. His opponent was Erynn—one of the golden-sashed participants. He had seen Erynn in action during the team trials, and her precision and speed had been nothing short of terrifying, and they're set at the 25th match.
Monty, standing beside him, let out a low whistle. "Looks like they’re not pulling punches for the final round."

Once all the participants had seen the chart, they were escorted back to the arena. The crowd erupted into cheers as the matchups were displayed on massive screens. The names of participants were illuminated, sparking excitement and speculation among the spectators.
Lord Adrian stood once more, addressing the crowd and participants.
"Rest well for the remainder of the day," he announced. "Tomorrow, the final round begins. Show us your strength, your skill, and your resolve. May the best among you prevail."
The participants were dismissed to their quarters, the tension palpable as they prepared for the challenges ahead.

Back to the inn, Rick and Monty gathered with their friends. Elias and Elric were seated near the fireplace, quietly discussing strategies. Rosa and Miriam brought a plate of food to the table, reminding everyone to eat and conserve their strength.
Lucy and Laura sat nearby, their expressions calm but focused. Lucy, ever the optimist, smiled warmly.
"You’ve got this, Rick and Monty. Just remember, it’s not about winning or losing—it’s about giving it your all."
Theo, leaning against the wall, gave a small grin. "And if you win, you’ll have one heck of a story to tell."
Finally, Marcus, the ever-supportive friend, clapped Rick on the back. "No matter what happens, we’re all proud of you. Just do your best."

He added, "Besides, I have high hopes for you two. Even if you don't make the top 50, the academy leaders would be foolish and blind not to pick you two. You’ve come this far without magic, and that alone makes you stand out."
Their words filled the room with a sense of camaraderie, strengthening the bond between them. Despite the challenges ahead, they knew they had each other’s backs.
As the night wore on, Rick and Monty lay awake in their beds, the weight of the tournament pressing on their minds.
"Tomorrow’s going to be tough," Monty whispered.
Rick nodded, staring at the ceiling. "Yeah. But we’ll have to face it one way or another."
With that, they closed their eyes, determined to give everything they had in the final round of the tournament.

chapters.label: Chapter 23
chapters.title: The First Duel.
chapters.summary: The final round of the Selection Tournament begins with intense one-on-one battles, and Rick is immediately matched against the powerful magic user Erynn. Despite being mocked for having no magic, Rick relies on his superior reflexes, strategy, and swordsmanship to outmaneuver her and claim a surprising victory.
paragraphs: The morning sun poured through the high windows of the arena, illuminating the determined faces of the participants. The energy in the air was electric, each warrior silently preparing for the final round.
Rick sat on a bench in the preparation area, his heart racing as he adjusted the grip on his sword. Beside him, Monty sharpened his blade with deliberate focus.
"You ready for this?" Monty asked without looking up.
Rick exhaled slowly. "I don’t think anyone is truly ready for something like this. But we’ll have to be."
A steward interrupted their conversation, announcing, "Participants, follow me. The final round is about to begin."
The group of participants rose, their footsteps heavy as they walked toward the waiting room.

Lord Adrian came forward to address the crowd and participants, his presence commanding. Beside him were the academy leaders, their robes adorned with intricate symbols representing their institutions.
"Welcome to the final round!" Lord Adrian’s voice boomed. "Today, we will witness the strength and resolve of these young warriors. Let the duels commence!"
The crowd erupted in cheers as the first two names appeared on the massive screen above the arena: Erynn vs. Rick.
Rick’s heart sank. He had hoped for more time to prepare, but fate had other plans.
"Rick’s first?" Rosa exclaimed, her brows furrowed. "Against Erynn? This is unfair!"
Elric crossed his arms, his face set. "Rick can handle it. He’s smarter than most of these loudmouths give him credit for."
Miriam leaned forward. "Still, Erynn’s magic is powerful. He’ll need to be careful."
Lucy and Laura exchanged worried glances. "We believe in him," Lucy said with a small smile. "Rick has a way of surprising everyone."
Marcus, grinned. "Time to show what you're capable of kid." He muttered.
"That boy, Rick," the king said, his voice measured. "Does he really have no magic?. Is it true, Prime Minister?"
The Prime Minister, an older man with a sharp gaze, nodded. "Indeed, Your Majesty. Yet, he has made it this far. Some might call it luck, others... determination."
"I see" the king added as he shifted his attention to the participants.
The nobles seated nearby exchanged whispers.
"How absurd," one scoffed. "A non-magic user competing at this level? It’s a disgrace."
Another snorted. "He won’t last five minutes against Erynn. She’s a prodigy."
The martial arts academy leaders sat in their designated section, watching with keen interest.
"The boy’s tactics have been sound so far," one of them remarked.
"True," said another, stroking his beard. "But Erynn is leagues ahead. This might be the end of his journey."
Monty clapped him on the back. "You’ve got this. Remember what we talked about—stay calm and focus on her movements."
Rick nodded, giving Monty a small smile before turning to face Erynn.
She stood confidently across the field, her golden sash gleaming in the sunlight. Her sword shimmered with magical energy, and a faint smirk tugged at her lips.
"So, you really are the one without magic," Erynn said as they squared off. "I’ll admit, making it this far is impressive. But this is where it ends."
Rick raised his sword, his grip steady despite the nerves twisting in his gut. "We’ll see about that."
The steward raised his hand. "Begin!"
Erynn moved first, hurling a glowing sphere of energy at Rick. He dove to the side, narrowly avoiding the explosion as it scorched the ground.
In the royal box, the king leaned forward, intrigued.
"Quick reflexes," he murmured.
"That poor boy doesn’t stand a chance!" someone shouted.
"Why even bother? He’s just going to embarrass himself."
"He made it this far—maybe he’s got some tricks up his sleeve," another countered.
Below, one of the nobles laughed. "Reflexes won’t win a duel against magic."
In the crowd, Rick’s friends leaned forward, their hearts pounding.
"Come on, Rick!" Rosa shouted, her voice almost drowned out by the noise.
Erynn advanced, her blade humming with energy. Their swords clashed, and the sheer force of her magic sent Rick stumbling back.
"Is that all you’ve got?" Erynn taunted.
Rick gritted his teeth. "Not even close."
He sidestepped her next strike, his sword arcing toward her exposed side. She blocked it with a flick of her wrist, her movements fluid and precise.
In the academy section, one of the leaders nodded appreciatively.
"He’s reading her moves well."
"But for how long?" another replied. "Without magic, he’s at a severe disadvantage."
Erynn summoned a wall of fire, cutting off Rick’s retreat. The audience gasped, and some began to laugh.
"He’s finished now!" someone yelled.
Rick’s friends weren’t convinced.
"Don’t underestimate him!" Elric snapped at a nearby spectator. "Rick always finds a way."
Miriam clasped her hands together, whispering, "Stay calm, Rick. You can do this."
Rick eyed the flames, his mind racing. As Erynn lunged, he feigned a stumble, leaving his left side exposed. She took the bait, her blade aimed for his chest.
At the last moment, Rick twisted his body, deflecting her strike and disarming her in one fluid motion. The crowd erupted in shock as her sword clattered to the ground.
"You’ve got to be kidding me!" a noble exclaimed.
Erynn scrambled back, summoning a burst of magical shards that hurtled toward Rick. He deflected most with his sword, though one grazed his arm, drawing blood.
In the crowd, Lucy gasped. "He’s hurt!"
Laura shook her head. "It’s just a scratch. He’s still in this."

Rick pressed the attack, closing the distance between them. Their blades clashed again, but this time, he forced her onto the defensive. With a final, well-timed strike, he knocked her sword from her hand and leveled his blade at her chest.
Erynn hesitated, her breathing ragged. Slowly, she raised her hands in surrender.
The steward stepped forward, raising his hand. "Winner: Rick!"
The arena exploded into cheers and disbelief.
"He actually won!" Theo shouted, pumping his fist in the air.
"That’s my Rick!" Rosa yelled, her grin stretching ear to ear.
In the royal box, the king smiled faintly. "A most unexpected victory. What do you think, Prime Minister?"
The Prime Minister chuckled. "He may lack magic, but his skill is undeniable. A true underdog, Your Majesty."
Erynn approached Rick, her expression a mix of frustration and respect. "I underestimated you. Well fought."
Rick nodded, his exhaustion evident. "Thanks. You’re tough."
As Rick walked back to the preparation area, Monty met him with a broad grin. "You did it! I knew you would!"
Rick managed a tired smile. "One down. Who knows how many to go."
Despite the challenges ahead, Rick allowed himself a moment of pride. He had proven that even without magic, he could stand among the best.

Next up was Edmond, a tall and stoic participant from the southern provinces, known for his incredible speed. His opponent, Ralmar, was a burly fighter with brute strength and a hammer that glowed faintly with magical runes.
The crowd buzzed with anticipation as the two squared off.
Ralmar twirled his hammer, sneering. "You’ll be flat on the ground in seconds, kid."
Edmond didn’t respond, his calm demeanor unshaken. The steward’s signal came, and the fight began.
Ralmar charged forward, swinging his hammer with devastating force. Edmond dodged with inhuman speed, weaving around the arena like a shadow.
"He’s fast!" someone in the crowd shouted.

Ralmar roared in frustration, summoning a wave of energy that cracked the ground. Edmond leaped high into the air, his sword gleaming as he brought it down in a swift arc, disarming Ralmar in one clean strike.
The crowd erupted into cheers.
"That boy’s got some skill," one of the academy leaders said, impressed.
Ralmar glared at Edmond as he accepted defeat, muttering, "You’re better than I thought."
The third duel paired Brock, a towering participant with a broad build and a reputation for overwhelming strength, against Seria, a nimble girl with razor-sharp daggers and an arsenal of wind magic.
Seria smirked as they entered the arena. "You might be big, but size doesn’t mean everything."
Brock shrugged, displaying a swift stance with his spear. "We’ll see."
The steward raised his hand. "Begin!"
When the duel began, Seria darted around Brock, her daggers flashing as she unleashed a barrage of wind blades. Brock batted them away with his spear, his movements deceptively fast for his size.
"She’s quick, but he’s smarter than he looks," Elric observed from the crowd.

As Seria attempted a flanking maneuver, Brock anticipated her movement, he stabbed the ground with his spear, unleashing shockwaves. The shockwave disrupted her balance, giving him the opening he needed to disarm her.
The audience cheered as Brock extended a hand to help Seria up. "Good fight," he said.
She took his hand, smiling. "You’re better than you look, big guy."
Lila, a petite but fiery fighter with flame magic, faced Durwin, a stoic warrior with a long spear and impenetrable defenses.
"Let’s make this quick," Lila said, fire sparking at her fingertips.
Durwin twirled his spear, his face unreadable. "Quick it shall be."
As the fight began, Lila launched fireballs in rapid succession, forcing Durwin to rely on his spear’s enchanted barrier. The crowd gasped as the arena lit up with flames.
"Her magic is impressive," Rosa said, her eyes wide.
"But can she get through his defense?" Miriam wondered aloud.

Durwin advanced steadily, deflecting each attack with precision. Lila gritted her teeth, switching tactics. She feigned an overhead fire strike, then ducked low, sweeping his legs with a burst of flame.
Caught off guard, Durwin fell, and Lila pressed her advantage, disarming him with a triumphant grin.
"Winner: Lila!" the steward announced.
The next round was Freya, a dual-wielding swordswoman, and Galvin, a staff-wielding mage.
Their fight was an intense display of skill, with Freya’s aggressive strikes countered by Galvin’s defensive spells. The crowd watched in awe as sparks and flashes filled the arena.
"These two are evenly matched," one of the nobles commented.
In a surprising twist, Freya used her swords to reflect Galvin’s own spell back at him, disorienting him just long enough to land the winning blow.
The audience erupted into applause as Freya stood victorious, helping Galvin to his feet.

As the day progressed, the duels continued. The arena, once buzzing with excitement, seemed to grow more tense as participants fell one by one. Finally, the screen above flickered, displaying the next matchup: Monty vs. Callan.
Rick, now seated with Rosa, Elric, and the others, leaned forward. “This is it. Monty’s turn.”
Monty stepped into the arena with a confident stride. Across from him stood Callan, a wiry boy with bright red hair and a cocky smirk. In his hand was a staff crackling with lightning magic.
“Another swordsman without magic?” Callan sneered, twirling his staff. “This will be over in seconds.”
Monty tightened his grip on his blade, his expression calm but focused. “We’ll see about that.”
The steward raised his hand. “Begin!”
Callan didn’t waste a second, slamming the butt of his staff into the ground. A wave of lightning surged toward Monty, tearing across the stone floor.
Monty sidestepped just in time, the electricity grazing his boots. Without hesitation, he charged forward, his blade gleaming in the sunlight.
Callan spun his staff, creating a shield of crackling energy to block Monty’s strike. Sparks flew as sword met magic, forcing Monty to leap back.
“You’re quick,” Callan said, his smirk widening. “But you can’t get past this.”
Callan raised his staff, summoning a storm of electricity that arced toward Monty. The crowd gasped as the bolts struck the ground, creating small explosions.
Monty kept moving, his footwork precise as he dodged the onslaught. He closed the distance again, feinting a high slash before spinning low, aiming for Callan’s legs.
The staff came down just in time, blocking the strike. Callan retaliated with a burst of lightning from his free hand, forcing Monty to retreat.
“Impressive,” one of the academy leaders murmured from the stands. “He’s holding his own against a powerful magic user.”
“But for how long?” another replied. “Callan’s magic will wear him down eventually.”
Back in the arena, Monty’s breathing grew heavier, but his eyes remained sharp. He noticed the way Callan’s movements grew slower after each powerful spell.
“He’s burning through his energy,” Monty muttered to himself.
Callan raised his staff for another attack, but this time, Monty was ready. He dashed forward, faster than Callan anticipated, and deflected the lightning with the flat of his blade.
The crowd erupted as Monty closed the gap. Callan tried to summon another shield, but his movements were too sluggish. Monty knocked the staff from his hands and leveled his blade at Callan’s throat.
Callan froze, his chest heaving. Slowly, he raised his hands in surrender.
The steward stepped forward, raising his hand. “Winner: Monty!”
Rick and the others cheered from the stands. “That’s Monty for you!” Rosa exclaimed.
Monty wiped the sweat from his brow as he walked back to the preparation area, his grin wide. Rick met him with a clap on the shoulder. “You were amazing out there.”
Monty laughed. “Thanks. But it’s only going to get harder from here.”
As the sun began to set, the final duels concluded. The once-crowded preparation area now held only 100 participants, each one battered but determined.
Lord Adrian returned to the arena floor, his regal presence silencing the murmurs of the crowd.
“Today, you have all proven your worth,” he began, his voice carrying across the arena. “From hundreds, only 100 of you remain. You have faced fierce opponents and overcome incredible odds.”

He paused, letting his gaze sweep over the participants. “But this is only the beginning. Tomorrow, the final stage of this tournament will begin. Rest well, for the trials ahead will test not only your strength but your spirit.”
The crowd erupted into applause as Lord Adrian raised his hand, officially adjourning the tournament for the day.
Rick, Monty, and their friends gathered near the exit, their exhaustion momentarily forgotten.
“We made it,” Rosa said, her grin wide.
“For now,” Elric added. “But tomorrow is going to be even tougher.”
Rick nodded, his mind already racing with strategies. “One step at a time. We’ll be ready.”
As the participants filed out of the arena, the air buzzed with anticipation for what was to come.
Above, the king and Prime Minister observed the participants as they left.
"An impressive group," the king remarked. "The next round will be fascinating."
"Indeed," the Prime Minister agreed. "We’ll see who has the will to make it to the end."

chapters.label: Chapter 24
chapters.title: The Final Day of the Tournament.
chapters.summary: The final day of the Selection Tournament brings the remaining participants into their most decisive battles. Monty faces the powerful Garreth and, despite his determination and impressive agility, is ultimately defeated. His resilience earns the respect of both Garreth and the spectators.
paragraphs: The arena buzzed with anticipation as the final round of the tournament began. For many, this was their last chance to secure a place in the prestigious Martial Arts Academy, an institution known for producing the most elite warriors in the kingdom. The academy did not just train fighters—it shaped the future of the kingdom. To be accepted meant gaining access to advanced training, powerful mentors, and an unparalleled path to greatness.

But only 100 participants would be chosen from the hundreds who had entered. The first 50 spots would go to those who proved themselves in both combat and magical ability, while the academy leaders would handpick another 50 candidates based on potential.
For some, this tournament was merely a stepping stone. But for others, this was everything.
Failure meant returning home in defeat. For many, there would be no second chance.
Lord Adrian stepped forward, his authoritative voice silencing the murmuring crowd.

“Many of you might wonder why this final round is necessary when we already have 100 participants who meet the requirements. This is because the Martial Arts Academy only accepts those who prove themselves not only through combat but also through their potential. After this round, each participant’s magical powers will be tested, and the top 50 will be chosen. The academy leaders will then select another 50 to complete the list of those joining us. Fight with all your might, for this is your final chance to prove your worth!”

The crowd erupted into cheers as the first pair of combatants stepped into the arena. The duels were intense, each showcasing the remarkable skill and determination of the participants. Soon, the screen reflected the names of the next duel, Monty Vs. Garreth.
Monty stepped forward, his face a mixture of determination and nervous energy. His opponent, Garreth, was a towering guy with bulging muscles and a confident smirk.
“He’s huge,” Rosa muttered, worry evident in her voice.
“Take a look at him!" Theo exclaimed " Are you sure that guy isn't older than 18?" He asked, "Monty doesn’t stand a chance,” Theo said, shaking his head.
“He’ll surprise us,” Elias said, though his tone lacked conviction.
Monty cracked his knuckles and grinned, masking his nerves. “Let’s get this over with,” he said, stepping into his stance.
Garreth laughed, his voice booming. “You’re brave, little guy. But bravery won’t save you.”

The steward signaled the start of the match, and Garreth charged forward like a bull. His massive fists swung with terrifying speed, but Monty’s smaller frame allowed him to duck and dodge, moving swiftly around his opponent.
With a sudden burst of speed, Monty landed a jab to Garreth’s ribs, followed by an uppercut to his jaw. The crowd gasped in surprise.
“Did you see that?” Laura exclaimed.
“He’s gotten faster,” Lucy added, leaning forward in her seat.
Monty pressed the attack, weaving around Garreth’s massive swings and landing a series of punches that forced the larger man to step back.
“Come on, Monty!” Theo cheered from the sidelines.
Rosa clapped her hands together, her worry momentarily replaced with hope. “He’s doing it!”
But Garreth’s patience was wearing thin. With a loud roar, he caught Monty’s next punch in his massive hand, twisting his wrist and pulling him off balance.
"You tried kid" Marcus muttered to himself, though a satisfactory grin tugged at his lips.
“That’s it,” Garreth growled, lifting Monty off the ground and slamming him onto the arena floor.
The crowd winced at the impact.
“That’s gotta hurt,” one spectator muttered.
“That kid is a good fighter, but he’s obviously outmatched,” another said.
Monty groaned, struggling to get back on his feet. Garreth didn’t give him the chance, delivering a powerful kick that sent him skidding across the arena.
Blood trickled from the corner of Monty’s mouth as he pushed himself up, his body trembling. Despite the pain, he grinned.
“You hit like a kid,” Monty said, spitting blood onto the ground.
The crowd erupted into laughter, admiring his resilience.
“Monty’s got guts,” Elias said, shaking his head in disbelief.
“He’s insane,” Theo muttered, though a smile tugged at his lips.

Garreth charged again, his fists glowing with magical energy. Monty managed to dodge the first swing, landing a punch to Garreth’s side, but the larger man retaliated with a devastating blow that sent Monty sprawling.
The steward stepped forward, raising his hand to signal the end of the match.
“Garreth wins!".
The audience erupted into applause as Garreth raised his fists in victory.
Monty lay on the ground, coughing but smiling. Garreth extended a hand to help him up.
“You’ve got heart, kid,” Garreth said.
“Yeah, and bruised ribs,” Monty replied, taking his hand. “Thanks for the fight."
As Monty left the arena, he was met by the healers who healed his injuries, his friends gathered around him.
“You did great out there,” Rosa said, placing a supportive hand on his shoulder.
Monty winced but grinned. “Yeah, but next time, you guys should remind me not to pick a fight with a guy who looks like he eats bricks for breakfast.”.
The group laughed, their spirits lifted despite Monty’s loss..
With Monty’s match concluded, the attention shifted to the next duels.

High above the arena, in the royal viewing box, King Alaric of the Rover Kingdom and King Imai of Marador sat side by side, observing the matches with keen interest. Their seats offered the best vantage point in the coliseum, allowing them to take in every movement, every strike, and every moment of brilliance.
Soon the screen displayed the next duel participants, Rick Vs Edmond.

King Alaric stroked his beard thoughtfully, his gaze fixed on the combatants. “It is quite something, isn’t it, Imai? Watching these young warriors push beyond their limits. Their hunger for greatness reminds me of our own youth."

King Imai chuckled, swirling the wine in his goblet. “Indeed, Alaric. Back then, we were not so different from them—full of fire and ambition. But tell me, do you see any among them who could one day shape the future of your kingdom?”.

Alaric nodded toward the arena, where a match had just concluded. “Several, in fact. That boy, Rick, interests me greatly. His technique is refined, his resolve unshaken. Even without magic, he stands his ground against those who wield it.”

Imai leaned forward slightly, watching as Rick stepped into the arena for his match against Edmond. “Ah, I see. His movements are sharp, calculated. And his resilience… admirable. If he unlocks his magic, he may become one of the greatest warriors of this generation.”
Alaric smirked. “Or even without it. Talent like his is rare. I have no doubt he will leave a mark, one way or another.”.
They both fell silent as the duel between Rick and Edmond unfolded before them. The excitement of the crowd mirrored their own rising intrigue.
Rick stepped into the arena, his eyes locking with Edmond’s. The crowd grew silent, the anticipation heavy in the air.
“Rick, you’ve got this!” Rosa shouted, her voice breaking the tension.
"Come on Edmond!" Kara exclaimed "give him all you've got" she added.
Theo crossed his arms, a grin on his face. “Show him what you’re made of Rick!".
Edmond smirked, cracking his knuckles. “I hope you’re ready, Rick. I won’t go easy on you.”
Rick grinned back. “Good. I wouldn’t want it any other way."
The steward signaled the start of the match, and Edmond wasted no time, rushing at Rick with incredible speed. But Rick was ready, sidestepping the attack and landing a swift kick to Edmond’s side.
The crowd erupted into cheers.
“Rick’s holding his own!” Elias exclaimed, his eyes wide with surprise.
Rosa clasped her hands together, her face lighting up with hope. “He’s amazing!"

Rick pressed his advantage, landing a flurry of punches and kicks that forced Edmond to retreat. Each attack was precise, each movement fluid. The audience watched in awe as Rick demonstrated his mastery of martial arts.
“Look at him go,” one of the academy leaders murmured. “Without magic, he’s still a force to be reckoned with.”
“Impressive,” another agreed.
But Edmond wasn’t done. With a shout, he summoned vines from the ground, wrapping them around Rick’s legs. The crowd gasped as Rick struggled against the magical restraints.
“This is it for him,” someone in the audience muttered.

But Rick wasn’t giving up. He broke free from the vines with a burst of strength but the distraction was all Edmond needed, he closed the distance between them in a swift move and countered Rick with his sword.
Rick narrowly evaded the strike but Edmond followed up with a counterstrike, his fist glowing with magical energy struck Rick, sending him sprawling to the arena floor.
Slowly Rick got up, his clothes torn from the impact, the crowd began murmuring, some whispering that the fight was over.

Rick stood up slowly, his breath ragged, the murmuring of the crowd became faint to his ears, then a memory played in his mind, he remembered Marcus' words "Even without magic this technique can be devastating". Taking a deep breath, he took a stance.
Marcus, watching from the sidelines, leaned forward and muttered to himself, “The Fist of Iron.”
“Isn’t that Marcus’s technique?” Laura asked, glancing at Lucy.
“It is,” Lucy replied, her eyes fixed on the duel. “I didn’t know he’d taught it to them.”
Rick slowly raised his hands, clenching them into fists and bringing them down to his stomach level. Edmond’s eyes narrowed.
“You’re strong, Rick, and whatever you’re planning might be an ace up your sleeve,” Edmond said, advancing. “But I won’t give you the chance to use it.”

As Edmond closed the distance, Rick's fist glowed faintly, not of magical energy but raw power, he unleashed his punch, breaking through Edmond’s magical barrier and sending him sprawling to the floor.
The crowd was stunned.
“What technique was that?” one academy leader asked.
“That boy is something else,” another said in amazement.
Marcus grinned, clapping twice. “Well done, boy. You’ve mastered it already.”
Edmond staggered to his feet, stabbing the ground with his sword for support. Blood trickled from his lip, but his expression was one of admiration.
“You’re incredible, Rick,” he said. “If that punch had magic behind it, I’d be done for. But now it’s my turn.”

Before Rick could respond, Edmond moved in a blur. His fist, glowing with magical energy, slammed into Rick’s chest. The impact sent Rick flying out of the arena, landing with a heavy thud. His clothes were torn to shreds, leaving only his tattered pants.
The steward raised his hand, signaling the end of the match. “Edmond wins!”
The crowd roared in approval as Edmond approached Rick, extending a hand to help him up.
“You fought well Rick,” Edmond said as Rick clasped his hand, allowing himself to be pulled to his feet.
“Thanks,” Rick replied, wincing as he stood. “You’re not too bad yourself."
As the two left the arena the healers met them halfway and tended to their injuries, healing them almost instantly, the audience buzzed with admiration for Rick’s performance.
“That boy is talented,” one of the academy leaders said.
“If he had awakened his magic, this fight would’ve been his,” another added.
“Even without magic, he was a perfect match for Edmond,” someone else remarked.
“Impressive, isn’t he?” another exclaimed enthusiastically.
The duels continued as the day went on, soon the final duel of the tournament reflected on the screen, Kara Vs. Lila.

chapters.label: Chapter 25
chapters.title: The Final Duel and Uncertainty.
chapters.summary: Kara defeats Lila in the tournament’s final duel, bringing the intense competition to an end. The remaining participants then undergo a magical ability test, but Rick and Monty once again show no signs of magic, leaving their chances of acceptance uncertain. Despite their disappointment, their friends reassure them that their exceptional performance has already earned them recognition. Meanwhile, King Alaric strengthens diplomatic ties with King Imai of Marador as everyone awaits the academy selection results that will determine the participants’ futures.
paragraphs: The crowd roared as Kara and Lila stepped into the arena, the final duel of the tournament about to begin. Both fighters were formidable—Kara, with her quick reflexes and calculated strikes, equipped with her magic and sword, and Lila, a mage-warrior wielding magic and two daggers with deadly precision.
The steward's voice echoed across the coliseum, heightening the tension. “The final match of the tournament—Kara versus Lila! Fighters, prepare yourselves!”
Lila swirls her daggers, her stance ready. Kara, in contrast, stood calm, one hand on the hilt of her sword, and the other already crackling with magical energy.
The battle began.

Kara moved first, thrusting her palm forward. A blast of wind shot toward Lila, powerful enough to send dust and debris flying. Lila dodged, rolling to the side before dashing in, her daggers flashing.

Kara parried with her sword, sparks flying as steel met steel. She twisted her wrist, sending a pulse of magic through the blade. The force knocked Lila back, but she landed on her feet, skidding to a halt.
Lila smirked. “That all you got?”
Kara’s eyes narrowed. “Not even close.”
She lifted her free hand, summoning a series of fire orbs that hovered around her. With a flick of her wrist, the flames shot toward Lila like meteors.

Lila moved swiftly, weaving between the attacks. One fireball grazed her arm, searing through her sleeve, but she didn’t slow down. Kara threw her sword—Lila deflected it—but that was just a distraction.

In a blink, Kara closed the distance, using the moment of distraction to launch a spinning kick that sent Lila stumbling. Without missing a beat, Lila struck with one of her daggers, slicing across Kara’s shoulder before leaping back.
Kara growled, clutching her wound. “Not bad.”
Lila slammed her daggers into the ground, sending a shockwave of energy through the floor. The ground cracked beneath Kara’s feet, forcing her to retreat as jagged spikes of earth shot upward.

But Kara anticipated this. Using her agility, she leaped off one of the rising stone pillars, flipping through the air and landing behind Lila. Before Lila could react, Kara pressed the cold steel of her sword against Lila’s back.
The crowd fell silent.
Lila tensed but let out a breath. “I yield.”
The arena erupted in cheers.
The steward stepped forward. “The winner—Kara!”
Kara lowered her blade, stepping back as Lila straightened, offering a nod of respect.
“You’re strong,” Lila admitted. “Next time, I won’t hold back.”
Kara smirked. “I’ll be waiting.”.

The dust had barely settled from the final duel when the remaining participants were ushered into the magic testing chamber. The room pulsed with arcane energy, runes glowing along the walls as each contestant stepped forward to have their magic examined.
Rick and Monty exchanged uneasy glances. This was the moment they had been dreading.

One by one, contestants placed their hands upon the testing stone. Some displayed dazzling bursts of magic, while others barely managed a flicker. When Rick and Monty’s turn came, they felt nothing—no surge, no warmth, no reaction at all.
Rick clenched his jaw, stepping aside as Monty tried. The result was the same.

King Alaric himself addressed the participants. “The results will be revealed at sunrise. The top fifty will be listed, and the handpicked contestants will also be listed separately, so do well to check carefully tomorrow. Rest well, for tomorrow will shape your fate.”
As the group left the chamber, Rick and Monty trailed behind, disappointment weighing on them.
Marcus clapped Rick on the back. “You two need to stop moping. Magic or not, you made it this far. That’s already impressive.”.
Kara nodded. “Exactly. Besides, magic isn’t everything. A strong will can push you further than any spell.”
Monty smirked. “Easy for you to say. You all awakened your magic in your time, didn't you?"
Laura rolled her eyes. “Maybe we all did" she said "but what does that matter?, I'm certain you kids will be in the second list” she added.
"She's right" Marcus smirked, "You kids performed well" he added "you surprised a lot of people in the tournament, myself included, that alone has sealed your spot in the top 100".
Rick met his gaze, feeling some of the heaviness in his chest lift. He managed a small smile. “Alright.”.

Inside the palace, King Alaric stood before King Imai, his expression warm yet regal. “Your presence at the tournament was an honor,” Alaric said. “This is the first step toward strengthening the bond between our kingdoms.”
King Imai, dressed in his royal robes, gave a respectful nod. “The honor was mine. Your people’s strength is admirable, and I look forward to continued peace between our lands.”

As a gesture of goodwill, Alaric had arranged for King Imai’s departure to be grand. Several court members accompanied him back to his kingdom, along with lavish gifts—fine silks, rare spices, and enchanted artifacts crafted by the kingdom’s best mages.

As the foreign king’s carriage rolled out of the capital, Alaric watched from the palace steps, his mind already turning toward the new relationship between his kingdom and the kingdom of Marador—along with the future of the tournament’s chosen warriors.

chapters.label: Chapter 26
chapters.title: The Choice of a Lifetime.
chapters.summary: The tournament results are revealed, and while Rick and Monty miss the top 50, they are selected among the remaining 50, ranking 51st and 60th respectively. Rick is unexpectedly granted the privilege to choose his academy and chooses the mysterious Architects Martial Arts Academy, driven by his curiosity about the legendary Architects. Surprisingly, many of his strongest friends—including Edmond, Kara, Whitney, Shirley, Lila, and Brock—follow his decision and switch to the Architects Academy. With Monty and the other selected students joining them, the group begins their new journey together, united by friendship and curiosity about what awaits them.
paragraphs: The grand hall was filled with nervous murmurs as the participants gathered to check the results displayed on two massive, enchanted screens. The first screen gleamed with the names of the top 50 contestants—the ones who had secured their positions through exceptional magical prowess and performances.
Rick stood with Monty, his stomach a knot of anticipation. Kara, Lila, Edmond, Whitney, Brock, and Shirley flanked them, offering quiet words of encouragement.

One by one, the names on the first screen appeared, drawing gasps and cheers. As the names appeared, cheers erupted, Edmond ranked 2nd, Kara 3rd Whitney 9th, and Shirley 10th, securing their places among the top 10 contenders, Lila ranked 12th and Brock ranked 18th placing them in the top 20th.
Excited for their friends even though it was obvious they would be among the top rankers, Monty nudged Rick, whispering, “No chance we’ll be up there, huh?”
Rick smiled faintly but said nothing, his heart sinking as the 50th name appeared, and it wasn’t his.
Disappointed, his face down he muttered to Monty "I really don't think we will be picked"
Monty noticing his friend's downcast demeanour replied "There's still hope, let's wait for the other 50" he said "hopefully we could be listed there" he added, doubt eminent in his tone.
Noticing the boys awkward demeanor, their friends approached them.
"Come on guys" Edmond said "it isn't over yet, I know you guys will make the list" he added.
"That's easy for you to say" Rick contorted "you guys have magic" he added.

"Even without magic you two held your own to the very end" Kara interjected "no one in this tournament had touch like you both did" she added "and your hard work will certainly pay off" she said, Lila, Brock and the others knodded in agreement.

Kara's words sank in, and lifted their spirits. "Thank you Kara" Rick replied "and all of you too" he added as he turned towards them. "Even if we don't make it into the academy this year we won't give up, we'll try again until we get in" he said, his demeanor brightening up.
"That's the spirit!" Brock exclaimed.
Suddenly the second screen flickered on behind Rick, then it began to display the list of the next 50 chosen contestants.
The screen displayed 51st: Rick.
Seeing this Monty tugged at Rick's arm with excitement "Look Rick!" He exclaimed, pointing at the screen "You made it, you're ranked 51"
Rick shifted his gaze to the screen, where the next 50 names began to appear.
“51st: Rick”—the name glowed in golden letters, marking him as the highest-ranked in the secondary list.
For a moment, Rick couldn’t believe his eyes. “I—I made it!” he stammered, and cheers erupted as his friends surrounded him, congratulating him.
Monty’s name followed soon after, listed as 60th. His face lit up with a mixture of shock and joy. “We made it!” he said, punching Rick lightly on the arm.
Edmond chuckled. “See? Told you two to stop doubting yourselves.”
“You might not have awakened your magic,” Lila added, “but your determination carried you this far.”
Rick’s heart swelled with relief and pride as cheers filled the hall.
Once the names were displayed, Lord Adrian, the official overseeing the tournament, stepped forward. His voice boomed across the hall, silencing the crowd.
“Congratulations to the top 100 contestants. You have earned your place in this year’s tournament. Now, let us introduce the leaders of the five prestigious Martial Arts Academies of our kingdom.”
The crowd hushed as five figures walked into the hall, each exuding authority and power.

Lord Adrian gestured to the first leader, a tall man with a silver mane and piercing eyes. “Lord Magnus, Master of the Silver Fang Martial Arts Academy—renowned for its elite warriors and focus on strength and combat techniques.”
Magnus inclined his head, his presence radiating discipline.
The second was a serene woman draped in white robes, her movements fluid like water. “Lady Mei of the White Lotus Martial Arts Academy—specializing in agility, precision, and balance.”
The crowd murmured in awe at her graceful demeanor.
Next was a vibrant man whose golden armor seemed to glow under the hall’s light. “Lord Cedric of the Stellar Sun Martial Arts Academy—masters of versatility, endurance, and leadership in battle.”
He raised a hand in greeting, his confident smile inspiring admiration.

The fourth leader, a woman with hair as white as snow, stepped forward with an air of icy calm. “Lady Freya of the Snow Frost Martial Arts Academy—known for their control of powerful magic and resilience.” Lord Adrian introduced. Her icy demeanor sent a chill through the room as she nodded curtly.
“And lastly,” Adrian finished, “Master Zashimi of the Architects Martial Arts Academy.”

The crowd stirred as a modestly dressed man with a humble air stepped forward. Unlike the other leaders, Zashimi’s academy was widely regarded as the least prestigious, its name tied more to myth than modern accomplishments.

Lord Adrian continued to addressed the participants. “The top 50 contestants will now step forward to choose their preferred academies. As for the remaining 50, the leaders will select you based on their discretion. Choose wisely, for your decision will shape your path."

One by one, the top 50 stepped forward. Kara chose Silver Fang without hesitation, followed by Edmond, and Whitney, Brock opted for Stellar Sun.  Shirley joined the Snow Frost, and Lila chose White Lotus.
At the end most contestants flocked to the Silver Fang Martial Arts Academy and the White Lotus Martial Arts Academy. Predictably, no one from the top 50 chose the Architects Martial Arts Academy.
"Now before we proceed" Lord Adrian addressed "Rick please step forward" he said, his voice commanding.
Rick came forward from the group of people, his expression filled with uncertainty.
“Rick, by special permission from His Majesty, you are granted the right to choose an academy.” Lord Adrian implied.
Gasps filled the room.
Rick was shocked by this, feeling the weight of hundreds of eyes on him.
“Which academy will you choose?” Lord Adrian asked.
Rick hesitated, pondering intently for a while before answering. “I’d like to join the Architects Martial Arts Academy.”
A wave of murmurs swept through the hall.
“The Architects?” someone whispered.
“Why would he choose them?, isn't that a lame choice?” another muttered.
Even the leaders looked surprised. Master Zashimi tilted his head, studying Rick with keen interest, while Lord Magnus frowned in disapproval.
Master Zashimi finally spoke, his voice calm yet resonant. “Are you certain? The choice is yours, but once made, it cannot be undone unless under special circumstances.”
Rick nodded. “I’m certain.”
“Foolish boy,” someone in the crowd muttered.
Lord Cedric leaned toward Zashimi. “Master Zashimi, It seems you’ve gained an interesting one this year.”
Lord Adrian raised a hand to silence the murmurs. "Rick has chosen the Architects Martial Arts Academy. Let it be recorded.”
Master Zashimi smiled faintly. “Welcome, Kid.”

As the second group of 50 participants awaited their fate, the leaders of the academies began making their selections. Monty’s heart pounded as names were called out, but none of the prestigious academies chose him.
Finally, it was master Zashimi's turn. But the most promising talents among the participants had all been taken by the other academies, save for the 10 that were left, Monty included.
"The rest of you are welcomed to be students and disciples of the Architects Martial Arts Academy" Master Zashimi said, gesturing for them to join Rick.

As the session concluded, Lord Adrian stepped forward, facing the top 50. "Now before this is officially sealed are there any of you who wish to switch Academies?" he asked as he intently glared at the contestants "If there are any kindly do so now" he added.
Murmurs broke out as Edmond, Kara, Whitney, and Shirley all stepped forward and switched to the Architects Martial Arts Academy.
Gasps filled the room, even some of the martial arts academy leaders were annoyed by this, but they could do nothing about it, as it was their choice.
“Why are they choosing the Architects Academy?” someone whispered.
“They’re in the top 10! This is insane.”
The murmurs grew louder when Lila and Brock, also stepped forward to join the Architects.
"Are you all sure about your decisions?" Lord Adrian asked, his expression stern, the kids nodded in confirmation.

"Then it is sealed!" Lord Adrian announced "with this the selection tournament is officially closed, you all will be given a one - time student permits that you will use when going to your various academies" he said "you are to protect and keep it safely until it is used as losing it before you get into the academies will deny you entrance into them" he concluded, dismissing everyone.
As the crowd’s murmurs swirled around him, Rick took a deep breath, his heart racing. He glanced at Master Zashimi, then at his friends who had just joined him in their controversial choice.
Why did I really choose this academy?

Rick’s gaze turned thoughtful. I’ve always been curious about the creators of this world—the Architects and their immense powers. Stories of their feats, their influence, and their mysterious disappearance have always lingered in the back of my mind. It’s only right I choose to be a student of the Architects Martial Arts Academy. Joining them might shed more light on their mystery and enlighten me further about them.
Before he could dive deeper into his thoughts, a firm nudge on his arm jolted him.

“Hey,” Monty said, his face breaking into a confident grin. “Don’t overthink it. You made the right call, and besides…” He paused, giving Rick a reassuring stare. “you have us all here now and we'll deal with anything that comes our way together.”
Rick blinked, gracefully. He smiled faintly, nodding in agreement as they left the hall.

chapters.label: Chapter 27
chapters.title: Celebrations, Determination, and Words of Encouragement.
chapters.summary: Rick and Monty celebrate their admission into the Architects Martial Arts Academy with their friends and loved ones, while several of their new companions reveal the personal reasons behind choosing the same academy.
paragraphs: As the participants left the grand hall, they were greeted by a sea of waiting families and friends. The morning sun bathed the courtyard in a golden glow, and the air buzzed with excitement and joy. Everywhere, people embraced, cheered, and offered congratulatory words to the newly admitted academy students.

Rick and Monty emerged from the hall with their friends, still soaking in the weight of the moment. The group was immediately spotted by Rosa, Theo, Elric, Elias, and Miriam, who rushed toward them. Rosa wasted no time, wrapping both boys in a tight hug that managed to be both heartfelt and slightly suffocating.
“I’m so proud of you two!” she exclaimed, her voice thick with emotion. “You’ve made it, despite everything. I knew you could do it.”
Rick and Monty exchanged a grin, their spirits buoyed by Rosa’s unwavering support.

Once the initial congratulatory words had been said, Theo, who had been fidgeting with barely contained curiosity, couldn’t hold back any longer. “Alright, spill it! Which academy were you guys chosen for?” he asked eagerly, his eyes darting between the two.
Monty glanced at Rick before answering with a confident tone, “The Architects Academy.”
Theo’s reaction was immediate and dramatic. “What?!” he exclaimed, his voice rising an octave. “Of all the academies? The Architects? Why did such a lame academy pick you guys!”

Before he could launch into a full-blown rant, Miriam smacked the back of his head with just enough force to make her point. “Shut up, Theo,” she said, her tone sharp. “They got into the academy, and that’s what matters. Unlike you, who ran away when you had your chance.”

Her words hung in the air for a moment, and Rick and Monty both turned to Theo, their curiosity piqued. Monty was the first to speak. “Wait, Theo, you were chosen for an academy?” he asked, a sly grin spreading across his face. “Did you abandon your training?”
Rick, unable to resist joining in, added, “What happened? Did you run away or something?”

Theo threw up his hands in exasperation. “Come on, give me a break!” he exclaimed, trying to defend himself. “They were going to send me to the war front! What academy sends a 17-year-old to a battlefield?” He gestured dramatically to himself, his voice laced with mock indignation.
The group burst into laughter at his antics, the tension of the day melting away in the shared humor.
Amid their discussion and banter, Lucy and Laura arrived, their faces lighting up when they spotted Rick and Monty. “I heard you guys made it!” Lucy called out as she approached.
“That’s awesome!” Laura added enthusiastically. “Which academy did you get into?”

Rick answered her, repeating their earlier reply about the Architects Academy. As he spoke, he cast a quick glance toward Marcus, who had just joined the group, his trademark warm smile firmly in place. Rick had been dreading Marcus’s reaction, fearing disappointment or disapproval, but to his surprise, Marcus seemed genuinely pleased.
“That’s fantastic,” Marcus said, clapping Rick on the shoulder. “The Architects Academy has its own unique strengths. You’ll both do great there.”

Rick felt a wave of relief wash over him. He hadn’t realized how much he’d been seeking Marcus’s approval until that very moment. The older man’s support eased the lingering doubts in his mind, solidifying his resolve.
Just as the tension melted into shared relief, Laura’s voice cut through with a burst of enthusiasm. “This calls for a celebration!” she yelled, throwing her arms into the air dramatically.

“Oh yeah!” Theo chimed in, his excitement returning full force. “Where are we going to celebrate? Are we heading to a grand suite? A festival? Oh, wait, there’s a new restaurant that just opened—I’d love to taste everything on their menu! Shall we go there?” His eyes practically sparkled at the thought.

Miriam didn’t let him finish his daydream. Smacking the back of his head yet again, she scolded, “Shut up, Theo! You’re not the one we’re celebrating, and you definitely don’t get to decide where we go.”
“Oh, right.” Theo rubbed the back of his head, looking sheepish. “Sorry, I got carried away.”

The group shared another round of laughter at Theo’s expense, the celebratory mood settling over them like a warm embrace. After some discussion, it was decided that they’d head home first to rest and plan something later.

The warm glow of lanterns illuminated the serene setting of the hot springs inn. The air was filled with the comforting scent of cedar and herbs, while the sound of flowing water added a soothing background melody. Rick and Monty, along with their loved ones, occupied a private area, laughter and joy weaving through their conversation. Plates of steaming delicacies were spread across the table, inviting everyone to indulge.

Just as Theo was in the middle of a spirited debate with Miriam about who would eat the last dumpling, Rick noticed a familiar figure across the room. Shirley and her family sat nearby, surrounded by a modest gathering of their own. Their smiles were genuine, and the pride in their eyes as they celebrated their daughter’s admission into the Martial Arts Academy was unmistakable.
Shirley spotted Rick and Monty and waved enthusiastically. “Rick! Monty!” she called out, her voice cutting through the chatter of the inn.

They walked over, greeted warmly by her family. Shirley’s father, a broad-shouldered man with a weathered face, extended a firm handshake. “You must be Rick and Monty,” he said. “Shirley’s mentioned you two quite a bit.”
“She has?” Monty asked, a teasing smirk playing on his lips. Shirley’s cheeks turned a faint shade of red as she gave Monty a playful nudge.
Shirley’s mother chimed in, her voice kind but direct. “You boys did well to get into the Architects Academy. It’s not an easy path, but it’s an honorable one.”
Rick nodded, appreciating the encouragement. “We’ll do our best,” he said, his voice steady.
As the two groups mingled, Shirley leaned closer to Rick. “I’m glad we’re all celebrating together,” she said softly. “It feels… like things are falling into place.”

Before Rick could respond, Theo’s voice boomed from their table. “Rick! Monty! Are you abandoning us already?” His dramatic tone earned a round of laughter, and the two boys excused themselves to rejoin their group.
While joy and celebration filled the hot springs inn, Edmond faced a storm of a different kind.

Back at his family estate, the opulent marble halls echoed with his father’s raised voice. “You cannot be serious, Edmond!” Lord Greybourne bellowed, his eyes blazing with fury. “The Architects Academy? A step away from mediocrity! Do you know the opportunities you’ve squandered?”
Edmond stood firm, his jaw set and his gaze unwavering. “It’s my decision, Father. I’ve made my choice.”

Lady Greybourne, seated with perfect posture, spoke in a voice colder than the winter wind. “Your father has connections. We can fix this disgrace. All you need to do is renounce this foolish decision, and you’ll be back in the Silver Fang Academy by tomorrow.”
“And then what?” Edmond shot back, his voice tinged with defiance. “Spend my life chasing your dreams instead of mine? No, I won’t do it.”
