Lord Greybourne’s fist slammed onto the table, silencing the room. “You’re throwing away everything we’ve built for you. Do not expect our support if you continue down this path.”
“I never expected it,” Edmond replied, his voice quiet but resolute. Without another word, he turned and left the room, leaving his stunned parents behind.
In the solitude of his chambers, Edmond allowed himself a moment to breathe. Despite the weight of his family’s disapproval, his resolve only grew stronger.
Back at the inn, the celebration began to wind down. The stars were out, casting their gentle light over the courtyard where Rick, Monty, and their friends gathered for some fresh air.

Shirley and her family were preparing to leave, but before she departed, she approached Rick one last time. “You’ve got a good group around you,” she said, her eyes reflecting the glow of the lanterns. “Hold onto that. You’ll need them more than ever in the days ahead.”
Rick nodded. “Thanks, Shirley. And congratulations again.”

When she was gone, Marcus stood up, clearing his throat. “Rick, Monty,” he began, “ You both have grow in ways I never imagined. The road ahead won’t be easy, but don’t forget why you started. Remember, you’re not just building for yourselves—you’re shaping something greater.”
Lucy chimed in, her tone light but sincere. “And don’t you dare lose touch with us. We expect updates, letters, and maybe some gifts when you become big shots.”
Laughter followed her comment, but it was clear everyone felt the weight of the moment.
Rick looked at his friends, his heart swelling with gratitude. “We won’t let you down,” he said firmly.
Monty nodded, adding, “We’ll give it everything we’ve got. That’s a promise.”

As the group dispersed, Rick and Monty stood side by side, gazing at the horizon. Determination burned in their eyes, the weight of their choices grounding them while the promise of the future lifted them.

As the evening deepened, the Greybourne mansion was cloaked in an unsettling silence. Edmond sat by the window in his room, staring at the admission token in his hands. The Architects Academy—his decision to join it was not impulsive but deliberate, born of a need to carve his own path. However, his parents saw it differently.

A knock at the door broke his thoughts. His father, Lord Greybourne, entered, followed closely by his mother. Both were clad in their usual regal attire, exuding an air of authority. Yet, their expressions betrayed a mix of disappointment and frustration.

“Edmond,” his father began, his tone unusually calm, “you must understand what you’re doing. The Architects Academy is beneath our family’s status. It’s filled with commoners—people who lack the discipline, resources, and prestige that institutions like the Silver Fang Martial Arts Academy offer.”
His mother nodded in agreement. “It’s an academy for rejects, Edmond. You are a Greybourne, a noble of high status. Your place is among the elite, not... not among the rabble.”

Edmond’s jaw clenched as he listened, his resolve hardening with every word. “You think you can talk me out of this?” he replied, his voice steady but laced with anger. “All my life, I’ve done what you wanted. I’ve lived up to your expectations, followed your rules. Why can’t you support me just this once?”
His mother sighed, her voice soft yet piercing. “We only want what’s best for you, Edmond.”
“What’s best for me?” Edmond shot back. “Why do you hate the commoners so much? What have they done to deserve your contempt?”

His father’s face darkened, his calm façade cracking. “You don’t understand the weight of our name, boy!” he bellowed. “The commoners don’t belong in the same league as us. And if you insist on tarnishing our name by joining that academy, you leave us no choice.”
Before Edmond could react, his father raised his hand and struck him across the face. The slap echoed in the room, but Edmond didn’t flinch. He stood his ground, his eyes blazing with defiance.
“You’re banned from leaving this room,” his father declared. “Let’s see how you’ll attend that worthless academy now.”
He turned and stormed out, his mother trailing behind. At the doorway, she paused and glanced back at her son. “You’re a disgrace to the Greybourne family, Edmond. I am highly disappointed in you.”
As they exited, Lady Greybourne called for the chief guard. “William!” she snapped, her voice sharp.
The man arrived quickly, bowing slightly. “Yes, ma’am?”
“Ensure that Edmond doesn’t leave his room or the mansion,” she ordered. “I want him monitored day and night until his admission token expires.”
“Yes, ma’am,” William replied. He signaled a group of guards, who took up positions outside Edmond’s room.

Inside, Edmond leaned against the window, his expression unreadable. He had heard everything. Quietly, he began gathering some clothes and supplies, his resolve stronger than ever. As night fell, he barricaded his door with furniture and slipped out of the window, disappearing into the darkness.

Elsewhere, Kara walked briskly down a quiet street, her face flushed with a mix of anger and determination. She had just left an exclusive restaurant where her parents were hosting a small gathering in her honor. Despite their reluctant support for her decision, they had made it clear how disappointed they were.
Ahead, she spotted Whitney leaning against a lamppost. The two exchanged knowing glances.
“Dodging your family too?” Kara asked, her tone light but tinged with frustration.
Whitney nodded, her expression guilty. “I lied to them, Kara. I told them I got into the Silver Fang Academy. They were so proud... I couldn’t bring myself to tell them the truth.”
Kara sighed. “At least they’re proud of you. My parents made it clear they think I’m throwing my future away.”
The two fell into step together, their shared frustrations drawing them closer.

Meanwhile, not far away, Lila and Brock sat on the steps of a quiet inn, sharing a simple meal. Both were orphans, having lost their families years ago in the chaos of war. Despite their hardships, they had found solace in each other and were determined to make something of themselves.
“This academy... it’s our chance,” Lila said, her voice soft but firm.
Brock nodded. “We may not have the resources or support that others have, but we have each other. And we’ll make it work.”
Their conversation was interrupted by the sound of footsteps. Turning, they saw Edmond approaching, his disheveled appearance betraying his recent escape.
“Where are you coming from?” Brock asked, recognizing it was Edmond.
Edmond replied. “i had to leave home else i would lose my chance into the academy”.
Lila and Brock nodded in understanding.
Moments later, Kara and Whitney walked into them, and together, the group decided to head to the inn where Rick and Monty were staying.

After they returned to the inn, Marcus and the others retired to their rooms, tired from the day's excitement. However, Monty and Rick remained wide awake, their energy renewed by the unexpected arrival of their friends. It wasn’t long before the group gathered by the fireside in the inn’s common room, the warm glow of the flames reflecting in their eager eyes.
The cozy atmosphere and the camaraderie among them led to a natural conversation, one filled with curiosity about their shared decision to switch to the Architects Martial Arts Academy.
Kara, leaning slightly forward, broke the silence. “Lila, Brock, I’m curious—why did you two switch? What made you leave the academy you’d already been admitted to?”

Lila smiled faintly, her gaze fixed on the flickering flames. “It just felt like the right thing to do,” she said, her voice thoughtful. “I can’t explain it fully, but I had this gut feeling, this sense that the Architects Martial Arts Academy was the real deal. It was like... I could see something others couldn’t. So, I made the switch.”
Her words hung in the air for a moment, and the others nodded in understanding.

Brock shrugged, a playful grin spreading across his face. “Honestly, I just thought it’d be better to learn with familiar faces. I figured it’d be more fun to have someone I know by my side, and Lila was already going. That’s why I switched.”
Kara tilted her head, processing their answers before shifting her gaze to Edmond. “What about you, Edmond? Why did you switch?”

Edmond sighed, running a hand through his hair as he thought about how to word his response. “I was tired of my parents controlling every decision in my life,” he began. “They wanted me to attend the Silver Fang Martial Arts Academy—it was their choice, not mine. I started wondering what kind of future I’d have if I kept living according to their wishes. Would I really be happy? So, I made the switch. It was a bold move, but I had to take control of my own life.”
His tone was resolute, and the group exchanged glances, impressed by his conviction.
“Well, Whitney,” Rick said, turning to her, “why did you make the switch?”

Whitney leaned back in her chair, her eyes distant as she recalled her reasoning. “I’d heard stories,” she said, “about a rare group of people who once studied at the Architects Academy. Their feats, their power—it all sounded like a legend. But there was something about those stories that intrigued me. I wanted to find out for myself if the academy could really produce warriors like that. That’s why I switched.”
Her words carried a quiet determination, and the others couldn’t help but admire her curiosity and drive.
“What about you, Kara?” Lila asked. “Why did you switch?”

Kara’s expression turned thoughtful as she clasped her hands together. “I’d heard the rumors,” she admitted. “How the Architects Academy was weak, how they lacked students because of their supposed incompetence. But... something didn’t add up. I felt there had to be more to it. Why would an academy even exist if it was as awful as everyone said? I wanted to know the truth, and that’s what drove me to make the switch.”
Her words left the group silent for a moment, each of them reflecting on their own reasons.

Then Edmond smirked, breaking the quiet. “So, Rick,” he said teasingly, “why on earth would you waste your one chance on an academy everyone says is worthless? If it turns out to be as bad as they claim, you’ll have made a terrible mistake.”
The group chuckled at Edmond’s mockery, and Rick couldn’t help but smile as he prepared his answer. “Well,” he began, “I’ve always had this feeling since I was a kid—”
“You’re still a kid,” Kara interrupted with a playful grin.

The room erupted in soft laughter before Rick continued. “Fair enough. But as I was saying, I’ve always had an interest in the Architects. There’s something about them that’s fascinated me for as long as I can remember. When I found out there was an academy in their honor, I couldn’t pass up the opportunity to satisfy my curiosity. Sure, I heard the rumors during the tournament, but I thought it through. I made my decision, and I’m sticking to it.”
The fire crackled as his words settled over the group, each of them feeling a renewed sense of purpose.
After a while, Kara, Whitney, Lila, and Brock rose from their seats. “It’s getting late,” Whitney said. “We should head home.”
“Yeah,” Kara agreed. “We’ll see you all tomorrow.”
They exchanged goodbyes and goodnights before heading out into the night, leaving Edmond behind.

As the others left, Edmond approached the innkeeper and paid for a room. He had no intention of returning to his family’s mansion. For now, this inn would be his home until it was time to depart for the Architects Academy.

As the evening drew to a close, the inn grew quieter, save for the occasional crackle of the fire in the hearth. After spending time with his friends, Edmond retired to the room he had booked, carrying with him the weight of the night's conversations.

Sitting by the small window, he gazed out at the moonlit sky. His thoughts lingered on his parents' harsh words and the decision he had made to break away from their expectations. For years, he had lived in the shadow of their ambitions, constantly seeking their approval. But tonight, for the first time, he felt a sense of freedom, even amidst the turmoil.

Reaching into his bag, he pulled out the Architects Martial Arts Academy token and turned it over in his hands. The symbol etched into its surface felt almost alive, radiating a quiet power that reassured him he was on the right path.
“No matter what,” he whispered to himself, “I’ll prove to them—and to myself—that I made the right choice.”

As the first rays of dawn began to creep over the horizon, Edmond set the token down and climbed into bed, his resolve stronger than ever. Tomorrow would mark the start of a new chapter, one that he was determined to write on his own terms.

chapters.label: Chapter 28
chapters.title: Journey to the Academy.
chapters.summary: Rick, Monty, and their friends prepare to journey to the Architects Martial Arts Academy. Their plans change when Edmond’s family places a massive bounty on him, forcing the group to protect him and keep his identity hidden.
paragraphs: The morning sun filtered gently through the windows of the inn, its warm rays ushering in a new day. The inn was alive with the sound of stirring footsteps and muted conversations, but in one of the rooms, the atmosphere was far from serene. Rick and Monty were already awake, sitting on their beds as they watched their friend Theo muttering in his sleep.
"Don't let it get cold, it will lose its savour then," Theo mumbled, his voice filled with a strange mix of desperation and delight.

Rick and Monty exchanged glances before bursting into laughter, trying their best to stifle the sound so as not to wake him. But their attempts failed miserably as Monty, with tears of laughter in his eyes, pointed out the drool dripping from Theo's lips.

At that moment, Elric walked into the room. "Good morning, kids," he said warmly, his deep voice resonating with affection. His gaze shifted between Rick and Monty, their faces red with suppressed laughter. "What's the laughter all about this morning?" he asked, his lips curling into a smile.

Monty, still grinning mischievously, gestured toward Theo, who was now muttering something else in his sleep. "It looks delicious… Let me have a bite, please," Theo mumbled, his hand twitching as though reaching out for an imaginary meal.
Elric chuckled, shaking his head. "That boy must have been dreaming about food all night," he said. "Let’s not wake him up just yet. Breakfast will be much livelier with him in this state."
Rick smirked. "I think he’s been dreaming about the pies from last night. I caught him sneaking an extra one when he thought no one was looking."
As their laughter subsided, Theo finally stirred, blinking groggily at the three faces staring at him. "What? Did I miss something?" he asked, his voice thick with sleep.
Monty burst out laughing again. "Nothing much, just your dreams about food. Are you sure you're not part bear? You eat like you’re hibernating for the winter!"
Theo groaned, pulling the blanket over his head as the others teased him mercilessly. "Fine, fine, I’m getting up. Stop ganging up on me!"
Elric clapped his hands. "Alright, enough teasing. Wash up and get ready. Breakfast is on the schedule, and we’ll need everyone to be sharp for the journey ahead."
Shortly after the group gathered, and headed to a well-reputed restaurant a few streets away. As they settled into a large corner table, laughter and conversation surrounded them.
That’s when they spotted Edmond. He was seated at a small table, eating alone, his face a mix of relief and lingering sadness.
Theo was the first to notice, nudging Elric dramatically. “That’s Edmond! I can’t believe he’s here all alone!”

Rick and Monty exchanged knowing looks before Rick began in a hushed tone, leaning closer. “It’s… complicated. He had a rough situation with his family" he said “He had to run away from home. His family—well, let’s just say things aren’t great for him there." He whispered.
"He told us yesterday that his parents didn't like his decision to join the Architects Martial Arts Academy.” Monty added.

"Ohh I see" Marcus muttered as he stood and approached Edmond, the rest of the group following close behind. Edmond looked up in surprise as they approached but quickly relaxed when he saw Rick and Monty.
When they reached him, Lucy spoke first. “Edmond, we couldn’t help but notice you sitting here alone. Rick mentioned your situation. Is everything all right?”
"Ohh I'm fine" Edmond said trying to hide the sadness in his tone. "It's just a little family problem"
“I understand" Marcus replied "you’re not alone anymore,” Marcus said warmly, his deep voice filled with reassurance. “Come sit with us.”

As Edmond joined the group, he explained everything—the overbearing control of his family, his desire for freedom, and his decision to escape and go to the academy. By the time he finished, the group was silent, their expressions a mix of sympathy and admiration.
"That's sad" Laura said thoughtfully "Parents are supposed to support their kids decisions mostly one about their future".
“You did the right thing,” Rosa said softly, her voice firm. “No one should be forced to live a life they don’t want.”
Their words of sympathy and encouragement calmed him down. "Thanks guys" he said "but I should get going now, I don't want to cause you guys much trouble" he implied as he turned to leave.
"Edmond wait!" Rick called out, Edmond halted, turning towards the group as Rick approached him.
"You said you were going to the academy right?" Rick asked.
"Yeah" Edmond replied "once I grab my things I'll be headed that way" he added.
"Why don't you join us?" Rick asked "it will be safer and less lonely if you travel with us" he added.
"I would love to Rick" Edmond replied "but knowing my parents they will do all they can to bring me back home" he said "and that means they could go to extreme measures to fulfil that" he implied.
"It's alright" Monty interjected "we will protect you until we get to the academy" he added "right guys?" Monty said, looking at the group for a reaction.
"Of course" Laura chimed brightly.

"You can stay with us Edmond" Lucy added "the journey starts tomorrow and we can guide you to the academy because I presume you do not know where it is located" she implied, Edmond's face fell realising she was right.

"You may be right" Edmond replied "I do not know the way to the Architects Martial Arts Academy but I..." he paused "I just don't want to cause trouble for you guys" he said humbly, his expression a mix of gratitude and concern.
"Hold up kid" Marcus said, his voice devoid of his earlier warm expression "I may not be much" he said "but these two are top generals of the Rover Kingdom" he implied nudging at Lucy and Laura.

"Don't you think it will be safer to travel in their midst than going alone?" He asked, not expecting an answer, he got up and walked towards Edmond, placing his hand on his shoulder "Don't be silly and join us already" he said, his voice warm and bright.
After giving it a thought for a while, his head remains bowed, he said "Alright, I will travel with you all".
The group had their meal and continued their chatter, the atmosphere lightening with love and joy, they returned to the inn after their meals.

Meanwhile, back at the grand estate of the Greybourne family, the scene was far from tranquil. When the maids arrived at Edmond’s room to deliver his breakfast, they found the door locked. Knocking produced no response, and concern quickly grew.

After failed attempts to open the door, the chief guard, Sir William, was summoned. With a swift spell, he used magic to forcefully open the door. As the heavy wooden door creaked open, the sight of an empty room greeted them. The window was ajar, the morning breeze rustling the curtains.
Edmond’s parents were informed immediately. His father’s face darkened with fury, while his mother’s hands trembled with barely concealed anger.
“How could this happen under our roof?” his father bellowed, slamming his fist onto the table.
“We must find him,” his mother said coldly. “We cannot allow him to tarnish the Greybourne family name.”
Sir William was ordered to issue a public bounty for Edmond’s capture. Within hours, posters were plastered across the city, offering handsome rewards:
200 gold coins for information leading to his location.
1000 gold coins for his safe capture.
An honorary position in their guard ranks and a piece of land for the captor that captures and delivers him safely.
The news spread quickly, drawing the attention of bounty hunters and mercenaries eager to claim the reward.
Back at the Inn, Theo rushed into the inn with a dramatic flair, a rolled-up poster clutched tightly in his hand.
Everyone turned to him in confusion as he slammed the poster onto the table.
"Guys, you won’t believe this!" Theo exclaimed, holding up the flyer. "I was getting some snacks when I saw this—there’s a bounty on Edmond’s capture!"

The group gathered around as Theo showed them the poster, their eyes scanning the poster in disbelief. It was a detailed announcement, complete with a drawing of Edmond and the generous rewards for his capture.
Edmond’s heart sank as he recognized the stern portrait of himself alongside the enticing reward. "I never thought they'd go this far"
"You have a weird family" Theo teased.
"Shut up Theo" Miriam interjected "this is not a time for one of your jokes" she scolded.
Marcus who sat at a corner of the inn sneered "Come on, it's alright. This is to be expected" he said, his unbattered expression surprised the group.
"What do you mean?" Elric asked, tugging at his beard.
Leaning forward Marcus replied "After all he is the only child of the Greybourne family" he implied "so it's only right if they do this" he said pointing at the poster.
"Ohh, that's right" Elias muttered.
"You shouldn't go out for the rest of the day" Lucy advised "to avoid exposing your location" she added.
The group nodded in agreement, one by one they assured Edmond that everything would be alright as long as he was with them.
"Don't worry Edmond" Rick said "you'll be fine with us" he added, Edmond nodded, his expression a mix of gratitude and worry.
"You should all get some rest" Marcus said "we'll begin the journey at first light tomorrow" he added.
Turning to the Innkeeper Elias said "I hope we can trust you to keep his presence here a secret until we leave"
"Of course!" The man replied. "But that would cost extra" he chimed his expression bright.
Marcus throws a pouch of coins to him "That should suffice, right?"
"Absolutely!" The Innkeeper chimed, keeping the money in his drawer.
Just as the group were going to their various rooms, a knock was heard at the door, everyone fell silent, the Innkeeper, a broad man with a light scar on his face walked up to the door.
Slightly opening the door he said "The Inn is full, come back tomorrow"
"We're here to see Rick and Monty" a feminine voice called out. The Innkeeper turned to the group expecting a response.
"That voice" Rick muttered.
"It's Lila" Monty added.
"Let them in" Rosa implied.
The Innkeeper opened the door and two figures slipped in.
The two figures entered the inn, their faces illuminated by the dim light. Lila and Brock stepped forward, their expressions a mix of relief and determination.
"Lila! Brock!" Rick exclaimed, a grin spreading across his face. He and Monty moved quickly to greet their friends.
"We’ve been looking for you," Lila said, her tone firm but warm. "Word travels fast, and we heard about the bounty on Edmond. Figured he'd be here and may need a little extra help on the journey."
Brock nodded in agreement. "Traveling with a target on your back isn’t easy. We thought it best to join you since we're headed to the same location and make sure everyone reaches the academy safely."
Marcus, standing at the back of the room, raised an eyebrow at the new arrivals. "And you are?" he asked, his voice neutral but sharp.
"They’re with us," Rick said quickly. "Lila and Brock are strong fighters and trustworthy allies."
"Strong fighters, huh?" Marcus said, crossing his arms. He scanned them critically before his gaze softened. "If Rick vouches for you, that’s good enough for me. Welcome aboard."
"Thanks," Brock said. "We’ll do our part to make sure no harm comes to Edmond—or anyone else."

"Speaking of Edmond," Lila added, her gaze turning to him. "You’re braver than most to stand against your family’s wishes like this. We’ll do all we can until we reach the academy. You can count on us."
Edmond smiled faintly, still overwhelmed by the group’s unwavering support. "Thank you. I don’t know how I’ll ever repay all of you."
"You don’t have to," Lucy said with a reassuring smile. "We’re all in this together now."
With the group now expanded, the innkeeper brought out additional rooms for Lila and Brock, though Marcus handed over yet another pouch of coins to ensure their presence would remain undisclosed.

The group settled in for the night, aware that their journey had grown even more perilous with the bounty hanging over Edmond’s head. But their resolve was firm—they would face whatever challenges came their way together.
The Next Morning.
As the sun rose, the group set out on the road to the academy, their caravan larger and their spirits high despite the danger.

Unbeknownst to them, three separate convoys were traveling along similar routes, each carrying a student with ties to influential families. Whitney, Shirley, and Kara were among those heading to the academy, escorted by groups of guards.

Whitney, a sharp and confident young woman with a fiery temper, rode at the front of her convoy, her piercing gaze scanning the horizon. Her guards followed closely, their hands resting on their weapons.
Shirley, softer-spoken but no less determined, rode with her own escort, her eyes filled with nervous excitement as she anticipated the challenges ahead at the academy.

Kara, the daughter of a prominent noble, seemed more annoyed than anything, brushing off her parents’ insistence on sending a full convoy with her. "I don’t need this much protection, I can take care of myself" she muttered under her breath.
Fate, however, had other plans.
As Rick and his group moved through a narrow woodland path, they encountered Whitney’s convoy first. The tension in the air was palpable as the two groups sized each other up.
Whitney dismounted from her horse, her fiery eyes locking onto Rick. "Hey Rick! It's nice to meet you out here" she exclaimed "You’re headed to the academy too, right?"
"That’s right, Whitney it's rather a good coincidence we ran into each other here" Rick replied.
"What's with convoy?" Theo sneered, gesturing at the soldiers behind Whitney.
"Well they're a farewell escort from my parents" she said, her face brimming brightly.
"What about Edmond" she asked "I heard what happened, his parents are so mean" she implied "placing a bounty on your own son is complicated" she added.
"I'm here" Edmond replied, taking off the hood that covered his face.
Surprised, Whitney exclaimed "Oh my goodness Edmond!" She said "I couldn't recognize you in that outfit earlier"
"He had to disguise so it will be harder for mercenaries and bounty hunters to recognize him" Monty implied.
Before Whitney could respond, the sound of hooves echoed in the distance. Shirley’s convoy appeared next, followed shortly by Kara’s.
The small clearing became a meeting point for all three groups, their paths converging unexpectedly.
Lucy stepped forward, her diplomatic tone cutting through the tension. "It seems we’re all headed to the same place. Wouldn't it be safer if we all travelled together?. Safety in numbers, after all."
"Of course!" Shirley chimed, rushing down from the magic beast she was riding on.
"Whitney! Rick! And Monty!" She called out as she approached them, Kara got down from the Shiryl that carried her.
"And who are you?" Shirley sneered, trying to recognise Edmond who had already put back his hood on.
"That's Edmond!" Whitney chimed.
"Huhhn!" Shirley exclaimed, Edmond slowly let's off his hood revealing his face.
"Edmond!" Kara exclaimed as she approached. "Ah it's good to see you" she implied.
"I'm glad to see you all too" Edmond replied, a smile tugging at his face.
"We heard what happened" Kara said "we were worried too, Whitney and I came to the Inn this morning but you were already gone" she added.
"We had to leave early" Rick replied.
"Well it's good we're all here" Shirley exclaimed.
Marcus, standing at the center of the growing crowd, let out a deep sigh. "Looks like we’ve got quite the party now."
With that the convoys joined rick and his group as they continued on their journey,  the path to the academy became more treacherous, but their combined strength and determination gave them hope.
Despite the dangers that lay ahead, one thing was certain: this was no longer just a journey. It was the start of something much greater.

chapters.label: Chapter 29
chapters.title: Journey to the Academy II.
chapters.summary: Rick and his companions continue their journey to the Architects Martial Arts Academy, but their journey takes a dangerous turn when a group of bounty hunters begins tracking them to capture Edmond. After noticing the threat, Marcus uses his Immortal Eyes of the Watcher to discover their numbers and confirms that an attack is imminent. The group camps by the River Edarr and prepares for the inevitable confrontation, knowing that the bounty hunters are waiting for the right moment to strike.
paragraphs: The journey to the academy continued as the group made their way through winding forest paths and mountainous terrain. The sun had begun its descent when they stumbled upon a quiet, remote village nestled in the valley. The place seemed untouched by time, with its simple cottages, cobblestone streets, and the faint sound of wind chimes echoing through the cool evening air.
Rick and Monty looked around in awe, marveling at the village's rustic charm. "This place looks like it's straight out of a storybook," Rick said, his eyes wide with wonder.
"I can't believe places like this still exist," Shirley added, her gaze fixed on the vibrant flowers lining the streets.

Kara, ever generous, offered to pay for their stay at the only inn in the village. “Privacy is important,” she said, ensuring that the entire inn was reserved for the group while leaving the bar area open for other customers.

Meanwhile, Lila and Brock, who had visited the village before, took it upon themselves to guide the others. They shared tales of their previous experiences, pointing out landmarks and introducing the group to some of the local customs.
Later that evening, the group decided to dine at a cozy local restaurant recommended by Lila. The smell of roasted meat and freshly baked bread filled the air, adding warmth to the homely ambiance.

As they settled in and began their meal, Lucy and Laura noticed a hooded figure sitting in the far corner of the room. The stranger's gaze seemed to linger on their table, though he made an effort to remain inconspicuous.
Laura leaned toward Lucy. "Do you see him?" she whispered.
Lucy nodded subtly, her hand resting instinctively on the hilt of her blade beneath the table. “He’s watching us,” she replied, keeping her voice low.

Marcus, too, caught sight of the hooded man and observed him discreetly. Though the stranger appeared to be just another traveler, his behavior betrayed him. Marcus noted the way he occasionally glanced at Edmond, as if sizing him up.
Meanwhile, Rick, Monty, and Theo were too absorbed in their food to notice anything unusual. Edmond, however, sat stiffly, a sense of unease washing over him.

When the meal ended, Marcus quietly informed the group about the stranger. "We’re being followed," he said, his voice firm. "That man has been watching us since we arrived. I suspect he’s a bounty hunter."
Back at the inn, the atmosphere grew tense. Marcus gathered everyone in the common room to discuss their next steps.
“We’ll leave at first light,” Marcus instructed. “For tonight, we need to be on high alert. Guards will take shifts around the inn, and I want everyone ready to move at a moment’s notice.”
Lila and Brock, refusing to let the knights and guards handle the situation alone, volunteered to stay awake and assist with the night watch.
“I won’t be able to sleep knowing someone might try to harm us,” Lila said determinedly.
“Same here,” Brock added. “We’ll also keep watch just in case.”

The guards and knights stationed themselves at strategic points around the inn, keeping a watchful eye on the surrounding area. The rest of the group reluctantly retreated to their rooms, though sleep seemed elusive for most.
As the night deepened, a sense of foreboding hung in the air.

Shirley, unable to sleep, sat by her window, watching the moonlight dance on the cobblestone streets. Suddenly, she noticed flickering shadows moving just beyond the perimeter of the inn. Her heart raced as she leaned closer, but when she looked again, the street was empty.

Edmond lay awake, staring at the ceiling. His thoughts were consumed by his family and the bounty hunters likely searching for him. Every creak of the floorboards and gust of wind outside made him flinch.
Meanwhile, the knights guarding the inn reported seeing glimpses of movement in the distance. “It’s probably just animals,” one of them said, though his voice lacked conviction.

Unbeknownst to them, the hooded man from the restaurant was still nearby. He stood in the shadows just outside the inn, his figure barely visible in the moonlight. His eyes remained fixed on the building as the lights inside began to flicker out one by one.

The next morning, the group awoke to the soft glow of dawn spreading over the village. Marcus, ever punctual, gave the order to prepare for departure. Within an hour, the caravan was ready, and they set out, leaving behind the quiet charm of the remote settlement.

As they followed the winding forest path, the village slowly faded from sight—its cobblestone streets and rustic cottages slipping into memory. For most of the group, the hooded man from the previous night was already forgotten, their thoughts shifting to the journey ahead.

But not everyone could let it go so easily. Lucy and Laura, unsettled since spotting the stranger, couldn't shake a nagging sense of unease. They exchanged wary glances, their hands never straying far from their weapons, yet they chose to focus on the road rather than voice their concerns.

Elias, however, strode forward with his usual easygoing confidence. He had noticed the tension in his companions but dismissed it with a shrug. Worrying won’t do us any good, he thought, his mind already drifting to thoughts of sparring with the knights escorting Kara.

The caravan moved in a steady rhythm, the clopping of hooves and the crunch of footsteps blending with the occasional bursts of lighthearted chatter and Theo's humors. For a brief moment, it seemed as though they might finally enjoy some peace after all they had endured.
But danger was closer than they realized.

In the dense underbrush behind them, the hooded man had regrouped with a band of bounty hunters—their numbers now swelling to thirty-five. Silent as phantoms, they followed, matching the caravan’s every step, closing the distance with practiced precision.
At the rear, Marcus remained quiet but vigilant. He had noticed the subtle disturbances—the faint rustle of leaves where there should have been none, the fleeting shadows moving through the trees.
His eyes narrowed. We’re not alone.

Closing his eyes, he muttered, "Immortal Eyes of the Watcher." At once, his perception expanded. Like ripples in still water, the presences of their pursuers became clear—flanking them from the sides, trailing them from the rear.
His suspicion was confirmed.
Still, he said nothing. Alerting the group now would only cause unnecessary panic. Instead, his grip tightened on the reins. We’ll handle it when the time comes.
And so, the caravan pressed on, blissfully unaware of the storm gathering in the shadows.

The sun was setting when the caravan reached the banks of River Edarr, its surface shimmering with golden hues as it stretched into the horizon. The journey had been long, and with the dense forest now behind them, the group welcomed the open space.
Lucy and Laura, who had been leading the caravan, slowed their pace before coming to a halt.

"We'll camp here for the night and continue at first light," Laura bellowed, her voice carrying over the group. One by one, the travelers dismounted from their horses and beasts, stretching their weary limbs.

At the rear, Marcus remained mounted atop his battle-hardened magical beast, a towering creature with the face of a saber-tooth tiger and hardened scales covering its muscular frame. Its tail, infused with latent magical energy, swayed left to right as if sensing something unseen.
Marcus smirked as he felt the distinct presence of their pursuers growing closer.
"This is where we make our stand," he muttered, dismounting.

As the caravan set up camp, responsibilities were quickly assigned. Two guards ventured into the forest to hunt for meat. Elric and Elias volunteered to fish in the river. Rosa and Miriam gathered firewood and began setting up a cookfire. The children—Rick, Monty, Edmond, Kara, Whitney, Lila, Brock, and Shirley, accompanied by Theo went to wade in the shallow parts of the river. Kara's escort knights, along with Whitney’s guards, insisted on accompanying them for protection.
While the camp settled into routine, unseen eyes watched from the shadows.

From within the thick underbrush, a group of thirty-five bounty hunters observed the unsuspecting travelers. Cloaked figures moved soundlessly between the trees, eyes locked onto their primary target.
"Why don't we attack now?" one of the hunters whispered.
The leader, a grizzled man with a scar running down his cheek, narrowed his eyes.
"We're not here for a fight," he muttered. "It's the boy we need."

He gestured toward Lucy and Laura. "Those two? They’re top generals of the Rover Kingdom. They're powerful." His gaze then drifted toward Marcus. A flicker of recognition passed through his face, but uncertainty lingered.
"That man… I've seen him before. But where?" He clenched his fists. "Regardless, I can tell he's dangerous."
Another hunter scoffed. "So what? The greater the fight, the fewer people to split the reward with." A smirk curled his lips.
The leader silenced him with a sharp glare. "We wait. When they’re asleep, when only a handful are keeping watch, we go in, take the Greybourne heir, and vanish. We only engage if necessary."
The hunters nodded in agreement, their figures dissolving back into the night.

At the riverbank, Marcus stood with his arms crossed, gazing at the shimmering water. He sensed them—those lurking in the darkness, their presence like a swarm of insects waiting for the right moment to strike.
Behind him, Lucy and Laura approached.
"What's up, Marcus?" Laura teased. "Trying to catch fish with that stare?"
Marcus let out a soft chuckle. "Get out of my hair, Laura."
Then, his expression hardened. "Did you notice? We're being followed."
The lightness in Lucy’s eyes faded as she exchanged a glance with Laura.
"Yeah," Lucy admitted, "but we’re unsure of their numbers."
Marcus smirked. "Thirty-five."
Laura blinked. "What, you got eyes in the forest?"
Lucy frowned. "If that's true, we're outnumbered."
Marcus sighed, "I used a technique—'Immortal Eyes of the Watcher.' It revealed their numbers to me."
Laura leaned in with sudden enthusiasm. "That sounds cool! Teach it to me, Marcus."
"Now’s not the time, Laura," Lucy scolded.
Laura huffed but straightened. "That’s actually why I wanted us to camp here," she admitted. "I figured we should deal with them now rather than be ambushed later."
Marcus nodded. "Then we prepare for them."

As night settled in, the guards returned with a freshly hunted antelope, Elias and Elric arrived with a bundle of fresh fish, and Rosa began cooking over a conjured pot. The rich scent of roasting meat filled the air as everyone gathered around the fire.
Marcus, Lucy, and Laura addressed the group.
"Listen up," Marcus began. "We’re not alone out here. We have bounty hunters on our tail—thirty-five of them."
A ripple of tension passed through the group.
Lucy stepped forward. "We’ll handle them, but everyone needs to be ready. No panic, no hesitation. Stick to the plan."
The younger ones paled but nodded, determination setting in.
They finished their meal in relative silence, knowing that before the night ended, battle would come.

chapters.title: Eyes of the Watcher.
chapters.summary: The journey to the academy takes a dangerous turn when the group is ambushed by bounty hunters seeking Edmond.
paragraphs: The night was deceptively calm. A faint breeze rustled the trees, and the crackling of a dying campfire was the only sound in the clearing. The caravan had settled for the night, their bodies weary from the day's travel. Marcus, deep in slumber, had his arms folded behind his head, his breathing slow and steady. Others were scattered around—some keeping watch, others resting by the fire.
Then, without warning, the air tensed.
A whisper of movement. A sharp breath drawn in the darkness.
Then chaos.

A sudden explosion of movement erupted from the shadows. Figures clad in dark armor, their faces masked, stormed into the camp. Steel flashed in the moonlight. Bounty hunters. They struck swiftly, slitting the throat of one of the outermost guards before he could raise an alarm. His body crumpled, and his sword clattered onto the ground.
“Ambush!” someone shouted, but it was too late—by the time the warning rang out, the bounty hunters had already engaged.

Kara’s knights and Whitney’s guards, caught off guard, scrambled to intercept the enemy. The clashing of blades and bursts of magic lit up the night, illuminating the chaos. Lucy, Laura, Rosa, Miriam, Elias, and Elric quickly fell into formation, fighting as a unit. The knights, though skilled, were up against seasoned warriors who had spent years perfecting the art of the hunt.
The bounty hunters were fast, ruthless, and precise.

Shirley’s guards barely had time to react before they were forced into combat. Swords clashed, sparks flew, and the once-quiet night was filled with the sharp cries of battle. Though outnumbered, the bounty hunters had the edge. They fought with a merciless efficiency that pushed the caravan’s defenders to their limits.

The battle was chaos. The clash of steel, the crackle of magic, and the cries of warriors filled the night. The caravan's defenders—Kara’s knights, Whitney’s guards, Shirley’s guards, and Rick’s group—were fighting desperately against the relentless bounty hunters. Though they had managed to cut down several enemies, exhaustion was evident in their every move. The bounty hunters were relentless, adapting to every shift in the battle, their ruthless efficiency giving them the upper hand.

Lucy, Laura, Rosa, and Miriam fought in sync, their movements coordinated as they battled side by side. Elias and Elric stood at the front, engaging multiple enemies at once, while the others held the line. But the bounty hunters' leader, a towering figure wreathed in a suffocating aura of raw power, had yet to enter the fight. He merely observed, his sharp gaze analyzing the battlefield, waiting for the right moment.
And then, he moved.
A blur of motion, he entered the fray, cutting through their ranks with terrifying speed and strength. The tide of battle shifted instantly in favor of the bounty hunters.

Elias, sensing the shift, gritted his teeth. "We have to stop him!" he shouted. Without hesitation, he lunged at the leader, his blade igniting with magical energy. He struck fast, his attacks precise, aiming to overpower the enemy before he could fully take control of the battlefield.
But the bounty hunters' leader was faster.

With a swift parry, he redirected Elias’s strike, twisting his wrist to create an opening before countering with a devastating punch. A surge of magical energy exploded from his fist, sending Elias sprawling across the battlefield, his sword flying from his grasp.
"ELIAS!" Elric shouted, eyes burning with fury. He darted forward, unleashing a barrage of sword strikes, each swing backed by his formidable strength.

The bounty hunters' leader dodged with unnerving ease, his movements fluid as he sidestepped each attack. Then, without warning, he countered with a brutal kick to Elric’s midsection. The force sent Elric crashing to the ground, momentarily stunned.
The battlefield around them blurred with movement—friends and foes locked in desperate combat—but for a brief moment, everything seemed to slow.
Theo, wounded and barely holding himself upright, turned his gaze toward the largest tent in the camp—where Marcus still slept.
"Marcus... wake up..."
With the last of his strength, Theo staggered toward him and shook him violently. "Marcus, wake up!"

Marcus groggily opened his eyes, irritation flashing across his face before he noticed the state of the battlefield. The chaos, the wounded, the desperation in Theo’s eyes—everything became clear in an instant.
His expression darkened. “Damn it,” he muttered.
Then, Marcus stood.
The battlefield roared on, but something changed. The moment Marcus moved, a deadly stillness spread through the air, as if the battlefield itself sensed what was coming.
The bounty hunters’ leader, now fully in control, smirked as he gave a sharp order. "Get the boy!"

Several bounty hunters broke from the fight, rushing toward Edmond. Kara, Whitney, and Shirley tried to intercept them, but they were too slow. The bounty hunters grabbed Edmond and started dragging him away.
That was when Marcus acted.
Three bounty hunters fell instantly. They didn’t even have time to react—one moment they were running, the next they collapsed, lifeless. The others froze, eyes wide with shock.
"Drop him." Marcus’s voice was cold, devoid of emotion.
The remaining bounty hunters hesitated only for a second before panic took over. They released Edmond and charged at Marcus.
It was their last mistake.

Marcus moved like a phantom, cutting through them with terrifying precision. Each strike was lethal, every movement effortless. Within moments, the battlefield was littered with fallen bounty hunters.

The leader of the bounty hunters, who had been watching his men get torn apart, clenched his jaw. His easy confidence cracked as he turned to face Marcus, his expression shifting from amusement to something darker.
A slow realization dawned upon him.
"You're the ex-general of the Imperial Army of the Rover Kingdom, aren't you?"
Marcus smirked. "It seems I’m famous."
"I knew it," the leader muttered, a glimmer of respect—or perhaps fear—flashing in his eyes. "I’m surprised I recognized you without your armor."
"Not many people do," Marcus said coolly.
The leader scoffed. "How could I call myself a bounty hunter if I failed to recognize someone like you?" He took a step forward. "Listen, I just want the boy. The rest of you can move on."
Marcus’s gaze hardened. "The boy is under my protection. If you want him, you’ll have to go through me."
The bounty hunter grinned. "Then we shall have it your way!"
Without another word, he launched a powerful magical attack. The battle had begun.

Marcus barely had time to react, sidestepping just as a blast of energy scorched the ground where he stood. He deflected another strike aimed at his head, his muscles tightening as he assessed his opponent.
"He’s strong..." Marcus thought, blocking a vicious swing. "Definitely at the Immortal Being Realm, but at what sub-rank? Vanguard? No... he’s still at the peak of the Infinite Luminary."
The bounty hunter pressed his attack, moving with unnatural speed. Marcus countered, but something felt off.
"How is he this powerful? He must be buffed..."
Then, the bounty hunter took a step back, smirking. "You lived up to your title, Marcus The Great Wall of The Rover Kingdom... but I have something that will end this fight."
He clasped his hands together.
"Ace Technique: Eternal Prison!"
The world around them changed. A surge of dark energy erupted from him, swallowing the battlefield.

The moonlit night was consumed by darkness, a void stretching in every direction. Strange seats of shadow formed, chains erupting from them, snaring everyone in their grasp—Kara, Whitney, Shirley, Lucy, Laura, and the others, even the horses and magical beasts. Their magic was blocked. Struggling was useless.
Lightning crackled in the air.
"Lightning of the Eternal Prison!"
The storm struck, and screams filled the air as lightning tore through the group. Pain radiated through their bodies. Some fell unconscious instantly.
All except one.
Marcus stood, unscathed.
The bounty hunter’s grin faltered. "Impossible..."
Marcus sneered. "Impressive technique... but did you really think something this weak could hold me?"
The bounty hunter gestured to the others, smirking. "Maybe not, but look at your companions."
Marcus’s eyes flickered to his left. Lucy and Laura barely held on. To his right, Monty and Rick were unconscious, blood dripping from Monty’s mouth.
His expression darkened. "What have you done?!"
With a single motion, Marcus shattered his chains.
"What?" the bounty hunter whispered, panic creeping into his voice. "How is he moving?"
"Your technique is weak," Marcus said flatly.
Desperate, the bounty hunter unleashed another lightning storm. This time, Marcus flinched. Blood trickled from his mouth.
"Heh," the bounty hunter sneered. "Not so tough now, are you?"
Then Marcus smirked.
Raising his hand, he snapped his fingers. "Ace Technique."
"What?"
"Eyes of the Watcher."*

The darkness trembled. The Eternal Prison shattered. The bounty hunter gasped as a new reality unfolded—a realm of radiant light, infinite in depth. Eyes, countless and unblinking, stared from every direction. And above them all, where the sky should be, a colossal, omniscient eye gazed down.
The bounty hunter trembled.
And then, darkness consumed him.

The bounty hunter’s leader gasped, his body trembling uncontrollably. The overwhelming presence of the colossal eye in the sky bore down upon him, stripping away his confidence, his bravado—his very sense of self. The brilliance of the Eyes of the Watcher dimension illuminated every shadow in his soul, every secret he had buried.
"W-what is this?!" he stammered, stepping back. "What did you do to me?!"
"How is this possible...how can another ace technique be on another ace technique?" The bounty hunters leader stuttered.
"It's... it's impossible"

Marcus exhaled, his breath steady, his expression unreadable. "You called upon your Eternal Prison, believing it to be unbreakable. But you failed to realize..." His gaze sharpened. "There is no prison greater than the one the Watcher creates."
"You already lost the battle the moment we first exchanged blows" Marcus said coolly "you just didn't notice it"
"It makes no sense!" The bounty hunters leader bellowed in agony.
"I already activated my ace technique from the start" Marcus smirked.
"Im.. impossible" the bounty hunters leader muttered "that can't be true!" He argued.

"Oh..but it is" Marcus answered "I just didn't imbue it with my essence, and that is why it didn't fully activate. And the moment I snapped my fingers, I imbued the technique with my magical essence and the sheer will of it overpowered your week dimension" Marcus grinned.
The bounty hunter clenched his fists, channeling all of his remaining magical energy. "Damn you bastard! I will not lose!"
Lightning erupted around him once more, a desperate storm that crackled through the dimension. The arcs of energy twisted violently, seeking Marcus, but the moment they neared him—
—they vanished.
The bounty hunter’s eyes widened. "W-what?!"
Marcus stepped forward, the weight of his presence crushing. "In this realm, your abilities hold no meaning."

The bounty hunter screamed in frustration, launching a barrage of attacks—flames, wind, darkness, every element at his disposal. Each spell surged forth—only to be absorbed into the all-seeing eyes around them. Not a single attack reached Marcus.
"No..." the bounty hunter whispered, a shiver crawling up his spine. "No, no, NO! This isn’t possible!"
Marcus raised a single hand. The air itself seemed to bend to his will.
"Judgment of the Watcher."
The colossal eye above them blinked.

A pulse of pure divine light descended upon the bounty hunters leader. The bounty hunter screamed as his body convulsed, his soul laid bare before the Watcher. Memories flooded his mind—not just his own, but the memories of every life he had ever taken, every innocent he had slain, the pain, the suffering they felt, he felt it all.
The weight of his sins crashed down upon him like an inescapable tide.
"P-please..." he gasped, falling to his knees, his strength utterly drained. "Spare me..."
Marcus’s expression remained impassive. "You never spared anyone, did you?"

The bounty hunter’s body shuddered violently under the weight of Marcus' power. His breath came in ragged gasps, his once-commanding presence reduced to nothing more than a trembling, broken shell. The ethereal light of the Eyes of the Watcher bore into him, dissecting his very essence, revealing every cruel act he had ever committed.
"No... no..." he whimpered, clawing at his own arms as if trying to strip away the sins now laid bare before him.

Marcus took a step forward, his boots making no sound in the endless brilliance of his realm. "Tell me," his voice carried an unnatural resonance, a whisper that echoed in the bounty hunter's soul. "Did the people you slaughtered ever get to beg for mercy?"

The leader flinched, his mouth opening and closing like a fish gasping for air. He had taken countless lives—men, women, even children—without hesitation, without remorse. He had laughed as they pleaded. And now...
Now he was the one begging.
"P-please... spare me... I had to do it to survive..." he croaked, his hands trembling as he tried to shield himself from the unblinking gaze of the Watcher.
Marcus stared at him, his expression unreadable. The air trembled as if the realm itself was waiting for judgment.
But before Marcus could decide, a weak voice called out.
"Marcus..."
Marcus turned his head slightly towards where the voice came from in his dimension.
It was Elias.
Despite the blood dripping from his temple, despite the pain in his battered body, he was conscious again. He was watching.
"That’s enough..." Elias murmured, his voice barely above a whisper, yet filled with conviction. "He can't take anymore of it..."
Marcus exhaled slowly, his gaze shifting back to the bounty hunter. The man was barely holding on, his entire body slumped forward, drained of all strength.
For a moment, silence reigned.
Then Marcus lifted his hand.
The Eyes of the Watcher flickered—then began to fade. The overwhelming pressure disappeared as the dimension started to collapse, its existence unraveling like a dream.

The bounty hunter gasped as reality returned—the real world, the night sky, the cold ground beneath him. He collapsed, barely able to move. His men were either dead, unconscious, or had fled in terror.
Marcus stared at the defeated man, his expression unreadable. "You should be dead," he said flatly. "I won't be so generous next time."
The bounty hunter leader coughed violently, barely able to keep his head up.
"Run," Marcus said. "And if you ever come for Edmond again..."
He let the sentence hang.
The leader didn't need to be told twice. With whatever strength remained in him, he stumbled to his feet and fled into the darkness, limping, broken, humiliated.
The moment he was gone, the tension in the air shattered. The group, still weak from the battle, let out breathless sighs of relief.
Kara, Whitney, and Shirley rushed to Edmond, who laid unconscious. The knights and guards, bruised and battered, gathered around, supporting one another.

Elric, having healed his own injuries, turned his gaze toward Edmond, who remained unconscious. Without hesitation, he moved toward him, kneeling beside him and placing his hands over Edmond’s chest. A soft, golden light enveloped his hands as he channeled his magic. "He took a severe blow, but he’ll recover," Elric murmured, his voice calm as the healing magic worked through Edmond’s injuries. Slowly, Edmond's breathing steadied, and his eyelids flickered before he let out a weak groan.
"Edmond," Kara whispered, gripping his hand tightly.
His eyes opened slightly, unfocused at first, but then recognition dawned in them.
"Easy," Elias muttered. "You took quite the beating."
Edmond exhaled, his hand moving to his head. "What… happened?"
Rick smirked. "You missed one hell of a fight."
Elric exhaled in relief. "You’re stable now. Rest a bit before moving too much." With that, he rose to his feet, ready to tend to the rest of the wounded.
The weight of the battle still lingered, but at least now, Edmond was back with them.
Afterwards Lucy, Laura, Elias, and Elric stood by Marcus, still trying to comprehend what they had just witnessed.
"Marcus," Lucy breathed. "What... When did you get the Ace technique?"

Marcus sighed, running a hand through his hair. "I've always had it," he said simply. "I never got in a situation where It was needed." His gaze darkened slightly. "I had to use it else I'd have lost all of you."
No one spoke after that. The battle was over, but its echoes lingered in their minds.
"I never thought he had transcended to the Immortal Realm" Elric thought to himself before casting a healing spell that healed him gradually.
Rick stared at Marcus for a long time, something unreadable in his expression. "I will be strong like you someday Sir Marcus...I promise, then I won't be a burden in battle" he thought.
Then, without another word, the group began tending to their wounded, the night air still heavy with the aftermath of the battle.
The Watcher had judged.
And for now, the battle was won.

chapters.title: Arrival at the Academy.
chapters.summary: The group finally arrive at the Architects Martial Arts Academy, narrowly avoiding another confrontation with bounty hunters at its gates.
paragraphs: The journey to the Architects Martial Arts Academy continued with an air of anticipation. The weary travelers, now within sight of their destination, felt relief wash over them as the towering gates of the prestigious academy loomed ahead. The sheer scale of the institution was breathtaking—massive stone walls fortified with intricate runes of protection, statues of legendary warriors standing as silent sentinels, and the faint hum of magical energy resonating in the air.

However, just as they neared the entrance, a group of five figures emerged from the shadows, blocking their path. The atmosphere turned tense as an overwhelming aura of power oozed from the newcomers, pressing down on the caravan like an unseen force. The knights and guards accompanying the group instinctively stepped back, their hands gripping their weapons tightly.
One of the bounty hunters stepped forward, a smirk curling on his lips. "Well, well, look who we have here," he said, his voice thick with amusement.
"The former General of the Imperial Army, Marcus, and the current top generals of the Rover Kingdom’s Army, Lucy and Laura. Never thought I'd see you three traveling together."
Another bounty hunter chuckled. "It's really him in the flesh. I never expected to see the mighty Marcus without his armor. This is almost nostalgic."

The leader of the group silenced them with a wave of his hand, his piercing gaze landing on Edmond. "We're here for the kid. His family is paying handsomely for his safe return. We promise not to harm him—we’re just here to collect our reward. Hand him over, and we’ll be on our way."

Edmond tensed, his hands curling into fists. Why won’t they just let me be? Why can't they support me—for once? Instead, they sent bounty hunters after him. He swallowed hard, his mind a storm of conflicting thoughts.
“I can feel the power radiating off these guys,” he said quietly, his eyes flicking toward the bounty hunters. “They’re no joke.”

He took a breath. “Fighting them would be reckless. I’m grateful for everything you've done for me, truly. But… I think it’s best if I go with them. I want to avoid any needless bloodshed. My parents won’t stop until they drag me back to the estate—no matter the cost.”
He bowed his head slightly, a gesture of respect. “Thank you, Marcus.”
“Don’t be lame,” Marcus muttered. "You think I'll let you go? After all that trouble to get you here only to let you go with them now?. How lame of you"
"I.... I am truly sorry Sir Marcus" Edmond stuttered.
Marcus narrowed his eyes. "He’s already at the academy gates. After all we’ve been through to protect him, do you really think I’ll just hand him over now? That would be a waste, wouldn’t it?"

The bounty hunter's expression darkened. "If that’s the case, don’t blame us if you get hurt. You three might be strong, but your other companions are not. The odds are in our favor—five against three. Surrender the boy, and we’ll avoid unnecessary bloodshed."

Lucy’s sharp eyes flickered to the bounty hunters, assessing them. "Their power level is uncertain, but their presence is undeniable. These aren’t ordinary mercenaries. They’re the real deal." She could feel the sheer intensity of their auras, pressing down like an invisible weight.

Laura’s gaze shifted to the caravan. The children trembled, their faces pale with fear. Even the knights seemed frozen in place. "We can’t fight them. There would be too many casualties." She stole a glance at Marcus, who was deep in thought.

Marcus gritted his teeth. "He’s right. The guards and knights wouldn’t stand a chance. Lucy, Laura, and I might be able to hold our ground, but five against three isn’t a favorable match-up, especially with the kids here. If these bounty hunters have unlocked their ace techniques, we’d be in serious trouble."
Just as the tension reached its peak, a deep creaking sound echoed through the air—the gates of the academy were opening.

A flood of figures poured out—students clad in the academy’s martial robes, their disciplined steps forming an imposing formation. Behind them, five teachers emerged, their gazes sharp and calculating. At the forefront stood a man radiating an undeniable presence—Master Yami, his hands clasped behind his back, his piercing eyes surveying the scene.
Marcus smirked. "Well, I guess the odds just shifted in our favor."

The lead bounty hunter clicked his tongue in frustration. He shot one last glance at Edmond, then exhaled sharply. "You’re lucky, kid," he muttered before turning on his heel. The bounty hunters disappeared into the shadows as swiftly as they had appeared.

With the immediate threat dissipated, the academy’s students returned inside, and the instructors ushered the group in. Edmond, still shaken, stole a glance over his shoulder. His mind was finally calm and relieved, but he still couldn't understand why his parents didn't support his decision. Why were they so desperate to stop him from being a student of The Architects Martial Arts Academy? What dangers awaited him within the walls of the academy?

The new students were soon led through the academy grounds, their excitement gradually fading into unease. The grandeur of the buildings was undeniable—tall spires, intricate stone carvings, and runic engravings pulsing with latent magical energy. Yet, despite the architectural beauty, the place had an eerie emptiness to it. Dust coated several corridors, some halls bore signs of neglect, and the number of students seemed shockingly low for an academy of such repute.

After a brief tour, the group gathered their belongings and prepared to depart. Marcus, Lucy, and Laura, along with Miriam, Elias, Elric, Rosa, Theo, and the knights and guards that escorted Kara, Shirley and Whitney, all stood near the academy gates, casting one last look at their young charges.
"This is where we part ways," Marcus said, his voice firm yet warm. "You've all made your choice to train here. Make the most of it."
Lucy smiled reassuringly. "And remember, just because we’re leaving doesn’t mean you’re alone. You have each other now."
Monty clenched his fists. "We’ll make you all proud. Just wait and see."
With final farewells exchanged, the guardians turned and left, their figures fading into the distance as the academy gates slowly closed behind them.

Soon after the kid's guardians had left, an instructor came to address them "Welcome to the Architects Martial Arts Academy," the instructor announced, his voice a calm yet commanding presence. "You can call me master Shen." He said. "Here, you will learn to master the way of the fist, the mind, and the spirit as well as controlling your magical essence and utilizing it to its peak. But be warned—this place does not suffer the weak. Only those with the will to endure will remain". He stopped and glanced at the kids, their weariness evident in their expressions "You should rest up, and prepare for the path ahead of you" he said as he left the kids to themselves.

Amidst the chatter amongst them, two figures approached, these ones were not  instructors, yet they carried an air of authority. The first was a young girl, her unusual green hair was tied up in pigtails, her face had a brilliant smile that made the new students wonder if she really was training in the academy. "Hello! My name is Kitsune" she chimed, "I am in charge of the girls dormitory and your wellbeing, so please be polite and helpful to me and yourselves" she said, as she pointed to the girls one after the other.

The other figure was a young man, slightly older than Edmond and Brock. He was tall and lean, his silver emblem glinting under the torchlight. His sharp gaze swept over the newcomers before he spoke. "My name is Darius. I am the lead student responsible for orienting new initiates," he said, his voice composed but edged with something keen—like a blade honed to perfection. "You must be tired from your journey. I will lead you to your dormitories. Rest is important. Training begins at dawn."
The boys followed Darius as he led them through the academy grounds and the girls were led by Emily to their dormitory.

The halls were vast, the ceilings high, the torches flickering with an unnatural blue glow. The echoes of their footsteps stretched unnaturally, as if the walls whispered their presence to something unseen. Shadows flickered at the edges of their vision, but whenever they turned, there was nothing there.
"Why does this place feel so... empty?" Monty whispered under his breath.
Darius didn't turn around. "Many have come before you. Not all have remained."
A chill crawled up their spines, but no one dared to ask what he meant.
Upon reaching the dormitory quarters, Darius gestured toward a pair of aged wooden doors. "The boys' quarters are here," he said.
Rick hesitated before asking, "Are there any rules we should know about?"
Darius finally met his gaze. For the first time, there was a flicker of something else in his expression. Amusement? Warning? It was hard to tell.
"Yes," he said. "Do not wander the halls alone at night. And if you hear whispers... do not answer them."
With that ominous statement, he turned and strode away, his silhouette vanishing into the dimly lit corridors.
The students stood in stunned silence.
"Well," Brock muttered, forcing a shaky laugh, "that was reassuring."
"Yeah," Monty added, clutching his bag a little tighter. "Great start."

Without another word, they stepped inside their dorm, the weight of uncertainty pressing upon them. Though the space was covered in dust, the furniture rusted in places, it was surprisingly more comfortable than they had expected. After dropping off their baggage, they took a moment to sit together, reflecting on their journey so far.
Meanwhile, in the girls’ dormitory, a similar conversation unfolded. Lila, Whitney, Kara, and Shirley set their bags down, eyeing their surroundings with a mix of curiosity and doubt.
"Why does this place feel so eerily cold and quiet?" Shirley asked.
"This place is totally abandoned, save for the few students and masters that are left" Lila recounted.
"I just hope we made the right choices coming here, otherwise it'd be a waste of our life" Whitney pouted.

"Well, it really is kinda quiet and uneasy here but let's not judge a book by it's cover" Kara said "let's look forward to discovering what this academy has in store and why the place is like this" she implied.
"That's right!" The girls sneered in unison.
As the night deepened, both groups drifted into silence, each student lost in their thoughts, wondering what tomorrow would bring.

The next morning, the academy grounds were bathed in soft golden light as the students awoke. The boys were the first to leave their dorm, stretching and taking in their surroundings. The eerie silence of the academy still lingered, but today, it felt different—livelier.

Rick and Monty led the group as they wandered the main halls, peering into abandoned training rooms, dusty libraries, and vast courtyards. There was an unmistakable air of power in the place, even though it seemed neglected.

As they explored, a sudden commotion at the gates caught their attention. A second caravan arrived, and from it, nine more students stepped forward. Each bore a distinct presence, their expressions ranging from excitement to wariness.
"Looks like the rest of our classmates have finally arrived," Rick muttered, watching as the new arrivals were ushered in.
Shirley crossed her arms. "Maybe now, things will become livelier and more interesting."
With new faces joining them, the mystery of the academy deepened, leaving them all with more questions than answers.
